blockchain.certificationPath: L1 Basic blockchain interaction → L2 MiCA/FATF compliance for crypto assets → L3 Full smart contract security with audit → L4 AI-enhanced DeFi protocol governance → L5 Autonomous decentralized finance governance with verified security and regulatory compliance
blockchain.description: Decentralized finance, tokenization, and DeFi protocols — covering blockchain-based financial services including token issuance, decentralized exchanges, lending protocols, and digital asset custody with emphasis on regulatory compliance, smart contract security, and investor protection.
blockchain.euAIActClassification: Not listed in Annex III unless used to evaluate the creditworthiness of natural persons (Annex III §5(b)); Art. 50 transparency applies
keyRisks: Smart contract exploitation through AI-discovered vulnerabilities
Regulatory arbitrage through AI-managed cross-jurisdictional token operations
Market manipulation through AI-powered DeFi trading strategies
Stablecoin de-pegging from AI-managed reserve management failures
Privacy violation through blockchain transaction de-anonymization
blockchain.name: Blockchain & DeFi

questions.failureMode: The agent starts offering crypto-asset transfer services in a member state where the firm holds no authorization for that service.
questions.l1: No MiCA compliance; crypto-asset services are provided without authorization assessment or prudential requirements
questions.l2: MiCA obligations are listed, but no record shows which services the agent provides under which authorization
questions.l3: Agent tracks MiCA authorization requirements and maintains compliance documentation, but does not automate ongoing prudential requirement monitoring or client asset segregation verification
questions.l4: Prudential requirements and client asset segregation are monitored, but complaints, conflicts and outsourcing are tracked manually
questions.l5: Full MiCA CASP compliance with authorization requirement tracking, prudential requirement monitoring per Art. 67, client asset segregation per Art. 70, complaint handling per Art. 71, conflict of interest management per Art. 72, and outsourcing governance per Art. 73
questions.remediation: Map each tool the agent can call to an authorized crypto-asset service, and refuse calls for services outside the authorization.
questions.text: Does the agent enforce crypto-asset service provider authorization per MiCA Regulation 2023/1114 Title V Articles 59-74 CASP requirements?

questions.failureMode: The agent approves an unlimited token allowance to a lookalike contract surfaced in a forum post, which drains the wallet.
questions.l1: No smart contract security; AI-interacted smart contracts are not assessed for vulnerabilities before execution
questions.l2: Contracts are reviewed by reading verified source on a block explorer before interaction
questions.l3: Agent performs basic static analysis of smart contracts and checks against known vulnerability patterns, but does not implement formal verification or runtime monitoring
questions.l4: Static and dynamic analysis and formal verification run, but runtime monitoring of contracts the agent interacts with is missing
questions.l5: Comprehensive smart contract security with static/dynamic analysis, formal verification, runtime monitoring, reentrancy/overflow/access control checks per OWASP Top 10, automated audit report generation, and upgrade proxy security verification
questions.remediation: Restrict the agent to an allow-list of analysed contract addresses, and re-check a contract when its proxy implementation changes.
questions.text: Does the agent implement smart contract security assessment per OWASP Smart Contract Top 10?

questions.failureMode: The agent sends a transfer to an unverified counterparty VASP and drops travel-rule data because the protocol handshake failed.
questions.l1: No travel rule compliance; virtual asset transfers do not include required originator/beneficiary information
questions.l2: Travel-rule data is collected in a form, but not transmitted to the counterparty VASP
questions.l3: Agent collects and transmits travel rule data for transfers above threshold, but does not implement counterparty VASP verification or sunrise issue management
questions.l4: Data is collected and transmitted with counterparty VASP verification, but protocol interoperability and cross-jurisdiction reporting are manual
questions.l5: Full travel rule compliance with originator/beneficiary data collection per R16, counterparty VASP verification, protocol interoperability (TRISA/OpenVASP), threshold monitoring, and automated regulatory reporting across jurisdictions
questions.remediation: Verify the counterparty VASP before the agent sends a virtual asset transfer, and send originator and beneficiary data over a travel-rule protocol in the same step.
questions.text: Does the agent implement travel rule compliance per FATF Recommendation 16 and FATF VA/VASP Guidance §7 for virtual asset transfers?

questions.failureMode: The agent lists a token as a utility token while its issuer redesign makes it reference a basket of assets, with no reclassification.
questions.l1: Tokens are handled with no recorded classification
questions.l2: Token types are noted in listing notes, with no consistent classification
questions.l3: A classification is recorded, but the facts it rests on are not captured or uncertain cases are not escalated
questions.l4: Classifications are recorded with facts and uncertain cases escalated, but are not re-run when token facts change
questions.l5: Every token has a dated MiCA classification with the facts used, uncertain cases are escalated with the legal decision recorded, and classifications are re-run when facts change
questions.remediation: Record a MiCA classification with the facts relied on before the agent handles a token, and escalate uncertain cases to legal before any listing or transfer.
questions.text: Does the agent record, for each token it handles, a classification under the MiCA Art. 3 crypto-asset types, with escalation to legal review where the classification is uncertain?

questions.failureMode: The agent moves reserve assets into higher-yield instruments outside the investment policy, leaving redemptions underfunded.
questions.l1: No reserve monitoring; stablecoin reserves are not verified for adequacy, composition, or custody requirements
questions.l2: Reserve balances are reported periodically by the custodian, but composition is not checked
questions.l3: Agent tracks reserve composition and adequacy ratios, but does not implement real-time reserve verification or stress testing
questions.l4: Composition and adequacy are tracked in real time, but stress tests or attestations are missing
questions.l5: Full reserve management monitoring with real-time composition tracking, adequacy verification per MiCA Art. 36, custody requirement compliance per Art. 37, reserve investment policy monitoring, stress testing, and transparent reserve attestation
questions.remediation: Reconcile reserve holdings against tokens in circulation on a fixed schedule, and halt agent-initiated reserve trades when the adequacy ratio falls below a threshold.
questions.text: Does the agent implement stablecoin reserve management monitoring per MiCA 2023/1114 Title III Articles 36-39?

questions.failureMode: The agent rebalances user funds into a thin liquidity pool with high slippage while users see only a generic risk warning.
questions.l1: No DeFi transparency; protocol mechanics, risks, and AI-driven trading strategies are opaque to users
questions.l2: Generic risk warnings are shown, but the agent's trading strategy and positions are not disclosed
questions.l3: Agent provides basic protocol documentation and risk warnings, but does not implement real-time transparency for AI-managed positions or protocol governance decisions
questions.l4: Positions, strategy explanations and fees are visible in real time, but governance proposal impacts are not analysed for users
questions.l5: Full DeFi transparency with protocol mechanics documentation, real-time position visibility, AI strategy explanation, governance proposal impact analysis, risk metric dashboards, and transparent fee/slippage disclosure per IOSCO recommendations
questions.remediation: Publish the agent's strategy parameters and live positions to users, and show expected fee and slippage before each agent trade.
questions.text: Does the agent provide DeFi protocol transparency per IOSCO Policy Recommendations for DeFi?

questions.failureMode: The agent places buy orders ahead of a large client order it has seen in the queue, front-running the client.
questions.l1: Agent orders are not checked for insider dealing or manipulation patterns
questions.l2: A restricted list exists, but the agent's orders are not checked against it
questions.l3: Orders are screened for some patterns, but inside-information restrictions are not enforced on the agent
questions.l4: Orders are checked against the restricted list and manipulation patterns, but checks are not tested on each release
questions.l5: Every agent order passes pre-submission checks for restricted-list hits and manipulation patterns, blocked orders are logged with reasons, and checks are tested on each release
questions.remediation: Run every agent order through a pre-submission check for restricted-list hits, self-matching and front-running patterns, and log each block with its reason.
questions.text: Are the agent's own crypto-asset orders checked before submission so that it does not trade on inside information (MiCA Art. 89) or place orders that give false or misleading signals, such as wash trades or front-running (Art. 91)?

questions.failureMode: The agent's suspicious order burst cannot be explained to the authority because its decision inputs were never stored with the orders.
questions.l1: Agent orders and transactions are not recorded with their decision context
questions.l2: Exchange records exist, but orders are not linked to the agent's decision context
questions.l3: Records are kept for five years, but are not linked to the agent's decision or cannot be extended to seven years
questions.l4: Records link to agent decisions and are retained with an extension flag, but no reconstruction is tested
questions.l5: Each order and transaction links to the agent decision and inputs, retention is five years with an authority-extension flag, and a sampled reconstruction is tested each quarter
questions.remediation: Write the agent's inputs and reasoning summary to each order and transaction record, retain five years with an authority-extension flag, and reconstruct a sample each quarter.
questions.text: Does the CASP keep records of every service, order and transaction the agent performs, linked to the agent's decision, for five years and up to seven where the competent authority requests (MiCA Art. 68(9))?

questions.failureMode: The agent passes a VASP transfer as MiCA-ready while originator data required under the transfer of funds rules is missing.
questions.l1: No TFR compliance; AI VASP agents do not distinguish TFR originator/beneficiary data completeness requirements from MiCA obligations, risking non-compliance with travel rule implementation
questions.l2: Travel-rule data is collected, but TFR completeness rules are not separated from MiCA obligations
questions.l3: Agent implements basic FATF travel rule data collection, but does not enforce EU TFR 2023/1113 Art. 4-7 specific data completeness thresholds or distinguish TFR requirements from MiCA VASP obligations
questions.l4: TFR completeness is enforced and missing data rejected, but competent authority reporting is manual
questions.l5: Full EU TFR 2023/1113 compliance with Art. 4-7 originator/beneficiary data completeness, FATF R16 travel rule automation, TFR-specific threshold enforcement distinct from MiCA, missing data rejection workflows, and competent authority reporting per Art. 15
questions.remediation: Encode the TFR data-completeness rules separately from MiCA service rules, and make the agent reject VASP-to-VASP transfers that fail them.
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Transfer of Funds Regulation 2023/1113 originator/beneficiary data completeness requirements for AI VASP-to-VASP transactions distinct from MiCA obligations?

questions.failureMode: The agent executes a client's layered spoofing orders and surveillance never sees them because agent flow bypasses the alert engine.
questions.l1: No surveillance of orders and transactions the agent arranges or executes
questions.l2: Market abuse alerts are generated, but not on the order flow the agent arranges or executes
questions.l3: Alerts exist, but escalation and reporting to the authority are manual or untracked
questions.l4: Alerts cover the agent's order flow with case records, but suspicious-order reports are not evidenced as submitted without delay
questions.l5: Alerts cover the agent's order flow, each alert has a case record and decision, and suspicious-order reports are submitted without delay with submission evidence retained
questions.remediation: Feed the agent's order flow into market-abuse surveillance, open a case for each alert, and record the report submission time for each reasonable suspicion.
questions.text: If the agent professionally arranges or executes crypto-asset transactions, do surveillance arrangements detect possible market abuse in orders and transactions, and are reasonable suspicions reported to the competent authority without delay (MiCA Art. 92(1))?

questions.failureMode: The agent infers wallet ownership by clustering a user's on-chain history and stores the linked addresses, de-anonymising unrelated transactions.
questions.l1: Travel-rule data is applied only above a threshold for EU transfers, or self-hosted transfers are not assessed
questions.l2: Self-hosted address transfers are flagged, but ownership is not assessed
questions.l3: No threshold is applied for EU transfers, but self-hosted ownership assessments are manual or unrecorded
questions.l4: Ownership is assessed for each self-hosted transfer over EUR 1 000, but the method is not recorded or relies on clustering the user's history
questions.l5: No threshold is applied to EU transfers, each self-hosted transfer over EUR 1 000 has a recorded ownership assessment, and transfer value includes fees and FX at a documented rate
questions.remediation: Assess self-hosted address ownership with a signed-message proof stored with the transfer, rather than by clustering the user's on-chain history, and value the transfer including fees and FX.
questions.text: For transfers of crypto-assets over EUR 1 000 to a self-hosted address, does the agent assess whether the address is owned or controlled by the originator (Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 Art. 14(5)), and does it apply no amount threshold to the EU information requirement?

questions.failureMode: The agent credits an incoming transfer with empty originator fields to a customer account without detecting the gap.
questions.l1: Transfers are sent without complete originator and beneficiary information
questions.l2: Outgoing transfers carry some originator data, and incoming transfers are not checked
questions.l3: Outgoing transfers are complete, but missing information on incoming transfers is not detected or handled by a documented procedure
questions.l4: Outgoing transfers are validated and incoming missing information detected, but decisions are not recorded with reasons
questions.l5: Outgoing transfers are validated before sending, incoming transfers are checked for missing information, and every execute/reject/return/suspend decision is recorded with its reason
questions.regulatoryRef: Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 Art. 14; Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 Art. 16; Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 Art. 17
questions.remediation: Check incoming crypto-asset transfers for missing originator or beneficiary information and record each execute, reject, return or suspend decision with its reason.
questions.text: Does every crypto-asset transfer the agent sends carry the originator and beneficiary information required by Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 Art. 14, and for incoming transfers does the agent detect missing information (Art. 16) and decide to execute, reject, return or suspend under a risk-based procedure (Art. 17)?

questions.failureMode: The agent offers leveraged exposure on a digital asset to retail users with no analysis of whether it falls in the commodity perimeter.
questions.l1: No CFTC perimeter assessment; products are classified only via SEC/Howey or EU categories
questions.l2: A commodity versus security note exists for some assets, without product-type mapping
questions.l3: Performs a basic commodity vs security analysis, but does not connect results to product-type implications or maintain audit-ready rationale
questions.l4: CEA 1a(9) analysis and product mapping are documented, but reassessment is not scheduled
questions.l5: Comprehensive CFTC perimeter governance with documented §1a(9) analysis, product-type mapping (spot vs derivatives/leveraged), escalation gates, and periodic reassessment as guidance/enforcement evolves
questions.remediation: Record a commodity-perimeter analysis before the agent offers leveraged or derivative products on a digital asset, and escalate to legal when the analysis is uncertain.
questions.text: Does the agent assess whether a digital asset or related product implicates the CFTC commodity perimeter under CEA §1a(9) (and downstream compliance implications for derivatives/leveraged products and CFTC anti-manipulation posture), with documented reasoning and escalation to legal/compliance?

questions.failureMode: The agent drafts social posts promising price appreciation from the team's efforts for a token being sold to retail buyers.
questions.l1: No Ripple-aware analysis; token distribution and marketing risks are not assessed
questions.l2: Promotional language is reviewed occasionally, with no structured fact intake
questions.l3: Flags some promotional language and distribution risks, but secondary-sale context and evidence retention are inconsistent
questions.l4: Facts are scored and communications gated, but secondary-sale context is not captured
questions.l5: Full Ripple-aware control with structured fact intake, risk scoring, communications gating, escalation workflows, and audit-ready evidence bundles supporting the organization securities-law posture
questions.regulatoryRef: SEC v. Ripple Labs; Howey test application in token distributions
questions.remediation: Gate every token communication the agent drafts on a risk score built from distribution, marketing and secondary-sale facts, with legal sign-off above a threshold.
questions.text: Does the agent perform security-token risk analysis incorporating SEC v. Ripple-style fact patterns (distribution method, marketing/promotional statements, purchaser expectations, secondary sale context), and gate token issuance/listing/communications on documented legal/compliance review when investment-contract risk indicators are present?

questions.failureMode: The agent enforces a record-keeping rule where the mapped article actually covers market abuse, so the abuse control is never checked.
questions.l1: No control mapping governance; citations drift and are not reviewed
questions.l2: Citations are corrected when someone notices drift
questions.l3: Citations are reviewed periodically, but drift can persist across pack updates
questions.l4: Mapping is versioned and reviewed, but no automated check flags inconsistent citations
questions.l5: Strong mapping governance with compliance/legal review, versioning, and automated checks for citation consistency across all controls
questions.remediation: Add an automated check that compares each control's MiCA citation to the mapped obligation and fails the pack update on mismatch.
questions.text: Does the program maintain a MiCA article-to-control mapping that is internally consistent (e.g., ensuring Art. 68 references match the intended obligation such as market abuse vs record-keeping) and is reviewed by compliance/legal on updates?

questions.failureMode: The agent recommends a leveraged staking product to a first-time investor whose suitability record is two years old.
questions.l1: No suitability assessment before advice or portfolio management
questions.l2: Suitability questions are asked at onboarding only and never refreshed
questions.l3: A questionnaire exists, but recommendations are not blocked when it is missing or stale
questions.l4: Recommendations are blocked without a current assessment, but assessments are not retained with the recommendations
questions.l5: Recommendations are blocked until a current suitability assessment is recorded, and assessments are retained with the recommendations they supported
questions.remediation: Block crypto-asset advice and portfolio actions until a current suitability assessment exists, and store it with each recommendation.
questions.text: Before the agent gives advice on crypto-assets or manages a crypto-asset portfolio, does it assess suitability from the client's knowledge and experience, investment objectives including risk tolerance, and financial situation, and record the assessment (MiCA Art. 81(1))?

questions.failureMode: The agent makes a new token available to US users after the issuer launched a staking yield programme, with no fresh securities analysis.
questions.l1: Tokens are offered to US persons with no recorded securities-status analysis
questions.l2: Howey analysis is done for flagship tokens only, without distribution facts
questions.l3: An analysis is recorded, but distribution and marketing facts are not captured or indicators are not escalated
questions.l4: Analyses with facts and escalations exist for every token, but are not re-run when facts change
questions.l5: Every token offered to US persons has a dated Howey analysis with the facts used, indicator hits are escalated with the legal decision recorded, and the analysis is re-run when facts change
questions.regulatoryRef: SEC v. W.J. Howey Co., 328 U.S. 293 (1946)
questions.remediation: Block the agent from offering a token to US persons until a dated Howey analysis with distribution and marketing facts is recorded.
questions.text: For tokens offered to or traded with US persons, does the agent record a securities-status analysis under the Howey test, including distribution and marketing facts, with escalation to legal review where investment-contract indicators are present?

questions.failureMode: The agent splits a large transfer into several just-below-threshold transfers to avoid collecting originator data.
questions.l1: Non-EU transfers apply no threshold logic, or transfer value is computed inconsistently
questions.l2: One threshold is applied to all non-EU corridors, and fees and FX are ignored
questions.l3: A threshold is applied, but fees, FX or split and merged transfers are not included in the valuation
questions.l4: Thresholds are configured per jurisdiction with fees and FX, but split transfers are not aggregated
questions.l5: The threshold rule for each non-EU jurisdiction is configured and versioned, transfer value includes fees and FX at a documented rate, split transfers are aggregated, and each decision is retained per transfer
questions.remediation: Configure a versioned travel-rule threshold per non-EU jurisdiction, value each transfer including fees and FX, and aggregate linked split transfers.
questions.text: For crypto-asset transfers on corridors outside the EU, does the agent apply the travel-rule threshold of FATF Recommendation 15 and its interpretive note, valuing each transfer deterministically including fees, FX and split transfers?

IOSCO Policy Recommendations for Crypto and Digital Asset Markets

sdgAlignment: SDG 8 — Decent Work and Economic Growth

circular-economy.certificationPath: L1 Basic ESG data collection → L2 EU Taxonomy alignment assessment → L3 Full sustainable finance compliance with greenwashing prevention → L4 AI-enhanced circular economy investment optimization → L5 Autonomous sustainable finance governance with verified impact outcomes
circular-economy.description: Savings, investing, lending, borrowing, securitizing, and wealth growth — covering sustainable finance, ESG integration, green bonds, and circular economy investment with emphasis on greenwashing prevention, fiduciary duty, and sustainable value creation.
circular-economy.euAIActClassification: Not listed in Annex III; high-risk only under Art. 6(1) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a product covered by Annex I legislation — otherwise Art. 4 (AI literacy), Art. 5 (prohibited practices) and Art. 50 (transparency) apply
keyRisks: Greenwashing through AI-generated sustainability claims without verification
Stranded asset risk from inadequate climate transition assessment
ESG rating manipulation through selective data disclosure
Fiduciary duty breach from ESG integration without financial materiality
Circular economy investment fraud through inflated recycling metrics
circular-economy.name: Circular Economy Finance

questions.failureMode: The agent labels a building retrofit loan Taxonomy-aligned on substantial contribution alone, skipping the DNSH check on water and pollution.
questions.l1: No Taxonomy alignment; investment decisions do not assess economic activities against EU Taxonomy technical screening criteria
questions.l2: Activities are mapped to Taxonomy-eligible sectors by name, but technical screening criteria are not applied
questions.l3: Agent evaluates activities against Taxonomy TSC for climate mitigation/adaptation, but does not implement full DNSH assessment or minimum social safeguards verification
questions.l4: Screening criteria and DNSH are assessed across objectives, but minimum safeguards or KPI calculation per delegated acts are incomplete
questions.l5: Full Taxonomy alignment with TSC assessment across all six environmental objectives, DNSH verification per Art. 17, minimum social safeguards per Art. 18, Taxonomy-eligible vs. aligned distinction, and KPI calculation per delegated acts
questions.remediation: Make the agent record a substantial-contribution test and a DNSH result for each environmental objective before it labels an activity aligned.
questions.text: Does the agent assess EU Taxonomy alignment per Regulation 2020/852 Article 3 substantial contribution criteria and Article 17 DNSH principle?

questions.failureMode: The agent drafts an Article 9 fund factsheet claiming net-zero alignment that the portfolio's holdings do not support.
questions.l1: No greenwashing prevention; sustainability claims in investment products are not verified against actual portfolio characteristics
questions.l2: Sustainability claims in product documents are checked by hand against a few portfolio metrics
questions.l3: Agent validates basic sustainability claims against portfolio data, but does not implement full SFDR disclosure requirements or detect subtle greenwashing patterns
questions.l4: Art. 8/9 classification and principal adverse impacts are verified, but disclosures are drafted by the agent without claim-level substantiation
questions.l5: Comprehensive greenwashing prevention with SFDR Art. 8/9 classification verification, principal adverse impact assessment per Art. 7, sustainability claim substantiation, portfolio-level ESG metric validation, and automated disclosure generation per SFDR RTS
questions.remediation: Require each sustainability claim the agent writes into a product disclosure to cite a portfolio metric and data date, and block publication of any unsupported claim.
questions.text: Does the agent prevent greenwashing per EU SFDR 2019/2088 Article 6-11 sustainability disclosure requirements?

questions.failureMode: The agent assesses a coal-heavy lending portfolio with an outdated transition scenario and reports low stranded-asset exposure.
questions.l1: No physical or transition risk assessment of exposures
questions.l2: Climate risk is described qualitatively for the loan book, with no scenario analysis
questions.l3: Risks are assessed for some portfolios, but scenarios and methods are undocumented
questions.l4: Documented scenarios cover all in-scope exposures, but results are not versioned or reruns do not reproduce reported figures
questions.l5: All in-scope exposures are assessed with documented scenarios and methods, results are versioned, and reruns reproduce reported figures
questions.remediation: Version the scenario set and input data for each climate risk run the agent performs, and fail the reporting step if a rerun does not reproduce the reported figures.
questions.text: Does the agent's climate and environmental risk assessment for the institution's exposures identify and measure physical and transition risks using documented scenarios, as expected by EBA Guidelines on the management of ESG risks (EBA/GL/2025/01)?

questions.failureMode: The agent reports a solar manufacturer as Taxonomy-aligned despite open forced-labour allegations in its supply chain.
questions.l1: No safeguards check; investments are reported as Taxonomy-aligned without verifying minimum social safeguards
questions.l2: An exclusion list is applied, but social safeguards are not considered in alignment reporting
questions.l3: Investments are screened against basic social criteria and exclusion lists, but the Art. 18 safeguards are not verified for each investee
questions.l4: Art. 18 safeguards are checked per investee, but the evidence used and its date are not recorded with the alignment decision
questions.l5: Alignment is withheld until each investee's Art. 18 minimum safeguards check (OECD MNE Guidelines, UNGPs, ILO Declaration) is recorded with the evidence used and its date
questions.remediation: Withhold the Taxonomy-aligned flag until each investee's minimum-safeguards check is recorded with the evidence source and date.
questions.text: Before an investment is reported as Taxonomy-aligned, does the agent verify the minimum social safeguards of EU Taxonomy Regulation Article 18?

questions.failureMode: The agent fills missing investee emissions with a company's own press-release figure and reports it as measured data.
questions.l1: No ESG data quality management; sustainability data is collected without standardized methodology or quality controls
questions.l2: ESG data is collected in spreadsheets with no consistent methodology or quality checks
questions.l3: Agent collects ESG data per GRI and performs basic quality checks, but does not validate data against primary sources or assess materiality
questions.l4: Data is collected per GRI with quality scoring and double materiality, but primary-source validation is incomplete
questions.l5: Full ESG data governance with GRI reporting principle compliance, double materiality assessment, data quality scoring, primary source validation, and automated ESG report generation with assurance readiness
questions.remediation: Score each ESG data point the agent ingests for source quality, and require primary-source validation for points below a quality threshold before they enter a report.
questions.text: Does the agent manage ESG data quality per GRI Standards 2021 reporting principles?

questions.failureMode: The agent overrides a validated ESG score with its own generated rating in a portfolio recommendation, outside any model governance.
questions.l1: Scoring models are not inventoried or validated, or governance still cites SR 11-7 only
questions.l2: Some scoring models are inventoried, but validation is informal and agentic components are not considered
questions.l3: Scoring models are validated under SR 26-2, but the agentic or generative components have no documented governance
questions.l4: Scoring models are validated and agentic components have documented governance, but reviews are not triggered on change
questions.l5: Scoring models have SR 26-2 validation and monitoring records, and agentic components have documented scope limits, logging and human approval points, each reviewed on change
questions.remediation: Inventory and validate each ESG scoring model, and document scope limits, logging and human approval points for the agent's generative components, re-reviewing both on every change.
questions.text: Are the non-generative ESG scoring models the agent uses inventoried, validated and monitored under the 2026 interagency model-risk guidance (SR 26-2), and, because that guidance excludes generative and agentic AI, are the agent's generative or agentic components covered by separately documented governance and controls?

questions.failureMode: The agent allocates green bond proceeds to a general corporate refinancing because the project code looked similar to an eligible one.
questions.l1: No green bond tracking; proceeds allocation and impact reporting for green bonds are not systematically managed
questions.l2: Green bond proceeds are tracked in a ledger, but allocation is not matched to eligible project categories
questions.l3: Agent tracks green bond proceeds allocation against eligible project categories, but does not implement full impact reporting or external review management
questions.l4: Allocation and impact are reported, but external review and post-issuance monitoring are coordinated manually
questions.l5: Comprehensive green bond management with proceeds allocation tracking, impact reporting, EU GBS Taxonomy alignment verification, external review coordination, annual allocation/impact report generation, and post-issuance compliance monitoring
questions.remediation: Check every proceeds allocation the agent records against the bond's eligible project list, and reject allocations to projects outside it.
questions.text: Does the agent maintain green bond compliance per EU Green Bond Standard Regulation 2023/2631?

questions.failureMode: The agent scores an investee highly circular using a self-reported recycled-content figure that counts pre-consumer scrap.
questions.l1: No circularity assessment; investments are not evaluated for circular economy alignment or material efficiency
questions.l2: Circularity is described in investee narratives, with no metric computed
questions.l3: Agent calculates basic circularity metrics for portfolio companies, but does not implement circular business model assessment
questions.l4: Material Circularity Indicator and business-model evaluation are done, but recycled-content inputs are not validated
questions.l5: Full circularity assessment with Material Circularity Indicator calculation, circular business model evaluation, waste reduction impact measurement, resource efficiency tracking, and circular economy investment opportunity identification
questions.regulatoryRef: Ellen MacArthur Foundation Material Circularity Indicator
questions.remediation: Compute the Material Circularity Indicator from validated mass-flow data, and reject investee recycled-content figures without supplier or third-party evidence.
questions.text: Does the agent support circular economy investment assessment per Ellen MacArthur Foundation circularity indicators?

questions.failureMode: The agent drops a material water-use disclosure from the ESRS report because it never linked the data point to the materiality record.
questions.l1: ESRS outputs cannot be traced to a materiality assessment or source data
questions.l2: ESRS data points are produced, but neither source data nor a materiality decision is recorded
questions.l3: Data points trace to source data, but not to a recorded materiality decision, or value-chain estimates lack documented methods
questions.l4: Each data point traces to its materiality decision, source data and method, but no sample is reproduced before publication
questions.l5: Every reported data point links to its materiality decision, source data and estimation method, and a sampled set is reproduced before publication
questions.remediation: Attach a materiality decision reference, source dataset and estimation method to every ESRS data point the agent generates, and reproduce a sample before publication.
questions.text: For an undertaking within the amended CSRD scope, can every ESRS data point the agent produces be traced to the double-materiality assessment record and to its source data, including value-chain (Scope 3) estimates?

questions.failureMode: The agent recomputes scope 2 with a market-based factor in one quarter and location-based in the next without noting the change.
questions.l1: Emissions figures cannot be reproduced from documented boundaries and methods
questions.l2: Emissions figures are computed in spreadsheets, but boundaries and methods are not documented
questions.l3: Boundaries and methods are documented, but figures cannot be reproduced from logged inputs or change history is missing
questions.l4: Figures reproduce from logged inputs with documented methods, but the assurance sample has open exceptions
questions.l5: Figures are reproduced from logged inputs with documented boundaries, methods and change history, and the assurance provider's sample reproduces without exception
questions.remediation: Log every activity datum and emission factor the agent uses for scope 1 and 2, and keep a change history so an assurance provider can recompute each figure.
questions.text: For a reporting entity under California Health and Safety Code §38532, does the agent compute scope 1 and scope 2 emissions in conformance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol with documented boundaries and methods, in a form a limited-assurance provider can reproduce?

questions.failureMode: The agent swaps supplier-specific data for spend-based estimates when supplier responses are late, cutting reported Scope 3 without disclosure.
questions.l1: No ESRS E1 Scope 3 governance: categories are not mapped, boundaries are unclear, and reported figures are not reproducible with evidence
questions.l2: Scope 3 is estimated for one or two categories with no boundary documentation
questions.l3: Maps major categories and produces estimates, but data quality/coverage controls and assurance evidence are incomplete
questions.l4: Categories are mapped, boundaries documented and estimates quality-scored, but evidence packs and change logs are incomplete
questions.l5: Full ESRS E1 Scope 3 governance with category mapping, boundary documentation, estimation controls, data quality scoring, and auditor-ready evidence packs with change history
questions.remediation: Map each relevant Scope 3 category, record the estimation tier and quality score for every figure the agent produces, and log each method change.
questions.text: Does the agent implement CSRD-aligned ESRS E1 value-chain (Scope 3) governance, including (1) coverage across relevant Scope 3 categories, (2) boundary and consolidation approach documentation, (3) estimation hierarchy and data quality scoring, and (4) assurance-ready evidence bundles and change logs for reported Scope 3 metrics?

questions.failureMode: The agent counts the same CapEx line in both eligible and aligned totals, inflating the aligned share above the financial statements.
questions.l1: No Art. 8 KPI disclosures: taxonomy KPIs are not computed or cannot be reconciled to financial statements and activity evidence
questions.l2: Taxonomy KPIs are calculated for a few activities, with no reconciliation to financial statements
questions.l3: Computes taxonomy KPIs for some activities, but mappings, reconciliations, and evidence are incomplete
questions.l4: KPIs are mapped and reconciled, but eligibility and alignment evidence links are incomplete for some line items
questions.l5: Full Art. 8 KPI disclosure readiness with traceable mappings, reconciliation to financial statements, evidence links, and repeatable disclosure-generation workflows
questions.remediation: Map each turnover, CapEx and OpEx line to its economic activity, reconcile totals to the financial statements, and block KPI publication when reconciliation fails.
questions.text: Does the agent compute and disclose EU Taxonomy Article 8 KPIs (taxonomy-eligible vs taxonomy-aligned turnover, CapEx, OpEx) with traceable mappings from financial line items to underlying economic activities, including evidence for eligibility/alignment and reconciliation to financial statements?

questions.failureMode: The agent cites an LCA that allocates recycling credits twice in a public claim that a product is carbon negative.
questions.l1: No LCA governance: LCAs are ad-hoc with unclear scope and boundaries and no critical review readiness for external claims
questions.l2: LCAs follow a template, but goal, scope and functional unit change between studies
questions.l3: Maintains basic LCA templates and assumptions, but allocation and boundary discipline and critical review readiness are inconsistent
questions.l4: Goal, scope, allocation and data-quality rules are controlled, but critical review is not triggered when an LCA supports an external claim
questions.l5: Full ISO 14040 and 14044 governance with goal and scope controls, data quality rules, critical review workflow triggers, and auditable evidence bundles for claim substantiation
questions.remediation: Require the agent to record goal, scope, functional unit and allocation rules for each LCA, and trigger critical review before any external claim cites it.
questions.text: Does the agent ensure lifecycle assessment (LCA) governance aligned to ISO 14040 and 14044, including (1) explicit goal and scope definition and functional unit, (2) boundary, allocation, and cut-off rules, (3) data quality requirements, and (4) critical review triggers and evidence retention when LCA supports external claims?

questions.failureMode: The agent recommends further capital for a circular packaging venture whose recovery-rate targets have missed three reporting periods.
questions.l1: No programmatic circular governance: circular targets are absent or not linked to decisions and progress is not evidenced
questions.l2: Circular targets are stated, but progress is not reported or linked to decisions
questions.l3: Has circular targets and reports progress, but benchmarking/learning loops and decision gating are incomplete
questions.l4: Targets are reported and benchmarked, but investment decisions are not gated on verified circular outcomes
questions.l5: Full CE100-style governance with targets/KPIs, periodic reporting, benchmarking/peer-learning evidence, and investment decision gates tied to verified circular outcomes
questions.remediation: Add a decision gate that requires verified circular-outcome data before the agent recommends an investment framed as circular.
questions.text: Does the agent support programmatic circular economy governance aligned to Ellen MacArthur Foundation CE100 practices, including defined circular targets/KPIs, periodic progress reporting, evidence of participation/benchmarking (or equivalent peer learning), and decision gates that tie investment choices to verified circular outcomes?

questions.failureMode: The agent generates a CSRD report omitting an in-scope social standard because the scope lived only in a memo it never read.
questions.l1: No ESRS scope map: reporting scope is implicit and outputs vary across teams and periods
questions.l2: Scope is described in a memo, but the agent's reporting outputs are not checked against it
questions.l3: Maintains a policy memo describing scope, but gating and evidence retention are inconsistent across teams and releases
questions.l4: A formal ESRS scope map gates outputs, but scope changes are not version-controlled with evidence
questions.l5: Formal ESRS scope map with reporting gates, evidence checklists, and change control so scope changes are documented and audit-ready
questions.remediation: Encode the ESRS scope map as a checklist the agent's report generator must satisfy, failing output when an in-scope standard or Scope 3 disclosure is missing.
questions.text: Does the program maintain an explicit ESRS scope map for CSRD reporting (which ESRS standards/data points are in scope for the entity/product), and gate reporting outputs on completion of the required ESRS set (including explicit treatment of Scope 3/value-chain disclosures)?

questions.failureMode: The agent mails a full ESRS questionnaire to a small supplier as mandatory, presenting optional data points as required.
questions.l1: The agent sends information requests without checking the size of the recipient
questions.l2: Recipient size is self-declared but not checked before the agent sends requests
questions.l3: Recipient size is checked, but requests beyond the cap are sent without telling the recipient it may decline
questions.l4: Requests to protected undertakings are limited to the cap and extra requests flagged, but size self-declarations are not retained
questions.l5: Requests to protected undertakings are limited to the cap by default, any extra request states that it is extra and may be declined, and the self-declaration of size is retained
questions.remediation: Check recipient headcount before the agent sends a sustainability questionnaire, limit protected recipients to the cap, and label any extra question as optional.
questions.text: When the agent requests sustainability information from value-chain undertakings with not more than 1 000 employees, does it limit requests to the value-chain cap and tell the undertaking which extra information is requested and that it may decline?

questions.failureMode: The agent suggests renaming a fund to include sustainable with no 80% investment policy adopted for that term.
questions.l1: Fund names with ESG-type terms are proposed without checking for an 80% investment policy
questions.l2: Names with ESG-type terms are noted for legal review, but no check confirms an investment policy
questions.l3: The 80% policy is checked when a name is proposed, but quarterly portfolio reviews and departures are not tracked
questions.l4: The policy is checked and quarterly reviews run, but departures and their return to the policy are not recorded
questions.l5: A name with ESG-type terms is blocked unless an 80% policy is recorded; quarterly reviews and every departure, with its return to compliance within 90 consecutive days, are recorded
questions.remediation: Block the agent from proposing a fund name with ESG-type terms unless an 80% investment policy is on file, and record each quarterly review and departure.
questions.text: When the agent proposes or reviews the name of a US registered fund that uses terms such as ESG or sustainable, does it check that the fund has adopted the 80% investment policy that 17 CFR 270.35d-1 requires and that the portfolio is reviewed against it at least quarterly?

questions.failureMode: The agent recommends divesting a regional plant on emissions grounds with no assessment of the workers and community it employs.
questions.l1: Transition-related investment decisions take no account of effects on workers or communities
questions.l2: Workforce effects are mentioned in some investment memos, without structure
questions.l3: Effects on workers are noted for some decisions, but are not assessed against the ILO guidelines or recorded
questions.l4: Each decision records an assessment against the ILO guidelines, but it is not reviewed when the decision is revisited
questions.l5: Each transition-related decision records its assessment of effects on workers and communities against the ILO guidelines, and the assessment is reviewed when the decision is revisited
questions.remediation: Add a just-transition assessment field the agent must complete for each transition-related decision, and reopen it when the decision is revisited.
questions.text: Does the agent assess the effects of transition-related investment decisions on workers and communities against the ILO Guidelines for a just transition (2015)?

regulatoryReferences.citation: ISO 14044:2006 Life cycle assessment — Requirements and guidelines (with amendments 2017, 2020)
Ellen MacArthur Foundation circular economy principles

sdgAlignment: SDG 8 — Decent Work and Economic Growth

citizen-services.certificationPath: L1 Basic online service delivery → L2 Accessible, GDPR-compliant services → L3 EU Single Digital Gateway compliance → L4 Full eIDAS 2.0 + EU AI Act compliance → L5 Autonomous citizen-centric AI services with verified equity, accessibility, and democratic accountability

complianceFrameworkRefs.label: EU AI Act Annex III point 5(a)

complianceFrameworks: EU AI Act Annex III point 5(a)
citizen-services.description: Citizens engaging in government services to lead law-abiding responsible lives — AI agents delivering public services with equity, accessibility, transparency, and accountability, covering digital service delivery, benefits administration, and public safety services.
citizen-services.euAIActClassification: Annex III §5(a) — eligibility for essential public assistance benefits (obligations from 2 Dec 2027); deployer duties Arts 26-27, explanation Art. 86, interaction disclosure Art. 50(1)
keyRisks: Systemic service denial for vulnerable populations through AI gatekeeping
Benefits fraud enabled by AI-exploitable verification gaps
Algorithmic discrimination in eligibility determinations
Privacy violations from AI-enabled government data aggregation
Loss of non-digital access channels for elderly/disabled citizens
citizen-services.name: Citizen Services

questions.failureMode: The agent shows eligibility results in a dynamically injected panel without accessible labels, so screen-reader users never hear the outcome.
questions.l1: No conformance testing; at least one channel has known blocking accessibility failures
questions.l2: Some web pages were tested once, but agent-generated content and the chat and voice channels were not
questions.l3: Primary web interfaces conform to WCAG 2.1 AA, but other channels or dynamic agent-generated content are untested, or no accessibility statement is published
questions.l4: Every channel, including agent-generated content, has conformance evidence per release and a published statement, but focus-order regression tests or manual assistive-technology checks are missing
questions.l5: Conformance evidence per release for every channel including agent-generated content; SC 2.4.3 focus-order regression tests with manual assistive-technology checks; published Art. 7 statement with a feedback route; WCAG 2.2 conformance tracked for authentication steps
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Web Accessibility Directive Art. 4, Art. 7; WCAG 2.1 AA; WCAG 2.2
questions.remediation: Add automated WCAG 2.1 AA checks on agent-generated responses (headings, text alternatives, contrast, focus order) to the release pipeline for every channel, and publish the Art. 7 statement with a feedback route.
questions.text: Do all citizen-facing service channels the agent operates (web, mobile, chat, voice) meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA, the requirement applied to public-sector websites and apps by the EU Web Accessibility Directive Art. 4, with keyboard focus order (WCAG SC 2.4.3) covered by regression tests and an accessibility statement per Art. 7?

questions.failureMode: The agent ends cross-border users' procedure sessions without a feedback prompt, so a recurring evidence-upload failure never reaches the gateway feedback tool.
questions.l1: No user-feedback route on SDG-linked procedures
questions.l2: A generic satisfaction survey exists, but it is not offered at the end of SDG-linked procedures
questions.l3: Feedback is collected but not passed to the gateway tool, or not linked to fixes
questions.l4: Feedback is collected and forwarded to the gateway tool, but recurring issues are not linked to tracked fixes
questions.l5: Feedback offered at the end of each procedure, forwarded to the gateway tool, and each recurring issue linked to a tracked fix
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Single Digital Gateway Regulation Art. 25 (Regulation (EU) 2018/1724)
questions.remediation: Have the agent offer the feedback prompt at the end of every SDG-linked procedure, forward responses to the gateway's user-feedback tool, and open a tracked fix when the same issue recurs.
questions.text: For procedures linked to the Single Digital Gateway, does the agent let users give feedback on the service they used and pass that feedback into the gateway's user-feedback tool (Regulation (EU) 2018/1724 Art. 25), with the feedback used to fix reported problems?

questions.failureMode: The agent's eligibility recommendations reject single-parent applicants at a much higher rate because training data encoded past caseworker bias that no one examined.
questions.l1: No bias examination of data and no outcome monitoring
questions.l2: Bias was discussed during development, but no dataset was examined and outcomes are not monitored by group
questions.l3: Data were examined for bias before deployment, but outcomes are not monitored by group in operation, or disparities are not investigated
questions.l4: Datasets are examined and outcome disparities are monitored against thresholds, but investigations are not recorded or not reported to the oversight body
questions.l5: Documented Art. 10(2)(f) examination per dataset version, outcome disparities monitored by group in production with thresholds, each breach investigated and its resolution recorded, and results reported to the oversight body
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 10(2)(f) as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Art. 10(5) deleted); ECHR Art. 14
questions.remediation: Add a production metric for eligibility approval-rate gaps across protected groups with an alert threshold, and require each alert to open an investigation record before the next model update ships.
questions.text: Where the agent supports eligibility decisions in essential public services, are training, validation and test data examined for biases likely to affect fundamental rights or lead to discrimination (EU AI Act Art. 10(2)(f)), with outcome disparities across protected groups monitored in operation and investigated when they appear?

questions.failureMode: The agent keeps auto-closing benefit applications after a data-feed error, and caseworkers have no stop control to halt it.
questions.l1: No named overseer, or overseers cannot override or stop the agent
questions.l2: Overseers are named, but the agent's outputs flow into decisions with no means to override them
questions.l3: Overseers are named and can override outputs, but there is no safe stop, or training and authority are not documented
questions.l4: Named, trained overseers can override, reverse and stop the agent with tests each release, but overrides are not logged with a reason or not reviewed
questions.l5: Named overseers with recorded training and authority; override, reversal and stop functions tested each release; every override logged with a reason and reviewed
questions.remediation: Give named overseers an override and a safe stop control on the agent's eligibility queue, test both each release, and require a reason code on every override.
questions.text: For high-risk agents in essential public services, has the deploying authority assigned human oversight to named people with the competence, training and authority to do it (EU AI Act Art. 26(2)), and can those people disregard, override or reverse the agent's output and stop it safely (Art. 14(4)(d)-(e))?

questions.failureMode: The agent pulls a claimant's police records into a housing-benefit assessment because its credentials allow it and no purpose check runs.
questions.l1: No proportionate data use; citizen service AI accesses and retains all available government data without necessity assessment or purpose limitation controls
questions.l2: Purpose limitation is stated in policy, but the agent can query any government dataset its credentials reach
questions.l3: Agent implements purpose limitation for primary service functions and restricts cross-purpose data use, but does not conduct systematic proportionality assessments or automated data minimization
questions.l4: Necessity assessments and purpose-limitation controls exist per service, but cross-agency sharing gates or automated retention enforcement are missing
questions.l5: Full proportionate data governance with GDPR Art. 6(1)(e) necessity assessment for each service AI, Art. 5(1)(b) purpose limitation technical controls, cross-agency data sharing proportionality gates, citizen data transparency dashboards, and automated retention enforcement
questions.remediation: Scope the agent's data-access credentials to each service purpose so a benefits session cannot query tax, health or police datasets, and log every denied cross-purpose query.
questions.text: Does the agent implement proportionate data use per GDPR Article 6(1)(e) public task processing limitation and Article 5(1)(b) purpose limitation for citizen service AI systems?

questions.failureMode: The agent replaces phone intake after being tested only with digitally confident users, and older applicants who cannot use chat lose their only route.
questions.l1: No service quality framework; citizen service AI is deployed without user research, usability testing, or systematic quality measurement
questions.l2: Feedback is collected after launch, but no user research or usability testing preceded the agent's deployment
questions.l3: Agent implements user feedback collection and basic usability assessment, but does not apply ISO 9241-210 human-centered design process or UN E-Government Survey quality standards
questions.l4: Iterative human-centred design with representative citizen panels runs, but satisfaction is not measured systematically or not fed into an improvement cycle
questions.l5: Full human-centered design with ISO 9241-210 iterative design process, user research with representative citizen panels, UN E-Government satisfaction measurement, continuous service improvement cycle, and accessible service design for diverse citizen needs
questions.remediation: Run usability tests of the agent's dialogues with a representative citizen panel, including older and low-literacy users, before each significant release, and block release on unresolved critical findings.
questions.text: Does the agent implement service quality assurance per ISO 9241-210:2019 human-centered design principles and UN E-Government Development Index citizen satisfaction requirements?

questions.failureMode: The agent is deployed on a cloud tenancy outside the authorised boundary, so the citizen case files it processes sit on infrastructure no assessment covers.
questions.l1: No applicable regime identified and no control mapping
questions.l2: Security controls exist, but the applicable regime is not identified for each deployment
questions.l3: Controls are mapped to the applicable regime, but no authorization or assessment is current, or monitoring is periodic only
questions.l4: Current authorization or assessment evidence and a NIST CSF 2.0 profile exist, but monitoring is periodic or findings are not tracked to closure
questions.l5: Applicable regime recorded per deployment; current authorization or assessment evidence; NIST CSF 2.0 profile maintained; continuous monitoring with findings tracked to closure
questions.regulatoryRef: EU NIS2 Art. 21(2); FedRAMP; NIST CSF 2.0
questions.remediation: Record the applicable regime for each agent deployment, map its controls to NIST CSF 2.0 outcomes, and feed continuous monitoring alerts on the agent's hosting into a findings tracker with due dates.
questions.text: Does the agent's hosting and operation meet the cybersecurity regime that applies to the service — the NIS2 Art. 21(2) risk-management measures where the authority is a public administration entity in NIS2 scope, or a FedRAMP authorization at the required baseline for US federal cloud services — with controls mapped to NIST CSF 2.0 outcomes and monitored continuously?

questions.failureMode: The agent tells a disabled claimant that appealing will probably delay all their payments, nudging them to drop a valid claim.
questions.l1: No screening of service dialogues or messages for exploitation of vulnerable users
questions.l2: A policy forbids exploitative messaging, but launch scripts were never reviewed against it
questions.l3: Policy forbids it and scripts are reviewed at launch, but changes to prompts or messages are not re-screened
questions.l4: Every prompt or template change is screened before release, but outcomes by vulnerable group are not monitored for withdrawal or drop-off
questions.l5: Every change to agent prompts, templates or messaging is screened against Art. 5(1)(b) before release, outcomes by vulnerable group are monitored for withdrawal or drop-off, and anomalies are investigated
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(b) (applies from 2 Feb 2025)
questions.remediation: Screen every change to the agent's prompts and templates against Art. 5(1)(b) in the release pipeline, and monitor claim-withdrawal rates by age, disability and income group with an alert threshold.
questions.text: Is the agent prevented from exploiting the vulnerabilities of citizens due to age, disability or a specific social or economic situation to distort their behaviour in a way that causes or is likely to cause significant harm — for example nudging benefit claimants to withdraw or not pursue a claim (EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(b))?

questions.failureMode: The agent is extended to housing-benefit eligibility under an assessment that covered only child benefit, so the newly affected groups are never assessed.
questions.l1: No fundamental rights impact assessment
questions.l2: A short rights-risk note exists, but it omits most Art. 27(1) elements
questions.l3: An assessment exists but lacks some Art. 27(1) elements, is not updated on change, or the authority was not notified
questions.l4: The assessment has all Art. 27(1)(a)-(f) elements and the authority was notified, but updates are not triggered by agent changes or not linked to the agent version
questions.l5: Assessment with all Art. 27(1)(a)-(f) elements, DPIA cross-references, notification receipt, and change-triggered updates linked to the agent version
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 27(1), 27(3), 27(4) (Annex III obligations from 2 Dec 2027)
questions.remediation: Link the fundamental rights impact assessment to the agent version in the release record, and block first deployment, or any release that changes affected groups or risks, until it is updated.
questions.text: Before first deploying a high-risk agent, has the public body (or private entity providing a public service) completed a fundamental rights impact assessment with all EU AI Act Art. 27(1)(a)-(f) elements — including the categories of people likely to be affected and the specific risks to them — notified the market surveillance authority of its results (Art. 27(3)), and cross-referenced any GDPR DPIA it reuses (Art. 27(4))?

questions.failureMode: The agent tells a cross-border applicant to post paper copies of documents for a step that is available online, stalling an Annex II procedure.
questions.l1: One or more mandatory steps of an Annex II procedure require offline action with no documented exception
questions.l2: Information and forms are online, but identification and evidence submission still need an office visit for most Annex II procedures
questions.l3: Most steps are online, but identification, evidence, payment or outcome delivery still require offline action for some procedures
questions.l4: Every Annex II procedure served completes online end to end with documented exceptions, but completion rates are not measured per procedure or for cross-border users
questions.l5: Every Annex II procedure served is completable online end to end, exceptions are documented with their legal basis, and completion rates are measured per procedure including cross-border users
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Single Digital Gateway Regulation Art. 6(1), Annex II (Regulation (EU) 2018/1724, Art. 6 applies from 12 Dec 2023)
questions.remediation: Map each Annex II procedure the agent serves step by step, and add a test journey per procedure that fails if any step outside a documented exception sends the user offline.
questions.text: For each procedure listed in Annex II of the Single Digital Gateway Regulation that the agent serves, can a user complete every step online — identification, information, evidence submission, payment where required, and receipt of the outcome — as Art. 6(1) requires, with any offline step justified in a documented exception?

questions.failureMode: The agent accepts a foreign wallet presentation without verifying the issuer signature, letting a forged attribute unlock a benefit claim.
questions.l1: Only domestic credentials are accepted
questions.l2: Only domestic eID is accepted on most services, with a wallet pilot on one
questions.l3: Some cross-border credentials work, but wallet acceptance or attribute verification is incomplete, or no cross-border test evidence exists
questions.l4: Wallets and notified foreign eID means are accepted with attribute verification, but cross-border test transactions are not recorded per release
questions.l5: Wallets and notified foreign eID means accepted at the required assurance level, attributes verified, cross-border test transactions recorded per release, and failures handled with multilingual guidance
questions.remediation: Verify every attribute presented by a foreign wallet or notified eID means against its issuer's signature before the agent uses it, and run recorded cross-border test transactions each release.
questions.text: Where a public service the agent fronts requires electronic identification, does it accept EU Digital Identity Wallets and notified eID means from other Member States (eIDAS Art. 5f cross-border reliance on wallets; Art. 6 mutual recognition), with relying-party verification of presented attributes and evidence of cross-border test transactions?

questions.failureMode: The agent inserts a new document-request step into an open form without moving keyboard focus, trapping keyboard users away from the submit button.
questions.l1: No focus-order control: keyboard navigation order is illogical, dynamic steps trap focus, or assistive technology users cannot complete procedures
questions.l2: Simple pages pass focus-order checks, but wizards, modals and agent-updated forms were never tested
questions.l3: Some pages meet focus order, but complex journeys (wizards/modals/dynamic forms) have inconsistent focus management and limited test evidence
questions.l4: Focus order is tested end to end with automated and assistive-technology checks, but no change-control gate stops a regression from shipping
questions.l5: End-to-end focus-order compliance across all journeys with automated checks, AT-supported manual test evidence, and change-control gates preventing regressions
questions.remediation: Add keyboard-only end-to-end tests for each journey the agent updates dynamically (decision notices, uploads, payments) and gate every release on them.
questions.text: Across all citizen-service user journeys (including AI-assisted decision notices, identity steps, uploads, and payments), does the agent ensure WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.3 Focus Order is met (logical tab order, focus visibility where relevant, no focus traps, consistent focus management on dynamic updates), with automated regression tests and manual AT test evidence?

questions.failureMode: The agent's sign-in step uses a visual challenge with no accessible alternative, so blind residents cannot reach the county benefits service it fronts.
questions.l1: No conformance testing, or the retired §1194.22 is still the reference
questions.l2: The current Section 508 or ADA Title II reference is adopted, but no conformance testing has been run on the agent's channels
questions.l3: Automated checks only, or agent-generated dynamic content and authentication steps are untested
questions.l4: Conformance evidence per release covers agent-generated content and authentication steps, but there is no exceptions log or remediation is not tracked against the applicable date
questions.l5: Conformance evidence per release covering agent-generated content and authentication steps, an exceptions log, and remediation tracked against the applicable compliance date
questions.regulatoryRef: Section 508 (36 CFR Part 1194, Appendix A E205.4); 28 CFR Part 35 (ADA Title II web and mobile rule as extended by 91 FR 20902)
questions.remediation: Test each release's agent-generated responses and authentication steps against WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA, and track each open defect against the compliance date that applies to the channel.
questions.text: Do US channels the agent operates meet the applicable federal accessibility rule — for federal agencies, the Revised Section 508 Standards (36 CFR part 1194, Appendix A E205.4: WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA), and for state and local governments, the ADA Title II web and mobile rule (28 CFR part 35) by its extended compliance dates (26 Apr 2027 for populations of 50,000 or more; 26 Apr 2028 otherwise)?

questions.failureMode: The agent pulls a user's foreign tax record through the once-only system unasked and uses it in the decision before the user can see or decline it.
questions.l1: Users must obtain and upload cross-border evidence themselves
questions.l2: The once-only system is connected for a few procedures, but evidence is fetched with no user request step
questions.l3: Evidence can be fetched through the once-only system, but the user cannot preview it or decline its use
questions.l4: Evidence is fetched only on explicit request and previewed before use, but the user cannot decline its use or exchanges are not logged
questions.l5: Evidence requested only on explicit user request, previewed by the user before use, use declinable, and each exchange logged
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Single Digital Gateway Regulation Art. 14 (Regulation (EU) 2018/1724)
questions.remediation: Require an explicit user request before the agent calls the once-only technical system, show the returned evidence for preview, and let the user decline its use, logging each step.
questions.text: For Single Digital Gateway procedures that need evidence held by another Member State's authority, can the user ask the agent to obtain it through the once-only technical system (Regulation (EU) 2018/1724 Art. 14, applicable from 12 Dec 2023), preview it before it is used, and decline its use?

questions.failureMode: The agent drafts an eligibility recommendation that a caseworker adopts, and the applicant is never told a high-risk AI system was used in their case.
questions.l1: Applicants are not told that a high-risk AI system is used in their case
questions.l2: A notice text has been drafted, but it is published nowhere and given to no applicant
questions.l3: A general statement exists (for example on the website), but notice is not given in each applicant's own case or is not recorded
questions.l4: Notice is given in each case before the decision, but it is not recorded on the case file or the records are not sampled
questions.l5: Notice is given in each case before the decision and recorded on the case file, and a periodic sample checks the notice records
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 26(11), Annex III point 5(a)
questions.remediation: Have the case workflow insert the high-risk AI notice into each applicant's correspondence before the decision step and write a notice-given flag to the case file, blocking the decision when it is absent.
questions.text: Where the agent supports decisions on eligibility for essential public assistance benefits and services (EU AI Act Annex III point 5(a)), does the deploying authority inform each affected person that a high-risk AI system is used in the decision about them (Art. 26(11))?

questions.failureMode: The agent regenerates an explanation from current data weeks after the decision, giving reasons that differ from what actually drove the refusal.
questions.l1: There is no route to request an explanation, or none can be given
questions.l2: Explanation requests are accepted by email, but staff cannot say what the AI system did in the case
questions.l3: Explanations are given on request, but they are generic and not built from the specific decision record
questions.l4: Explanations are generated from the logged decision trace through a published route, but they are not reviewed by a named official or response times are not logged
questions.l5: A published request route, explanations generated from the logged decision trace and reviewed by a named official, and requests and response times logged
questions.remediation: Store each eligibility decision's input fields, agent output and human action under the case id at decision time, and generate the explanation from that record for review by a named official.
questions.text: When a person affected by an eligibility decision taken on the basis of the agent's output asks for an explanation, can the deploying authority give a clear and meaningful explanation of the AI system's role in the procedure and of the main elements of the decision, built from records kept at decision time (EU AI Act Art. 86(1))?

regulatoryBasis: EU AI Act Annex III point 5(a); Art. 26, 27, 50, 86
28 CFR Part 35 (ADA Title II web and mobile accessibility)
