clinical-lifecycle.certificationPath: L1 Basic clinical workflow support → L2 Evidence-based protocol compliance → L3 Full QMS per ISO 13485 with clinical governance → L4 AI-assisted clinical decision-making with FDA/MDR compliance → L5 Autonomous clinical lifecycle governance with verified patient outcomes
clinical-lifecycle.description: Therapeutic, surgical, psychoanalysis, and alternative medicine — covering clinical practice modalities with emphasis on evidence-based practice, patient safety, clinical governance, and treatment efficacy monitoring.
clinical-lifecycle.euAIActClassification: Art. 6(1) and Annex I (Regulation (EU) 2017/745 MDR, 2017/746 IVDR) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a medical device; Annex III §5(d) for emergency healthcare patient triage
keyRisks: Surgical planning errors from AI-generated anatomical analysis
Therapeutic protocol deviation undetected by automated monitoring
Alternative medicine interactions with conventional treatments missed by AI
Clinical governance failure from over-reliance on AI recommendations
Patient harm from AI-managed treatment titration without adequate safety margins
clinical-lifecycle.name: Clinical Lifecycle

questions.failureMode: The agent runs on a system prompt or tool configuration edited in production without design review, so its clinical outputs no longer match the validated design.
questions.l1: No design controls; clinical AI systems are developed without systematic design input/output verification or validation
questions.l2: Design inputs and outputs are recorded for the core model, but there are no design reviews and prompts and tools have no design file entries
questions.l3: Design and development files exist per ISO 13485 clause 7.3, but design reviews or validation records are incomplete for agent components (prompts, tools, orchestration)
questions.l4: Every AI component including prompts and tool configurations has design entries, reviews and validation, but records are not yet controlled per 21 CFR 820.35
questions.l5: Design inputs, outputs, reviews, verification, validation, transfer and changes are recorded for every AI component including prompts and tool configurations; records are controlled per §820.35
questions.remediation: Put system prompts, tool definitions and orchestration config under design control: each change gets a design input, review sign-off and validation run.
questions.text: Does the agent implement design and development controls for clinical AI per ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.3 as incorporated by 21 CFR §820.10 (QMSR, effective 2 February 2026), including design and development file evidence?

questions.failureMode: The agent recommends a therapeutic protocol from a superseded guideline version retrieved from a stale index, and the deviation from current practice goes unnoticed.
questions.l1: Recommendations do not identify the guideline or version used
questions.l2: Some recommendations name a guideline in free text, without version or date
questions.l3: Guideline and version are recorded for some recommendation types; superseded versions are not detected
questions.l4: Every recommendation records guideline and version and superseded versions are flagged, but flagged items are not routed to a clinician
questions.l5: Every recommendation records guideline and version; a currency check flags superseded versions on each knowledge update; flagged recommendations are reviewed by a clinician
questions.regulatoryRef: WHO Handbook for Guideline Development (2nd ed.); NICE PMG20 Developing NICE guidelines
questions.remediation: Store guideline id and version with each recommendation and run a currency check on every knowledge update that blocks recommendations citing withdrawn versions.
questions.text: Does the agent record which clinical guideline and version each recommendation relies on, and flag recommendations that rely on superseded guideline versions?

questions.failureMode: The agent auto-completes the time-out using a surgical plan built from the wrong side or another patient's imaging, and the mismatch reaches the operating room.
questions.l1: No surgical safety automation; surgical checklists are paper-based with no automated verification or compliance tracking
questions.l2: Checklist items are captured digitally for some procedures, but sign-in, time-out and sign-out are not enforced as separate phases
questions.l3: Agent digitizes the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist with sign-in/time-out/sign-out phases, but does not integrate with surgical scheduling, equipment verification, or post-operative monitoring
questions.l4: Checklist phases are enforced and linked to the surgical schedule and implant records, but intraoperative alerts and post-operative detection are missing
questions.l5: Full surgical safety orchestration with automated checklist compliance, surgical scheduling integration, equipment/implant verification, intraoperative monitoring alerts, post-operative complication detection, and surgical outcome tracking per WHO checklist and JCI COP.7
questions.regulatoryRef: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist 2nd ed.; JCI COP.7
questions.remediation: Block the agent from marking time-out complete until site, side and implant identifiers match the scheduled procedure and imaging, logging every mismatch.
questions.text: Does the agent implement surgical safety per WHO Surgical Safety Checklist (2nd ed.) and JCI Standard COP.7 with pre/intra/post-operative verification?

questions.failureMode: The agent silently adjusts a titration after a patient deteriorates and never raises a candidate adverse event, so a reportable incident is missed.
questions.l1: No adverse event automation; clinical adverse events are reported manually with potential underreporting and delayed submissions
questions.l2: Adverse events the agent encounters are noted in free text, with no structured capture or report drafting
questions.l3: Agent facilitates adverse event capture and generates MedWatch/vigilance reports, but does not implement automated event detection or trend analysis
questions.l4: Candidate events are queued for human reportability decisions, but deadline tracking or trend-to-CAPA linkage is not yet evidenced
questions.l5: Candidate events detected by the agent are queued for human reportability decisions with timestamps; reportable events are submitted within regulatory deadlines (sample audit); trends are reviewed and linked to CAPA records
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA 21 CFR Part 803; EU MDR 2017/745 Art. 87
questions.remediation: Open a candidate adverse event record whenever an agent titration or device output coincides with a harm signal, routed to a human with a deadline timer.
questions.text: Does the agent support adverse event and serious incident reporting per FDA 21 CFR Part 803 and EU MDR 2017/745 Article 87 vigilance requirements?

questions.failureMode: The agent keeps recommending lower-intensity treatment for one demographic group after a model update, and clinicians accept it because no subgroup check runs.
questions.l1: No subgroup performance review of CDS outputs
questions.l2: Demographic fields are stored with CDS outputs, but no subgroup performance analysis has been run
questions.l3: Subgroup performance was reviewed once; mitigations are undocumented
questions.l4: Subgroup performance is monitored on a schedule against a documented threshold, but it is not re-run after each model change or reported to governance
questions.l5: Subgroup performance is monitored on a schedule and after each model change; disparities above a documented threshold trigger recorded mitigation; results are reviewed by clinical governance
questions.remediation: Run a subgroup performance job after every model or prompt change and on a schedule, opening a mitigation record when a group's error rate passes the threshold.
questions.text: Does the agent's deploying covered entity make reasonable efforts to mitigate discrimination risk from its clinical decision support outputs per 45 CFR §92.210(c), including monitoring performance by race, color, national origin, sex, age and disability where data permit?

questions.failureMode: The agent's recommendation is not recorded next to the clinician's order, so after a harm event no one can tell whether staff followed or overrode the AI.
questions.l1: No clinical audit trail; treatment decisions and modifications are not systematically recorded with attribution
questions.l2: Some clinical decisions are logged with user attribution, but the AI recommendation shown is not captured alongside them
questions.l3: Agent logs major clinical decisions with timestamps and user attribution, but does not implement Part 11 compliant electronic signatures or prevent audit trail tampering
questions.l4: Recommendation, model version, clinician action and override reason are logged and tamper-evident, but e-signatures on FDA records do not meet Part 11
questions.l5: Sampled decisions show recommendation, model version, clinician action and override reason with timestamps; audit trails cannot be edited by users; electronic signatures meet Part 11 where records are FDA-regulated
questions.remediation: Log the exact recommendation text, model version and clinician accept or override reason in an append-only store at display time, and test that users cannot edit it.
questions.text: Does the agent keep an attributable audit trail of clinical decisions it supports, including the AI recommendation shown and any clinician override, with secure time-stamped audit trails per 21 CFR §11.10(e) for FDA-regulated records?

questions.failureMode: The agent ships a hotfix to its dose-calculation tool without integration or system testing because no safety class drives the release gate.
questions.l1: No software lifecycle management; clinical AI updates are deployed without systematic development process controls
questions.l2: Agent code is in version control, but releases have no change documentation or assigned software safety class
questions.l3: Agent tracks software versions and maintains basic change documentation, but does not implement full IEC 62304 software development lifecycle with safety classification-appropriate rigor
questions.l4: Safety class is assigned and Clause 5 activities are performed, but the Clause 6 maintenance process and anomaly resolution tracking are incomplete
questions.l5: Full IEC 62304 compliance with safety classification-driven development rigor, software requirements traceability, architecture documentation, unit/integration/system testing per Clause 5.5-5.7, and maintenance process per Clause 6 with anomaly resolution tracking
questions.remediation: Assign an IEC 62304 safety class to each agent software item, including the dose-calculation tool, and gate releases on the tests that class requires.
questions.text: Does the agent manage medical device software lifecycle per IEC 62304:2006/AMD1:2015 Clause 5 software development process for clinical AI?

questions.failureMode: The agent proposes a titration step larger than the safe increment because hazards such as stale vitals or a hallucinated lab value were never analysed.
questions.l1: No clinical risk management; AI-assisted clinical decisions are not subject to systematic hazard identification or risk assessment
questions.l2: Hazards for the AI function are listed informally, with no risk estimates or linked controls
questions.l3: Agent maintains a risk management file with identified hazards for major clinical AI functions, but risk estimation and control measures are not systematically updated with real-world evidence
questions.l4: Hazards, quantitative estimates and verified controls are maintained, but post-market evidence does not trigger risk file updates on a defined cadence
questions.l5: Comprehensive clinical risk management with systematic hazard identification per Clause 5, quantitative risk estimation per Clause 6, risk control implementation and verification per Clause 7, residual risk evaluation, and continuous post-market risk monitoring with evidence-based updates
questions.remediation: Add agent hazards (hallucinated lab value, stale vitals, out-of-range titration step) to the risk file, each with a verified control such as a hard dose-step limit.
questions.text: Does the agent implement clinical risk management per ISO 14971:2019 Clause 5-7 hazard identification, risk estimation, and risk control for AI-assisted clinical decisions?

questions.failureMode: The agent presents only its top-ranked treatment, so clinician and patient defer to the AI without weighing alternatives or the patient's preferences.
questions.l1: No shared decision-making support; treatment options are presented without patient preference integration or decision aid tools
questions.l2: The agent presents a single recommended treatment; alternatives appear only when the clinician asks
questions.l3: Agent presents treatment options with basic risk/benefit information, but does not implement structured decision aids or patient preference elicitation
questions.l4: Validated decision aids and preference elicitation are used with risk communication, but decision quality is not measured
questions.l5: Full shared decision-making with validated decision aids, patient preference elicitation tools, risk communication per Ottawa DSF, treatment option comparison with personalized outcome predictions, and decision quality measurement
questions.regulatoryRef: NICE NG197 Shared decision making; Ottawa DSF
questions.remediation: Require the agent to present every guideline-supported option with absolute risk figures and record the patient's stated preference before a plan is finalised.
questions.text: Does the agent support shared clinical decision-making per NICE Shared Decision Making guidelines and Ottawa Decision Support Framework?

questions.failureMode: The agent ignores a patient's free-text note about an herbal product and proposes an anticoagulant without checking the herb-drug interaction.
questions.l1: No CAM safety integration; alternative medicine use is not tracked or assessed for interactions with conventional treatments
questions.l2: Traditional and complementary medicine use is captured as free-text notes that the agent does not parse or check
questions.l3: Agent records patient-reported CAM use and checks major herb-drug interaction databases, but does not integrate CAM safety into the overall clinical risk assessment
questions.l4: Structured capture and checks against a named, dated source run with clinician review, but related adverse events are not reported
questions.l5: Patient-reported use is captured in structured form; interaction checks run against a named, dated source; flagged interactions are reviewed by a clinician; adverse events linked to such products are reported
questions.remediation: Parse patient-reported herbal and traditional products into structured entries and check them against a named, dated interaction source before any new prescription.
questions.text: Does the agent record patient-reported traditional and complementary medicine use and check it for interactions with conventional treatment, consistent with the WHO Global Traditional Medicine Strategy 2025-2034?

questions.failureMode: The agent's protocol adherence degrades in the field after a data source change, and no post-market follow-up data reaches the clinical evaluation to catch it.
questions.l1: No PMS plan or PMCF for the AI function
questions.l2: Complaints and incidents involving the AI function are logged, but no PMS plan defines what data is collected
questions.l3: PMS data is collected, but no PMCF plan exists or PMCF results do not update the clinical evaluation
questions.l4: PMS and PMCF plans exist and PMCF reports update the clinical evaluation, but claims are not traceable to specific PMCF evidence
questions.l5: PMS plan and PMCF plan exist; PMCF evaluation reports are dated and feed the clinical evaluation update; the notified body can trace each claim to PMCF evidence
questions.regulatoryRef: EU MDR 2017/745 Art. 83; EU MDR 2017/745 Annex XIV Part B
questions.remediation: Feed agent performance data (override rates, protocol deviation alerts, field incidents) into a PMCF plan whose dated reports trigger a clinical evaluation update.
questions.text: For MDR-regulated clinical AI, does the agent support the post-market surveillance system (MDR Art. 83) and the PMCF plan and evaluation report (Annex XIV Part B), linked to the clinical evaluation?

questions.failureMode: The agent's anatomical segmentation is released after a model update without verification, and surgical plans are built on mislabelled structures.
questions.l1: No design verification; outputs are not verified against inputs and evidence is missing or ad hoc
questions.l2: Some outputs are tested, but tests are not linked to design inputs and acceptance criteria are not written
questions.l3: Maintains some verification tests and trace links, but coverage is incomplete and acceptance criteria are inconsistently documented
questions.l4: Verification protocols have acceptance criteria and full traceability, but release is not blocked automatically when evidence is missing
questions.l5: Full design verification governance with protocol templates, defined acceptance criteria, traceability completeness checks, automated gap reporting, and release gating on verification evidence
questions.remediation: Write acceptance criteria per design input, such as segmentation accuracy on a labelled test set, and block release when a trace link lacks a passing result.
questions.text: Does the agent manage and evidence design and development verification per ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.3 as incorporated by FDA 21 CFR §820.10 (QMSR), including verification planning, objective evidence that design outputs meet design inputs, acceptance criteria, and bidirectional traceability (input -> output -> verification results)?

questions.failureMode: The agent's interface pre-fills acceptance of its recommendations, and clinicians click through an incorrect suggestion because automation bias was never tested.
questions.l1: No usability evaluation; UI/workflow changes ship without summative evidence for safety-critical tasks
questions.l2: Informal user feedback on agent screens is gathered, with no use-related risk scenarios
questions.l3: Performs some usability testing, but it is not tied to use-related risk controls and evidence is incomplete for regulated review
questions.l4: Summative studies with representative users are traced to risk controls, but residual use-related risk acceptance is not documented for every task
questions.l5: Full usability evaluation lifecycle with use-related risk scenarios, representative-user studies, traceability to risk controls, documented residual risk acceptance, and audit-ready reports
questions.remediation: Run summative usability tests in which representative clinicians face seeded wrong AI recommendations, and record whether they catch them.
questions.text: Does the agent support usability engineering per IEC 62366-1:2015+AMD1:2020 by capturing summative usability evaluation evidence for safety-critical clinical workflows (use-related risk scenarios, representative users, documented residual use-related risk)?

questions.failureMode: The agent misses protocol deviations repeatedly, but the failures are handled as IT tickets outside the QMS, so no CAPA or change control follows.
questions.l1: No MDR QMS; controls are scattered and not governed by an audit-ready QMS framework
questions.l2: A few procedures exist (for example CAPA), but they do not cover the AI function or name owners
questions.l3: Has documented procedures for some Art. 10(9) elements, but integration, ownership, and evidence linkage are incomplete
questions.l4: Integrated procedures with named owners and evidence pointers exist, but audit packs are assembled by hand and QMS effectiveness is not monitored
questions.l5: Comprehensive MDR QMS orchestration with integrated procedures, evidence pointers per control, automated audit pack generation, and continuous monitoring of QMS effectiveness
questions.remediation: Route nonconforming agent outputs, such as a missed protocol deviation, into the MDR QMS nonconformity and CAPA procedure with a named owner and due date.
questions.text: Does the agent implement and evidence EU MDR 2017/745 Article 10(9) manufacturer QMS requirements, including integrated procedures for risk management, clinical evaluation, PMS/vigilance, control of nonconforming outputs, CAPA, and change control (with role/accountability assignments)?

questions.failureMode: The agent's titration logic has no approved input defining the maximum dose step, so it applies a developer-chosen value with no safety margin review.
questions.l1: No controlled design inputs; requirements are informal and not approved or traceable
questions.l2: Requirements exist in tickets or documents, but are not reviewed or approved
questions.l3: Maintains requirements, but completeness/conflict checks and approval/traceability are inconsistent
questions.l4: Inputs are structured, approved, conflict-checked and traced, but regulatory, safety and usability coverage is not checked systematically
questions.l5: Full design input control with structured requirements, review/approval workflow, conflict detection, regulatory/safety/usability coverage checks, and bidirectional traceability to verification/validation evidence
questions.remediation: Write titration safety limits (maximum step, minimum interval, hold conditions) as approved, testable design inputs and trace each to a V&V result.
questions.text: Does the agent manage design and development inputs per ISO 13485:2016 §7.3.3, ensuring inputs are complete/unambiguous, include regulatory + safety + usability requirements, are reviewed/approved, and are traced through outputs, verification, and validation?

questions.failureMode: The agent runs in production with a protocol rule file that drifted from the validated baseline, so deviations it should flag pass unchecked.
questions.l1: No controlled production processes; releases and configuration changes are manual and not validated or monitored
questions.l2: Releases are scripted, but configuration and model weights are copied by hand with no record of what was deployed
questions.l3: Uses CI/CD and basic change controls, but environment/configuration drift and release validation evidence are incomplete
questions.l4: Pipelines are validated and configuration baselines enforced, but production KPIs are not linked to deviation and CAPA handling
questions.l5: Fully controlled production controls with validated pipelines, configuration baselines, segregation of duties, monitored production KPIs, deviation/CAPA linkage, and audit-ready release evidence
questions.remediation: Pin model weights, prompts and protocol rule files to a signed configuration baseline and open a deviation record on any production drift.
questions.text: Does the agent enforce production and process controls per ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.5.1 as incorporated by FDA 21 CFR §820.10 (QMSR) for clinical AI systems (controlled build/release processes, configuration/environment controls, process validation where applicable, and production monitoring with deviation handling)?

regulatoryReferences.citation: FDA Quality Management System Regulation (21 CFR Part 820, incorporating ISO 13485:2016 by reference)
ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice
ISO 13485:2016 Medical devices — Quality management systems

clinical-trials.certificationPath: L1 Basic trial data collection → L2 GCP-compliant electronic data capture → L3 Full ICH E6(R3) compliance with risk-based monitoring → L4 AI-enhanced trial design and adaptive protocols → L5 Autonomous clinical trial governance with verified participant safety and data integrity
clinical-trials.description: Drug and therapy testing, efficacy assurance, and participant management — covering the clinical trial lifecycle from protocol design through participant recruitment, data collection, analysis, and reporting with emphasis on participant safety, data integrity, and regulatory compliance.
clinical-trials.euAIActClassification: Art. 6(1) and Annex I (Regulation (EU) 2017/745 MDR, 2017/746 IVDR) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a medical device; Art. 2(6) excludes systems developed and put into service solely for scientific research and development
keyRisks: Participant safety compromise from AI-managed dose escalation
Data integrity failures in AI-processed clinical trial data
Informed consent violations through AI-mediated participant communication
Selection bias in AI-driven participant recruitment algorithms
Regulatory rejection due to AI-generated data quality issues
clinical-trials.name: Clinical Trials

questions.failureMode: The agent schedules the next dose cohort while an unassessed serious adverse event sits in its queue, exposing new participants to a higher dose.
questions.l1: No safety monitoring automation; adverse events are reported manually with potential delays in serious adverse event detection
questions.l2: Adverse events are logged by the agent, but serious events are not distinguished or timed against reporting deadlines
questions.l3: Agent tracks adverse events and generates safety reports per §312.32 timelines, but there is no risk-based monitoring plan or aggregate safety review
questions.l4: SAE candidates are queued for human assessment and IND deadlines are met in samples, but DSMB reports or narratives lack an accountable reviewer
questions.l5: Risk-based monitoring plan exists; SAE candidates detected by the agent are queued for human assessment with timestamps; 7-day/15-day IND reports meet deadlines in a sample audit; DSMB reports and narratives are reviewed by an accountable person
questions.remediation: Check emerging adverse event data against the protocol's dose-escalation stopping criteria before the agent schedules the next cohort, holding for human review.
questions.text: Does the agent support participant safety monitoring per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.11.4 (monitoring) and §3.13 (safety assessment and reporting) and FDA 21 CFR §312.32 IND safety reporting?

questions.failureMode: The agent answers consent questions with paraphrased risk information not in the approved form, or presents an outdated form after an amendment.
questions.l1: No digital consent management; informed consent is paper-based with no AI-specific disclosures or ongoing consent verification
questions.l2: Consent forms are electronic, but required elements and AI disclosures are not checked
questions.l3: Agent manages electronic informed consent with §50.25 required elements and AI disclosures, but does not support dynamic consent for protocol amendments or multimedia consent delivery
questions.l4: eConsent has all elements, AI disclosures, comprehension checks and re-consent, but form versions are not matched to IRB/IEC approval
questions.l5: Full eConsent with all §50.25 elements, AI-specific disclosures, comprehension checks, re-consent for amendments, and IRB/IEC-approved consent form version control per ICH E6(R3) §2.8
questions.remediation: Block the agent from presenting any consent form version that does not match the current IRB/IEC-approved version, and log the version each participant signed.
questions.text: Does the agent enforce informed consent per FDA 21 CFR §50.25 required elements and ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §2.8 with AI-specific disclosures?

questions.failureMode: The agent maps a CRF field to the wrong SDTM variable or invents a controlled-terminology value, producing submission datasets that fail validation.
questions.l1: No CDISC compliance; clinical data is collected in proprietary formats without standardized variable definitions
questions.l2: Case report forms use some CDASH variable names, with no SDTM mapping
questions.l3: Agent implements CDASH-aligned case report forms and generates SDTM datasets, but does not automate mapping validation or implement full CDISC compliance checking
questions.l4: CDASH eCRFs, validated SDTM mapping, ADaM and define.xml exist, but traceability from collection to submission is not checked end to end
questions.l5: Full CDISC implementation with CDASH-compliant eCRF design, automated SDTM mapping with Pinnacle 21 validation, ADaM dataset generation, define.xml creation, and end-to-end data standards compliance from collection through submission
questions.regulatoryRef: CDISC CDASH v2.2; CDISC SDTM v2.0
questions.remediation: Validate every SDTM dataset the agent generates against conformance rules before release, with a mapping spec tracing each variable to its CDASH source.
questions.text: Does the agent maintain clinical data standards per CDISC CDASH v2.2 for data collection and SDTM v2.0 for regulatory submission datasets?

questions.failureMode: The agent detects a protocol deviation but logs it only in the EDC, so the IRB never receives it and continuing review proceeds on incomplete information.
questions.l1: No IRB management automation; ethics committee submissions and approvals are tracked manually
questions.l2: Approval letters are stored, but the agent does not track submission status or approval expiry
questions.l3: Agent tracks IRB submission status and approval timelines, but does not automate continuing review preparation or protocol deviation reporting
questions.l4: Submissions, continuing reviews, deviations and amendments are tracked, but multi-site IRB coordination and annual reports are manual
questions.l5: Comprehensive IRB management with automated submission preparation, continuing review documentation, protocol deviation reporting, amendment tracking, annual report generation, and multi-site IRB coordination per 21 CFR Part 56 and EU CTR Art. 4
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA 21 CFR Part 56; EU CTR 536/2014 Art. 4
questions.remediation: File each protocol deviation the agent detects to the site's IRB reporting queue with category and date, and flag continuing review dates ahead of lapse.
questions.text: Does the agent manage IRB/Ethics Committee oversight per FDA 21 CFR Part 56 and EU CTR 536/2014 Article 4 ethics committee assessment?

questions.failureMode: The agent's pre-screening ranks candidates by EHR data completeness, systematically filtering out underrepresented groups with sparser records.
questions.l1: No recruitment equity; participant selection algorithms may exclude underrepresented populations or perpetuate historical trial enrollment biases
questions.l2: Enrolment demographics are reported after the fact, with no goals or eligibility-criteria review
questions.l3: Agent monitors demographic enrollment metrics and flags underrepresentation, but does not implement proactive diversity recruitment strategies or assess eligibility criteria for unnecessary exclusions
questions.l4: Goals and criteria review are documented and subgroup enrolment is tracked, but shortfalls do not trigger recorded actions
questions.l5: Enrolment goals and eligibility-criteria review are documented per trial; enrolment by subgroup is tracked against goals; shortfalls trigger recorded actions; the guidance status is tracked as draft
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA Diversity Action Plans draft guidance (2024); ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.1
questions.remediation: Audit the agent's pre-screening selection rates by subgroup against enrolment goals weekly, and require a recorded action when any group falls below goal.
questions.text: Does the agent support equitable participant recruitment, checking eligibility criteria for unnecessary exclusions and tracking enrolment against diversity goals, per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.1 trial design and FDA's Diversity Action Plans draft guidance (June 2024)?

questions.failureMode: The agent auto-corrects out-of-range lab values in the EDC without recording the original value or reason, erasing evidence a monitor would need.
questions.l1: Agent edits are not attributable and the agent is not in the computerised-systems inventory
questions.l2: Agent edits are attributed to a service account, but no audit trail of prior values or validation exists
questions.l3: Audit trail exists, but agent version or correction rationale is missing, or validation is not proportionate to risk
questions.l4: Agent version, reason and timestamp are recorded and validation is risk-proportionate, but Part 11 signature controls are not evidenced
questions.l5: Every agent-made capture or correction records agent version, reason and timestamp; the agent is in the computerised-systems inventory with risk-proportionate validation records; Part 11 controls are evidenced for electronic records and signatures
questions.regulatoryRef: ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §4.2.2, §4.2.4, §4.3; FDA 21 CFR Part 11
questions.remediation: Record agent version, correction reason and prior value with every data change the agent makes, and add it to the computerised-systems inventory.
questions.text: Does the agent capture metadata and audit trails for trial data it captures, transforms or corrects (ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §4.2.2, §4.2.4), and is it managed as a validated computerised system (§4.3) meeting FDA 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic trial records?

questions.failureMode: The agent posts a registry update whose primary outcome or enrolment figure contradicts the protocol, undermining the trial record.
questions.l1: No trial registration management; registration and results reporting obligations are tracked manually with risk of non-compliance
questions.l2: The trial is registered, but update and results deadlines are not tracked
questions.l3: Agent tracks registration status and results reporting deadlines, but does not automate registration data updates or results submission preparation
questions.l4: Registry data elements and results submissions are prepared automatically, but registrations are not cross-checked across registries
questions.l5: Full registration compliance with automated WHO ICTRP data element population, ClinicalTrials.gov registration and update management, results reporting within 42 CFR Part 11 timelines, and protocol registration verification across multiple registries
questions.regulatoryRef: WHO ICTRP Registration Standards; 42 CFR Part 11
questions.remediation: Generate registry updates from the trial master record, check them for consistency across registries, and require a human approver on each.
questions.text: Does the agent support trial registration per WHO ICTRP standards and ClinicalTrials.gov 42 CFR Part 11 results reporting requirements?

questions.failureMode: The agent drafts a results manuscript whose participant flow numbers do not match the locked database and omits withdrawn participants.
questions.l1: No CONSORT compliance; trial reports do not follow standardized reporting guidelines
questions.l2: Trial reports follow a house template that addresses some CONSORT items
questions.l3: Agent generates trial report templates aligned with the CONSORT checklist, but does not generate the participant flow diagram or check completeness of every checklist item
questions.l4: Flow diagram generation and checklist completeness checks run, but harms reporting per the CONSORT extension is not covered
questions.l5: Full CONSORT compliance with automated participant flow diagram generation, complete checklist item documentation, subgroup analysis reporting, harm reporting per CONSORT extension, and publication-ready manuscript preparation with all required elements
questions.remediation: Generate the participant flow diagram from EDC disposition counts and block report drafts whose numbers do not reconcile with the locked database.
questions.text: Does the agent support CONSORT 2025 compliant trial reporting with complete and transparent results disclosure?

questions.failureMode: The agent assigns a kit that had a temperature excursion, or reveals the treatment arm in a resupply message and breaks the blind.
questions.l1: No supply chain management; investigational product distribution, storage, and accountability are tracked manually
questions.l2: IP stock is counted at sites periodically, with no link to dispensing
questions.l3: Agent tracks IP inventory and distribution, but does not implement temperature monitoring, expiry management, or randomization-integrated dispensing
questions.l4: Temperature monitoring, expiry management and randomisation-driven dispensing run, but accountability or blinding integrity checks are incomplete
questions.l5: Comprehensive IP supply chain with temperature-monitored distribution, expiry management, randomization-integrated dispensing, accountability reconciliation, return/destruction documentation, and blinding integrity verification per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.15.3
questions.remediation: Quarantine kits automatically on temperature excursion or expiry so the agent cannot assign them, with dispensing driven only by the randomisation system.
questions.text: Does the agent manage investigational product supply per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.15.3?

questions.failureMode: The agent enrols a minor on a parent's consent alone and skips the age-appropriate assent step.
questions.l1: No vulnerable population protections; consent processes do not differentiate for children, cognitively impaired, or other vulnerable groups
questions.l2: Age is checked at enrolment, but other vulnerable conditions are not identified
questions.l3: Agent identifies vulnerable participants and applies additional consent requirements, but does not implement age-appropriate assent processes or legally authorized representative management
questions.l4: Assent, representative consent and capacity reassessment are recorded, but Subpart D and Art. 32 conditions are not checked before enrolment
questions.l5: Assent and legally acceptable representative consent are captured where required; capacity reassessment is scheduled and recorded; Subpart D and Art. 32 conditions are checked before enrolment
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA 21 CFR Part 50 Subpart D; ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §2.8; EU CTR 536/2014 Art. 32
questions.remediation: Before enrolling a minor or a participant lacking capacity, require recorded assent or representative consent and block enrolment without it.
questions.text: Does the agent implement vulnerable-population protections per FDA 21 CFR Part 50 Subpart D (children), ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §2.8 consent provisions and EU CTR 536/2014 Art. 32 (minors)?

questions.failureMode: The agent's remote-data pipeline silently drops wearable readings for some participants, and no tolerance limit flags the loss of an endpoint data stream.
questions.l1: AI-managed trial activities and DHTs are outside the quality management system
questions.l2: AI-managed activities are known to the quality team, but are not in the risk assessment
questions.l3: Risks of AI-managed activities and DHTs are listed, but critical-to-quality factors or tolerance limits do not cover them, or DHT fitness-for-purpose evidence is missing
questions.l4: CtQ factors and tolerance limits cover AI-managed activities and DHTs have V&V evidence, but breaches beyond limits are not consistently acted on
questions.l5: Critical-to-quality factors and quality tolerance limits cover AI-managed decentralised activities; each DHT has verification and validation evidence for its use; deviations beyond limits are recorded and acted on; the E6(R3) transition is documented
questions.regulatoryRef: ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.10; FDA Conducting Clinical Trials With Decentralized Elements guidance (2024); FDA Digital Health Technologies for Remote Data Acquisition guidance (2023)
questions.remediation: Set a quality tolerance limit for each AI-managed decentralised activity, such as remote data completeness, and alert the study team on breach.
questions.text: Does the agent operate under the sponsor's ICH E6(R3) risk-based quality management (Annex 1 §3.10), with critical-to-quality factors and quality tolerance limits covering AI-managed decentralised elements and digital health technologies used for remote data acquisition, as described in FDA's decentralized-elements (2024) and DHT (2023) guidances?

questions.failureMode: The agent closes a monitoring finding as resolved because a field was edited, without the source document verification the monitor required.
questions.l1: No electronic monitoring controls; monitor access is unmanaged and monitoring evidence/follow-up is incomplete or not audit-ready
questions.l2: Monitors use shared EDC credentials, with no activity log
questions.l3: Implements basic remote monitoring access and findings tracking, but activity logging, SDV approach documentation, and closure evidence are inconsistent
questions.l4: Role-based access, uneditable activity logs and SDV plans exist, but findings do not link to CAPA or monitoring evidence is not consolidated
questions.l5: Role-based monitor access, monitor activity logs users cannot edit, SDV/SDR plan management, consolidated centralised and on-site monitoring evidence, CAPA linkage, and inspection-ready monitoring reports
questions.remediation: Give monitors role-based access to eSource, EDC and eTMF, log every view and finding, and have the agent track each finding to closure with a due date.
questions.text: Does the agent support electronic/remote monitoring per ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §3.11.4 by enforcing controlled monitor access to electronic systems (eSource/EDC/eTMF), logging monitor activities and findings, supporting documented SDV/SDR approaches, and tracking follow-up actions to closure?

questions.failureMode: The agent classifies a suspected unexpected serious reaction as expected using outdated reference safety information, so the SUSAR is never reported.
questions.l1: No EU CTR safety reporting; SUSAR/periodic safety reporting is manual, inconsistent, or not traceable to source safety cases
questions.l2: EU safety cases are recorded, but SUSAR deadlines are not tracked
questions.l3: Tracks EU safety cases and reporting deadlines, but reconciliation, completeness checks, and submission evidence are incomplete
questions.l4: SUSAR and annual safety reports are orchestrated and reconciled to cases, but compliance across member states is not monitored continuously
questions.l5: Full EU CTR safety reporting automation with SUSAR + periodic safety report orchestration, case/report reconciliation, submission evidence retention, audit trails, and continuous compliance monitoring across member states
questions.remediation: Reconcile every safety case against submitted SUSAR and annual reports daily, flagging cases with no submission before their reporting deadline.
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU CTR 536/2014 Articles 41-43 safety reporting workflows (investigator-to-sponsor reporting, SUSAR reporting to the Agency, annual safety reporting), with timelines, submission tracking, and reconciliation against case processing?

questions.failureMode: The agent's storage clean-up job deletes investigator case histories before the retention period ends, leaving the trial unable to support an inspection.
questions.l1: No retention governance; site records are incomplete or retention periods are not tracked/enforced
questions.l2: Site records are kept, but retention periods are undefined
questions.l3: Maintains records and basic retention policies, but trigger-based retention scheduling, completeness checks, and retrieval readiness are inconsistent
questions.l4: Completeness checks and trigger-based retention run, but retrieval for inspection or cross-system linkage is untested
questions.l5: Full §312.62 compliance with record completeness checks, trigger-based retention automation, defensible destruction holds, rapid retrieval/export for inspection, and cross-system linkage (EDC/eSource/pharmacy/IRB) with audit logs
questions.remediation: Calculate each record's retention end date from its regulatory trigger and place a destruction hold the agent cannot override before that date.
questions.text: Does the agent enforce investigator recordkeeping and retention per FDA 21 CFR §312.62, including complete case histories, drug disposition records, and retention scheduling based on regulatory triggers (e.g., 2 years after marketing application approval or discontinuation/withdrawal notice)?

questions.failureMode: The agent sends recruitment messages for a new site before that site's ethics committee approval is recorded.
questions.l1: No Helsinki governance; approvals are not reliably tracked and study activities can proceed without confirmed independent ethics approval
questions.l2: Approval letters are filed, but there is no tracking of conditions and no gate on study start
questions.l3: Tracks ethics approvals, but enforcement (no-start gating) and condition/continuing oversight tracking are inconsistent
questions.l4: No-start gates and condition tracking are enforced, but continuing oversight reminders or escalation workflows are incomplete
questions.l5: Full Helsinki-aligned ethics governance with no-start/no-change gates, approval condition tracking, continuing oversight reminders, deviation/escalation workflows, and audit-ready ethics committee evidence exports
questions.remediation: Gate every activity the agent can trigger (recruitment messages, screening, randomisation) on a recorded ethics approval for that site and protocol version.
questions.text: Does the agent implement research ethics committee governance consistent with Declaration of Helsinki §23 by ensuring protocol/materials are submitted for independent ethics review and approval prior to trial start, tracking conditions/approvals, and preventing study activities prior to documented approval?

questions.failureMode: The agent copies participant names and trial health data into a prompt to an external model, outside the documented research basis and safeguards.
questions.l1: No GDPR research basis/safeguards; health data is processed without a documented Art. 9(2)(j) basis or consistent safeguards
questions.l2: A research basis is assumed but undocumented, and trial data is processed with direct identifiers
questions.l3: Documents a research basis and applies some safeguards (e.g., pseudonyms), but minimization, retention, and access governance are inconsistent across systems/vendors
questions.l4: Lawful basis, default safeguards, retention and access reviews exist, but DPIA linkage or supervisory-authority evidence is incomplete
questions.l5: Full GDPR research governance with documented lawful basis, safeguards-by-default across EDC/eSource/analytics, automated retention + access reviews, DPIA linkage, and audit-ready evidence for supervisory authorities and partners
questions.remediation: Give the agent only pseudonymised trial data, keep the re-identification key in a separate system it cannot call, and log every key access.
questions.text: Does the agent implement GDPR special-category health data processing for scientific research under Art. 9(2)(j), including Art. 89 safeguards (pseudonymisation where possible, purpose limitation, data minimization, access controls, and retention governance) for clinical trial datasets and operational systems?

regulatoryReferences.citation: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for Good Clinical Practice
FDA human subject protection, IRBs and IND regulations (21 CFR Parts 50, 56 and 312)
WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform standards
ISO 14155:2026 Clinical investigation of medical devices for human subjects — Good clinical practice

cognition-to-intelligence.certificationPath: L1 Basic data processing → L2 GDPR-compliant profiling controls → L3 EU AI Act high-risk compliance → L4 ISO 42001 AI management certified → L5 Autonomous explainable intelligence with continuous bias monitoring and democratic oversight
cognition-to-intelligence.description: Contextual data interpretation moving from master data through meta, empirical, analytical, to contextual intelligence — profiled, personalized, and preferentiated — AI agents that transform raw data into actionable, trusted intelligence with explainability and bias controls.
cognition-to-intelligence.euAIActClassification: General Purpose AI — Chapter V obligations for general-purpose AI models (Art. 53; Art. 51 classification with systemic risk) where the agent provides or integrates a GPAI model; Art. 50 transparency for systems interacting with natural persons
keyRisks: Discriminatory automated decisions affecting rights per GDPR Art. 22
Context collapse in personalization leading to filter bubbles
Opaque intelligence surfaces eroding human agency
Data quality degradation amplified by AI inference chains
Over-personalization enabling manipulation and behavioral nudging
cognition-to-intelligence.name: Cognition to Intelligence

questions.failureMode: The agent hands a deployer a risk score with no stated inputs or confidence, so the reviewer accepts an output whose known limitation applied.
questions.l1: Outputs ship with no stated inputs, confidence or limitations, and no instructions for use exist.
questions.l2: Free-text explanations accompany a few output types; no confidence or limitation fields, and instructions for use are an unpublished draft.
questions.l3: Explanations (e.g. feature attribution) are attached to some output types, or instructions for use omit at least one Art. 13(3)(b) item (capabilities, limitations, output interpretation).
questions.l4: Every output type carries an explanation record enforced by a release test, but instructions for use are not re-issued when the model or prompts change.
questions.l5: Every output type carries an explanation record (main inputs, confidence or uncertainty, known limitations); instructions for use cover each Art. 13(3)(b) item; an automated test per release fails when an output type ships without its explanation record.
questions.remediation: Add a release test that enumerates every intelligence output type and fails when one ships without an explanation record holding inputs, confidence and limitations.
questions.text: Does the agent attach an explanation to every intelligence output and supply instructions for use covering capabilities, limitations and output interpretation, as EU AI Act Art. 13 requires for high-risk systems (Annex III systems from 2 December 2027)?

questions.failureMode: The agent is retrained on a refreshed dataset that under-represents a protected group and starts ranking that group lower, with no examination catching it.
questions.l1: No documented bias examination of training, validation or testing data; special-category personal data used for bias work without a recorded necessity decision.
questions.l2: Bias checks ran once on the training set with no named metrics; special-category data was pulled for bias work without any necessity record.
questions.l3: Documented bias examination with named metrics exists for some but not all of the training, validation and testing data sets, or special-category processing lacks a written strict-necessity record.
questions.l4: Bias examination with metrics covers training, validation and testing data each release, but special-category processing lacks access or deletion records.
questions.l5: Bias examination records with metrics and mitigation actions exist for training, validation and testing data for every release; each special-category processing for bias correction has a strict-necessity record, an access log and a deletion record; examination re-runs on each dataset change.
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 10(2)(f)-(g); EU AI Act Art. 4a (inserted by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
questions.remediation: Gate each dataset version on a bias examination job that computes named group metrics on the train, validation and test splits and blocks release above threshold.
questions.text: For a high-risk AI system it provides, does the agent's provider examine training, validation and testing data for possible biases and apply measures to detect, prevent and mitigate them (EU AI Act Art. 10(2)(f)-(g), applicable to Annex III systems from 2 December 2027), limiting any processing of special categories of personal data for that purpose to what is strictly necessary (Art. 4a)?

questions.failureMode: The agent's retrieval sources and model are swapped in production with no AI risk assessment rerun, so a degraded inference chain ships unnoticed.
questions.l1: No AI management system: no AI policy, AI risk assessment record or statement of applicability.
questions.l2: An AI policy exists, but no AI risk assessment covers the agent's intelligence pipelines.
questions.l3: AI policy and an AI risk assessment exist, but there is no statement of applicability for the Annex A controls, or no internal audit or management review on record.
questions.l4: Statement of applicability, internal audit and management review are on record, but nonconformities raised against the agent are not tracked to closure.
questions.l5: AIMS scope, AI policy, AI risk assessment and treatment records, statement of applicability for Annex A controls, and an internal audit and management review within the last 12 months; nonconformities tracked to closure.
questions.remediation: Write a statement of applicability mapping each Annex A control to the agent's pipelines and open a tracked nonconformity for every control that lacks evidence.
questions.text: Does the agent implement AI system lifecycle management per ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Annex A controls including risk assessment and continuous improvement?

questions.failureMode: The agent built for internal analytics is redeployed to score consumers without re-mapping context, so it applies enterprise assumptions to individuals.
questions.l1: No record of intended purpose, deployment context or applicable laws for deployed intelligence systems.
questions.l2: Intended purpose is described informally for the flagship system; deployment context and applicable laws are not recorded for any system.
questions.l3: MAP records (intended purpose, context and applicable laws per MAP 1.1, risk categorisation) exist for some deployed systems, or were not updated after the last material change.
questions.l4: MAP records cover MAP 1.1-5.2 for every deployed system and are updated on change, but are not linked to MEASURE and MANAGE entries.
questions.l5: Every deployed system has MAP records covering MAP 1.1-5.2, including impact characterisation; records are updated on each material change and linked to MEASURE and MANAGE entries.
questions.remediation: Make a MAP 1.1 context record (purpose, users, setting, laws) a deploy precondition and reopen it automatically whenever a material change ticket is filed.
questions.text: Does the agent implement NIST AI RMF Map function requirements for contextual risk identification in deployed intelligence systems?

questions.failureMode: The agent retrieves an erased user profile from a stale vector cache and keeps personalising on data the user had asked to delete.
questions.l1: No retention limits or purpose review for personal data in prompts, logs, training data or inference caches.
questions.l2: Log retention is set informally; prompts, traces and inference caches keep personal data indefinitely.
questions.l3: Documented purpose and retention periods for some stores (e.g. logs) but not for inference caches or training datasets, or erasure requests are not propagated to them.
questions.l4: Every store has a purpose and automated deletion, but erasure requests reach logs and caches and not fine-tuning sets, or lack completion records.
questions.l5: Every store holding personal data (prompts, logs, caches, training and fine-tuning sets) has a documented purpose and a retention period enforced by automated deletion; erasure requests reach every store with completion records.
questions.remediation: Inventory every store the inference pipeline writes (prompts, traces, vector caches, fine-tuning sets) and attach a TTL deletion job and an erasure hook to each.
questions.text: Does the agent enforce data minimization per GDPR Article 5(1)(c) in intelligence generation, preventing unnecessary personal data retention in AI inference pipelines?

questions.failureMode: The agent keeps pushing high-margin content to a vulnerable user and no human holds a control to override that personalization decision.
questions.l1: No human review or override path for personalization decisions.
questions.l2: Operators can switch personalization off globally, but nobody can review or override an individual personalization decision.
questions.l3: A human review path exists for some personalization decision types, but overrides are not logged or are not available to affected users.
questions.l4: Every decision type has a named reviewer and logged overrides, but override outcomes are not reviewed on a documented schedule.
questions.l5: Every personalization decision type has a named human reviewer with an override control; overrides and outcomes are logged and reviewed on a documented schedule.
questions.regulatoryRef: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021): Human oversight and determination
questions.remediation: Expose a per-decision override control to the named reviewer for each personalization decision type and write every override with its reason to an append-only log.
questions.text: Does the agent's personalization keep humans able to review and override its decisions, as set out in the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI principle 'Human oversight and determination'?

questions.failureMode: The agent's recommendation flips under a trivial input perturbation and the affected person has no route to contest the resulting decision.
questions.l1: Material-decision recommendations carry no explanation, no robustness test record, and no route for affected people to contest them.
questions.l2: Some material-decision recommendations carry a short explanation; there are no robustness tests and no contest route.
questions.l3: Explanations and a human review route exist, but there is no documented robustness testing or no contestation channel for affected people.
questions.l4: Explanations, robustness tests and a contestation channel exist for every decision type, but the accountability review does not run on a fixed schedule.
questions.l5: Human agency preserved with contestability mechanisms for material AI decisions, documented robustness testing, transparency documentation for each decision type, and a recorded accountability review on a fixed schedule.
questions.regulatoryRef: OECD AI Principles 1.3 Transparency and explainability; OECD AI Principles 1.4 Robustness, security and safety
questions.remediation: Add a contest link to every material-decision output that opens a case with the decision id, and run perturbation robustness tests per decision type before release.
questions.text: Does the agent support human agency in intelligence systems affecting material decisions, per OECD AI Principles 1.3 'Transparency and explainability' and 1.4 'Robustness, security and safety' (OECD/LEGAL/0449, amended 3 May 2024)?

questions.failureMode: The agent follows an instruction hidden in a retrieved web page and calls a write tool it was only meant to read with.
questions.l1: No documented adversarial security evaluation of the agent.
questions.l2: Ad hoc prompt-injection attempts before a launch; results undocumented and no coverage of extraction, excessive agency or tool misuse.
questions.l3: Adversarial tests run before release for some of the named categories; results documented but not re-run on model, prompt or tool changes.
questions.l4: The suite covers every named category and re-runs on each change, but does not block release or omits threat-model categories beyond the named four.
questions.l5: A documented test suite covers each named category and every further category in the agent's threat model, runs on each model, prompt or tool change, blocks release on failure, and stores results as MEASURE 2.7 evidence.
questions.remediation: Build a red-team suite for prompt injection, model extraction, excessive agency and tool misuse, run it on every model, prompt or tool change, and fail release on regression.
questions.text: Does the agent evaluate and document its security and resilience per NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.7, with adversarial tests covering at least prompt injection, model extraction, excessive agency and tool misuse?

questions.failureMode: The agent inserts a generated chart image into a report with no AI label or provenance, and readers take it as measured data.
questions.l1: No Art. 50 transparency and no legal-requirements register; intelligence systems generate content without synthetic media labeling and the legal and regulatory requirements that apply to them are not documented
questions.l2: A generic AI-generated footer appears on some outputs; applicable laws are known to staff but not listed anywhere.
questions.l3: Agent implements basic AI content disclosure and lists some applicable legal requirements, but does not automate EU AI Act Art. 50 synthetic media labeling or keep the NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.1 register of legal and regulatory requirements current
questions.l4: Synthetic media labeling is automated and the register exists, but register entries lack an owner or review date, or some outputs carry no provenance.
questions.l5: Full EU AI Act Art. 50 compliance with automated synthetic media labeling, AI-generated content watermarking, a maintained NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.1 register of the legal and regulatory requirements that apply, with an owner and review date per entry, and transparent AI content provenance for all intelligence outputs
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 50; NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.1
questions.remediation: Stamp every generated output with a provenance manifest at the generation call, and keep a legal-requirements register with an owner and review date per entry.
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations for AI-generated content including synthetic media labeling, and keep a register of the legal and regulatory requirements that apply to its intelligence systems (NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.1)?

questions.failureMode: The agent answers customers by voice and email as if it were a human because disclosure was only wired into the web widget.
questions.l1: No AI-interaction disclosure on any channel.
questions.l2: Disclosure appears on the web chat only after several turns, or only in the terms of service.
questions.l3: Disclosure at first interaction on the primary channel, but missing or untested on at least one other channel in use (e.g. voice, email, API-delivered replies).
questions.l4: Every channel discloses at first interaction with a regression test, but 'obvious from context' exceptions are not individually justified in writing.
questions.l5: Disclosure at first interaction on every channel in the channel inventory, in an accessible format, with an automated regression test per channel and a recorded rationale for each 'obvious from context' exception.
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 50(1); EU AI Act Art. 50(5)
questions.remediation: Inject the AI-interaction notice into the first-turn template of every channel in the inventory and add one regression test per channel that asserts it.
questions.text: Does the agent inform natural persons that they are interacting with an AI system, at the latest at the first interaction, unless this is obvious from the context (EU AI Act Art. 50(1), applicable from 2 August 2026)?

questions.failureMode: The agent auto-declines an applicant and the appeal loops back to the same model, so no human ever intervenes in a legally significant decision.
questions.l1: No human-intervention, point-of-view or contestation route for decisions within Art. 22.
questions.l2: Users can email support to dispute a decision, but there is no defined human intervention step for Art. 22 decisions.
questions.l3: A manual escalation route exists, but requests, submitted viewpoints and outcomes are not recorded per decision.
questions.l4: Each request is logged with reviewer, outcome and reasons, but response times are not measured against a documented target.
questions.l5: Each Art. 22 decision exposes all three safeguards; every request is logged with timestamps, the human reviewer, the outcome and reasons; response times are measured against a documented target.
questions.remediation: Attach to every Art. 22 decision an endpoint for human intervention, viewpoint and contest, logging reviewer, outcome, reasons and timestamps per request.
questions.text: For decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, does the agent implement GDPR Article 22(3) safeguards by enabling (1) human intervention, (2) user ability to express their point of view, and (3) contestation/appeal with documented outcomes, timelines, and audit trails?

questions.failureMode: The agent keeps running a hallucination-prone summarisation step after the risk was logged, because the agreed action never reached the release process.
questions.l1: No planning loop; risks are informal, actions are undocumented, and improvements are ad hoc
questions.l2: Risks are listed in a spreadsheet with no owners or due dates for the actions.
questions.l3: Maintains a basic risk register and some actions, but integration into ops processes and effectiveness evidence is incomplete
questions.l4: The register is versioned and actions are wired into change and release, but no effectiveness metric is collected when an action closes.
questions.l5: Full §6.1 planning with versioned registers, accountable action plans, operational integration, effectiveness measurement, and audit-ready evidence packs
questions.remediation: Link every open AI risk action to a change or release ticket with an owner and due date, and record an effectiveness metric when the action closes.
questions.text: Does the agent support ISO/IEC 42001:2023 §6.1 planning by maintaining an AI risk/opportunity register, defining actions with owners and due dates, integrating actions into operational processes (change/release), and tracking effectiveness metrics with evidence suitable for AIMS audit?

questions.failureMode: The agent's explanation cites a source document that was never in its context, and the trace cannot be replayed to show what it actually used.
questions.l1: No IEEE 7001 transparency process; explanations are absent or purely narrative with no traceability
questions.l2: Narrative explanations are logged, but inputs and transformations cannot be replayed to reproduce an output.
questions.l3: Provides explanations and some logs, but lacks Level-3 traceability, reproducibility, and maintained process artifacts
questions.l4: Explanations are traceable and reproducible with role views, but transparency-process templates and review records are not maintained.
questions.l5: Meets Level 3 with traceable explanation records, uncertainty disclosure, role-specific views, and complete transparency-process documentation & review evidence
questions.remediation: Persist inputs, retrieval ids, model version and seed for every output so its explanation can be replayed, and test reproducibility on a sample each release.
questions.text: Does the agent achieve IEEE 7001:2021 §6.3 Level 3 transparency by producing traceable, reproducible explanations (inputs, transformations, uncertainty), role-appropriate explanation views, and maintained transparency-process artifacts (templates, logs, review records) for each intelligence output?

questions.failureMode: The agent's output drift crosses a harmful level with no trigger threshold or named owner, so it keeps serving degraded intelligence for weeks.
questions.l1: No documented AI roles, escalation triggers, incident playbook or legal-requirements register.
questions.l2: Owners are known informally; there are no escalation thresholds for harm, drift or bias and no model-provider due diligence.
questions.l3: Roles and an incident playbook are documented, but escalation triggers lack thresholds, the legal-requirements register is missing or stale, or model providers lack due-diligence and termination criteria.
questions.l4: Thresholds, register and provider criteria exist, but the playbook has never been exercised or the register missed its annual review.
questions.l5: Legal-requirements register reviewed at least annually; RACI covering each GOVERN category; escalation triggers with measurable thresholds; playbook exercised at least once with records; due diligence, monitoring and termination criteria on file for every model provider.
questions.remediation: Define numeric escalation triggers for harm, drift and bias that page a named owner, and run one tabletop exercise of the AI incident playbook with records.
questions.text: Does the agent operationalize NIST AI RMF GOVERN by keeping a register of the legal and regulatory requirements that apply to it (GOVERN 1.1) and defining accountable roles (RACI), escalation triggers (harm, drift, bias), incident response playbooks, and third-party/model-provider governance (due diligence, monitoring, and termination criteria)?

questions.failureMode: The agent's generated audio loses its watermark when the export API re-encodes it, so downstream platforms cannot detect it as synthetic.
questions.l1: Generated outputs carry no machine-readable marking.
questions.l2: Visible labels appear on generated images only; nothing machine-readable is embedded in any modality.
questions.l3: Marking applied to some generated modalities; detection not verified by test for at least one generated modality.
questions.l4: Every modality is marked and detection is tested, but marking is stripped on an export or API path, or the Code of Practice mapping is missing.
questions.l5: Every generated modality is marked; detection is verified by test per modality; marking survives the agent's export and API paths; conformance is mapped to the Commission Code of Practice on marking and labelling AI-generated content (10 June 2026).
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 50(2); EU AI Act Art. 111(4) (as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)
questions.remediation: Embed a machine-readable mark at generation for each modality and test that a detector still finds it after export through every API and download path.
questions.text: Where the agent generates synthetic audio, image, video or text, are outputs marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated, with systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 compliant by 2 December 2026 (EU AI Act Art. 50(2); Art. 111(4) as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744)?

questions.failureMode: The agent silently starts using a new upstream model version through a floating alias, and a capability its tasks depend on regresses unreviewed.
questions.l1: Model used without the provider's integrator documentation or a pinned version.
questions.l2: The model is called through a floating alias; the provider's documentation was read once and not retained.
questions.l3: Integrator documentation stored and model version pinned, but no recorded assessment of whether the agent's fine-tuning or modification is significant.
questions.l4: Documentation is retained per pinned version with a significance assessment, but a model version change does not trigger re-review.
questions.l5: Documentation retained per pinned model version; a capability and limitation register linked to agent tasks; a written modification-significance assessment against the Commission GPAI guidelines; re-review triggered by every model version change.
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 53(1)(b); EU AI Act Annex XII
questions.remediation: Pin the model by exact version id, store the provider's Annex XII documentation beside the pin, and fail deploy when the pin changes without a re-review record.
questions.text: When the agent integrates a third-party general-purpose AI model, does its provider obtain and retain the model provider's information and documentation for integrators (EU AI Act Art. 53(1)(b), Annex XII), pin the model version, and record whether its own modifications are significant enough to make it a GPAI model provider?

questions.failureMode: The agent keeps making significant decisions about a California consumer who opted out, because the opt-out arrived by email and never reached the pipeline.
questions.l1: No inventory of ADMT used for significant decisions and no Pre-use Notice.
questions.l2: Significant-decision uses are known to the team but not inventoried; no Pre-use Notice exists.
questions.l3: Pre-use Notice published; opt-out requests handled manually without a tracked response record.
questions.l4: Inventory, Pre-use Notice and opt-out logging are in place, but some requests lack response timestamps or evidence is not dated before 1 January 2027.
questions.l5: ADMT inventory covers every significant-decision use; Pre-use Notice delivered before use; every opt-out request logged with response timestamps; evidence in place before 1 January 2027.
questions.regulatoryRef: CPPA ADMT regulations, Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11 §7200(b); CPPA ADMT regulations §7220; CPPA ADMT regulations §7221
questions.remediation: Route every ADMT opt-out into a tracked queue that records receipt and response timestamps and suppresses the agent for that consumer once honoured.
questions.text: Where the agent is used to make significant decisions about California consumers, does the business give a Pre-use Notice (§7220) and handle requests to opt out of automated decisionmaking technology as §7221 requires, with compliance in place by 1 January 2027 for uses that began earlier (Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11 §7200(b))?

questions.failureMode: The agent keeps executing a batch of flawed outputs after an overseer spots the problem, because the only way to interrupt it is a redeploy.
questions.l1: No override or interrupt control available to the people overseeing the agent.
questions.l2: Engineers can roll back the deployment, but overseers have no override control or stop procedure of their own.
questions.l3: Individual outputs can be overridden, but there is no tested interrupt ('stop') procedure, or it does not cover every deployment channel.
questions.l4: Override and stop exist on every channel and are logged, but the stop procedure is not tested each release or time to halt is not recorded.
questions.l5: Every deployment gives named overseers an override-and-reverse control and a stop procedure; the stop procedure is tested on each release with the time to halt recorded; every override and stop is logged with the overseer's identity.
questions.remediation: Give named overseers a stop control that halts the agent's queue and tool calls on every channel, and test it each release with time to halt recorded.
questions.text: For a high-risk AI system it provides, is the agent designed so that the people overseeing it can disregard, override or reverse its output and interrupt it through a 'stop' button or a similar procedure (EU AI Act Art. 14(4)(d)-(e), applicable to Annex III systems from 2 December 2027)?
