questions.remediation: Generate the agent's outbound dependency list from its tool and model configuration on each release and fail the build if a provider is missing from the DORA register.
questions.text: Is every ICT third-party service the payment agent depends on (model or API providers included) recorded in the DORA register of information and managed under the entity's ICT third-party risk policy?

questions.failureMode: The agent adds a third-party analytics tag to the checkout page during a conversion fix, opening a path for card-skimming code.
questions.l1: No payment-page script governance: scripts are loaded without authorization controls or integrity monitoring, allowing silent skimming or exfiltration
questions.l2: Scripts on payment pages are listed once, but there is no authorisation or integrity check
questions.l3: Maintains a script inventory and basic CSP, but integrity or change detection and alerting are incomplete and not audit-ready
questions.l4: Authorised scripts are allow-listed with integrity hashes and CSP, but unauthorised changes are alerted, not blocked, and evidence is not bundled
questions.l5: Full PCI 6.4.3 readiness with authorized-script allowlisting, continuous integrity monitoring (SRI/CSP/hashes), automated change approval workflows, real-time alerting or blocking for unauthorized scripts, and audit evidence bundles for assessor review
questions.remediation: Allow-list payment-page scripts with SRI hashes and CSP, and block the agent from deploying any page change that adds or modifies a script without an approval record.
questions.text: For payment pages, does the agent enforce PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 6.4.3 by maintaining an authorized script inventory, validating each script legitimacy (source/owner/purpose), implementing change detection and integrity controls (e.g., SRI/CSP/script hashing), and alerting or blocking on unauthorized or modified scripts that could capture payment data?

questions.failureMode: The agent's runaway retry loop double-charges customers for hours and the incident is treated as a bug, missing the initial notification window.
questions.l1: Agent incidents are not classified or reported on DORA time limits
questions.l2: Agent incidents are logged in the IT ticketing system, but are not classified against DORA criteria
questions.l3: Incidents are classified, but reporting clocks are tracked manually or some limits were missed without notifying the authority
questions.l4: Classification runs and reporting timers are enforced, but late-submission notices to the authority are not retained
questions.l5: Classification runs on every agent incident, 4h/24h/72h/one-month timers are enforced, and submissions and any late-submission notices are retained
questions.regulatoryRef: EU DORA Art. 18; EU DORA Art. 19; Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/301 Art. 5
questions.remediation: Classify every agent incident against DORA criteria at creation and start the 4h, 24h, 72h and one-month timers automatically when it is classified as major.
questions.text: Are ICT incidents involving the agent classified under DORA criteria and, when major, reported within the RTS time limits: initial notification within 4 hours of classification and no later than 24 hours after awareness, intermediate report within 72 hours of the initial notification, final report within one month?

questions.failureMode: The agent reuses one authentication result to execute a second payment with a higher amount in the same session.
questions.l1: No dynamic linking: MFA may be used but authentication is not bound to amount or payee and transaction details can be manipulated
questions.l2: Multi-factor authentication is used, but the authentication result is not linked to transaction details
questions.l3: Binds authentication to some transaction details and displays amount and payee, but integrity protections and manipulation detection are incomplete across channels
questions.l4: Authentication is cryptographically bound to amount and payee in both channels, but tamper detection and binding audit logs are incomplete
questions.l5: Full RTS dynamic linking with cryptographic binding to amount and payee, secure display and confirmation, channel-consistent enforcement (web/app), tamper detection, and audit logs demonstrating binding and user confirmation
questions.regulatoryRef: EBA RTS on SCA (EU) 2018/389 Art. 4 (dynamic linking)
questions.remediation: Sign the amount and payee into the authentication challenge, verify the signature at execution, and log a tamper event whenever the executed values differ.
questions.text: Does the agent implement SCA RTS dynamic linking by cryptographically binding authentication to the specific transaction amount and payee (and ensuring integrity-protected display or confirmation of those elements to the payer), and by preventing post-authentication manipulation of amount or payee in both browser and app flows?

questions.failureMode: The agent authorises a supplier payment after a no-match verification result because it treats the result as a soft warning.
questions.l1: Transfers are authorised without verification of payee
questions.l2: Verification of payee runs for some transfers, but its result is not shown to the payer
questions.l3: Verification of payee runs, but the agent can proceed after a mismatch without an explicit payer decision
questions.l4: Close-match and no-match force a payer decision, but not-possible outcomes and their handling are not tested
questions.l5: Every transfer records the verification result before authorisation, close-match and no-match force an explicit payer decision, and tests cover match, close-match, no-match and not-possible outcomes
questions.remediation: Call verification of payee before every euro credit transfer, show close-match and no-match to the payer, and make the agent's authorise tool refuse after a mismatch without an explicit payer decision.
questions.text: For credit transfers in euro that the agent prepares or initiates, is verification of payee obtained before the payer authorises, is any close match or mismatch shown to the payer, and does the agent refuse to authorise on the payer's behalf after a mismatch?

questions.failureMode: The agent routes a stablecoin transfer to an exchange without beneficiary details because its validation applies only to fiat rails.
questions.l1: Transfers are sent without complete originator or beneficiary information
questions.l2: Originator and beneficiary fields exist for fiat transfers only, and are often empty
questions.l3: Required fields are populated for fiat transfers, but crypto-asset transfers and missing-information handling are inconsistent
questions.l4: Information is validated for fiat and crypto-asset transfers, but incomplete transfers are handled case by case without a documented policy
questions.l5: Originator and beneficiary information is validated for every fiat and crypto-asset transfer, incomplete transfers are held or rejected under a documented policy, and the evidence is retained for supervisory review
questions.remediation: Apply the same originator and beneficiary validation to crypto-asset transfers as to fiat, and hold or reject incomplete transfers under a documented policy with the decision retained.
questions.text: For transfers of funds and crypto-assets, does the agent ensure the required originator and beneficiary information accompanies each transfer under Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 and the FATF R.16 payment-transparency standard revised in June 2025?

questions.failureMode: The agent keeps queueing payments during a fraud-service outage and releases them unscored when the queue drains.
questions.l1: The agent is outside the resilience testing programme
questions.l2: Agent hosts are in the vulnerability scan list, but the agent's model and API dependencies are not
questions.l3: The agent is included in annual vulnerability scans, but scenario-based tests and remediation tracking are missing
questions.l4: A risk-based test plan covers the agent and its dependencies with scenario tests, but testers are not independent or findings are not tracked to closure
questions.l5: Risk-based test plan covering the agent and its dependencies (vulnerability assessments, scenario and performance tests, source code review where relevant), independent testers, and findings tracked to closure
questions.remediation: Add scenario tests where the agent's model provider, payment API or fraud service is slow or down, and track each finding to closure with an owner and date.
questions.text: Are the agent and the ICT systems it relies on covered by the digital operational resilience testing programme required by DORA (EU) 2022/2554 Articles 24 and 25, including vulnerability assessments, scenario-based tests and tracked remediation of findings?

questions.failureMode: The agent's creditworthiness model is retrained on a new market segment while the impact assessment still describes the old one.
questions.l1: No fundamental rights impact assessment
questions.l2: A risk memo on credit scoring exists, but it is not a fundamental rights impact assessment
questions.l3: An assessment exists, but it is not tied to the deployed version or not updated on change
questions.l4: The assessment is versioned with the deployed system, but it is not updated when the model or affected groups change
questions.l5: The assessment is versioned with the deployed system, covers the processes, affected groups, risks, human-oversight and mitigation measures, and is updated on every material change
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 27; EU AI Act Annex III §5(b)
questions.remediation: Block deployment of a creditworthiness model version unless a fundamental rights impact assessment tied to that version is on file, and reopen it on every material change.
questions.text: Before deploying an AI system that evaluates the creditworthiness or credit score of natural persons, has the deployer completed a fundamental rights impact assessment under AI Act Art. 27(1), tied to the deployed version?

questions.failureMode: The agent sends a remittance on a user's chat instruction without showing the exchange rate and amount to be received before payment.
questions.l1: Remittance transfers can be paid for without a pre-payment disclosure
questions.l2: Fees are disclosed for remittances, but the exchange rate and amount to be received are not shown before payment
questions.l3: A disclosure is shown, but it omits applicable elements (such as the exchange rate or covered third-party fees) or is shown after payment in some channels
questions.l4: A full disclosure is shown before payment in user-initiated flows, but agent-initiated transfers skip it or the disclosure shown is not retained
questions.l5: Payment is blocked until a pre-payment disclosure with every applicable §1005.31(b)(1) element is shown, for agent-initiated and user-initiated transfers alike, and the disclosure shown is retained with the transfer
questions.remediation: Make the remittance tool refuse payment until a pre-payment disclosure with every applicable element is shown to the sender, for agent-initiated transfers too, and store it with the transfer.
questions.text: For remittance transfers the agent initiates or prepares, is the sender given the pre-payment disclosure of 12 CFR 1005.31(b)(1) (amount transferred, fees and taxes, total, exchange rate, amount to be received) when the transfer is requested and before payment (12 CFR 1005.31(e)(1))?

regulatoryReferences.citation: ISO 20022 Financial services — Universal financial industry message scheme
Bank Secrecy Act regulations (31 CFR Chapter X)
Dodd-Frank Act Title X (Consumer Financial Protection Act of 2010)

sdgAlignment: SDG 8 — Decent Work and Economic Growth

drug-discovery.certificationPath: L1 Basic research data management → L2 FAIR data compliance with CDISC standards → L3 Full GMP/GLP compliant AI-assisted discovery → L4 ICH Q8-Q12 quality-by-design integration → L5 Autonomous drug discovery governance with verified reproducibility and regulatory submission readiness
drug-discovery.description: Biological research, molecules, drug and therapy production — covering the drug discovery pipeline from target identification through lead optimization, preclinical development, and manufacturing with emphasis on data integrity, reproducibility, and regulatory compliance.
drug-discovery.euAIActClassification: Out of scope under Art. 2(6) when developed and put into service solely for scientific research and development; otherwise Art. 6(1) and Annex I (Regulation (EU) 2017/745 MDR, 2017/746 IVDR) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a medical device
keyRisks: AI-generated molecular candidates with hidden toxicity profiles
Data integrity failures in AI-managed laboratory information systems
Irreproducible AI-discovered drug targets due to training data bias
GMP violations from AI-optimized manufacturing process changes
Intellectual property disputes over AI-generated molecular structures
drug-discovery.name: Drug Discovery

questions.failureMode: The agent writes CMC results into a LIMS through an unvalidated connector on a shared account, so the records are neither attributable nor input-checked.
questions.l1: Systems the agent writes to are unvalidated; data integrity relies on informal checks
questions.l2: Some lab systems have validation documents, but systems the agent writes to have no access or change control
questions.l3: Key systems are validated, but the agent integration is outside validation scope, or back-up restore is not tested
questions.l4: Validation covers the agent integration and restore is tested, but periodic review is overdue or attributable-record sampling is not done
questions.l5: Validation covers the agent integration; access and change control are evidenced; back-up restore is tested (Annex 11 §7.2); periodic review records exist; attributable, contemporaneous records are sampled at review
questions.remediation: Bring the agent's write path into each GMP system's validated scope: a dedicated agent account, input checks on every write and change control on its connector.
questions.text: Are the computerised systems the agent uses for GMP-relevant discovery or CMC data validated and controlled per FDA 21 CFR §211.68 and EU GMP Annex 11 §4 and §7 (documented validation, input/output checks, access control, change control, back-up and restore checks, periodic review)?

questions.failureMode: The agent recommends a granulation parameter outside the approved design space as an optimisation, and operators apply it as a routine adjustment.
questions.l1: No QbD integration; drug development processes are not designed with systematic quality risk management
questions.l2: Operating ranges are recorded, but no design space or QRM record covers AI-proposed parameters
questions.l3: Agent supports design space exploration and basic risk assessment per ICH Q9, but does not implement full QbD lifecycle including control strategy development
questions.l4: Design-space boundaries with evidence and QRM records exist, but out-of-boundary agent proposals are flagged rather than blocked
questions.l5: Design-space boundaries and their evidence are documented; agent-proposed parameters outside the boundary are blocked pending change control; QRM records cover each AI-influenced parameter
questions.remediation: Check every agent-proposed process parameter against the documented design-space boundaries and block values outside them until change control approves.
questions.text: Does the agent operate within a design space defined per ICH Q8(R2) (explicit boundaries, supporting evidence, rules for changes inside versus outside the design space) with quality risk management per ICH Q9(R1)?

questions.failureMode: The agent trains a target-ranking model on an assay dataset with no provenance or protocol metadata, so its target hits cannot be reproduced by another lab.
questions.l1: No FAIR compliance; research data is siloed, poorly documented, and not interoperable across systems
questions.l2: Datasets sit in shared folders with file-name conventions only, no identifiers or metadata
questions.l3: Agent assigns persistent identifiers and basic metadata to datasets, but interoperability and reusability are limited by proprietary formats and incomplete documentation
questions.l4: Persistent identifiers, rich metadata, machine-readable formats and provenance exist, but licence terms or automated FAIR assessment are missing
questions.l5: Full FAIR implementation with persistent identifiers (DOI), rich metadata per CDISC standards, machine-readable data formats, provenance documentation, license specification, community standard compliance, and automated FAIR maturity assessment
questions.regulatoryRef: FAIR Guiding Principles (Wilkinson et al. 2016); CDISC Foundational Standards
questions.remediation: Require a persistent identifier, assay protocol and provenance record for every dataset the agent trains on or retrieves, and reject datasets missing them.
questions.text: Does the agent maintain FAIR data principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) per FAIR Guiding Principles and CDISC data standards for research datasets?

questions.failureMode: The agent ranks a generated molecule highly without mutagenicity screening, or trusts a QSAR call outside its applicability domain, hiding a toxic structural alert.
questions.l1: No computational toxicology; molecular candidates are not screened for mutagenic or toxic potential using in silico methods
questions.l2: In silico toxicity is run ad hoc on some compounds with an unrecorded tool and version
questions.l3: Agent performs basic QSAR toxicity predictions for lead compounds, but does not implement full ICH M7 assessment workflow or validate predictions against experimental data
questions.l4: The M7 workflow, ADMET and structural-alert screening run on every candidate, but confidence is not calibrated against experimental results
questions.l5: Comprehensive computational toxicology with multi-model QSAR screening, ICH M7(R2) compliant mutagenicity assessment, ADMET prediction, off-target activity profiling, structural alert identification, and prediction confidence calibration with experimental validation tracking
questions.regulatoryRef: ICH M7(R2); FDA QSAR Guidance for Mutagenic Impurities
questions.remediation: Run every agent-generated candidate through the M7 in silico workflow before ranking, and send predictions outside a model's applicability domain to expert review.
questions.text: Does the agent implement computational toxicology screening per ICH M7(R2) assessment of mutagenic impurities and FDA QSAR guidance?

questions.failureMode: The agent's generated structure is filed with no record of which person conceived and modified it, leaving inventorship open to challenge.
questions.l1: No IP management; AI-assisted discoveries are not systematically documented for patent protection or inventorship determination
questions.l2: Contributions are mentioned in meeting notes, but agent prompts and outputs are not retained
questions.l3: Agent logs AI contributions to discovery processes and maintains invention disclosure records, but does not implement systematic inventorship analysis or freedom-to-operate assessment
questions.l4: AI and human contributions are logged per invention disclosure with inventorship analysis, but freedom-to-operate and prior-art checks are not linked
questions.l5: Full IP governance with automated invention disclosure capture, AI contribution documentation per USPTO guidance, freedom-to-operate analysis, prior art monitoring, patent landscape mapping, and inventorship determination support for AI-assisted discoveries
questions.regulatoryRef: USPTO Revised Inventorship Guidance for AI-Assisted Inventions (90 FR 54636, 2025)
questions.remediation: Retain each prompt, agent output and the human edits that followed, linked to the invention disclosure, so the human contribution can be shown per claim.
questions.text: Does the agent document AI contributions to discoveries so that inventorship of AI-assisted inventions can be determined per the USPTO Revised Inventorship Guidance for AI-Assisted Inventions (2025)?

questions.failureMode: The agent adjusts a manufacturing parameter mid-batch and the batch record shows the new value with no change control or approver.
questions.l1: No GMP automation; manufacturing procedures and batch records are managed manually without AI-assisted process optimization controls
questions.l2: Batch records are kept, but AI-suggested parameter changes are applied without a written procedure
questions.l3: Agent generates batch production records and tracks process parameters, but AI-recommended process changes are not validated through formal change control per §211.100
questions.l4: AI-recommended changes pass formal change control within the validated design space, but deviation and CAPA linkage is incomplete
questions.l5: Full GMP compliance with automated batch record generation per §211.188, AI process optimization within validated design space, formal change control for AI-recommended modifications, deviation management, and CAPA tracking per §211.192
questions.remediation: Write an AI-recommended parameter into the batch record only after approved change control, recording recommendation, approver and procedure version.
questions.text: Does the agent enforce GMP manufacturing controls per FDA 21 CFR §211.100 written procedures and §211.188 batch production records for AI-optimized processes?

questions.failureMode: The agent writes a specification value into Module 3 that it paraphrased or hallucinated rather than extracted from the source record.
questions.l1: No CTD preparation support; quality documentation for regulatory submissions is compiled manually
questions.l2: Module 3 sections are drafted by hand from exported spreadsheets, with no cross-reference checks
questions.l3: Agent assists with CTD Module 3 document compilation and cross-references, but does not automate data extraction from laboratory systems or validate completeness against ICH requirements
questions.l4: Extraction from LIMS and ELN, cross-reference validation and completeness checks run, but human sign-off before submission is not recorded
questions.l5: CTD Module 3 compilation with automated extraction from LIMS/ELN, cross-reference validation, completeness checks against ICH M4Q, eCTD formatting, and human sign-off recorded before submission
questions.remediation: Link every value the agent places in Module 3 to its LIMS or ELN source record and block compilation when a value has no source or differs from it.
questions.text: Does the agent support regulatory submission preparation per ICH M4 Common Technical Document (CTD) Module 3 quality documentation?

questions.failureMode: The agent nominates targets that mirror the over-studied genes and ancestries in its training corpus, so hits fail to replicate in broader populations.
questions.l1: No responsible AI practices; drug discovery AI may perpetuate biases in target selection or compound optimization
questions.l2: Model training data is described informally, with no bias check
questions.l3: Agent documents AI model training data and performs basic bias checks, but does not implement systematic fairness assessment or diverse population representation in molecular modeling
questions.l4: Data diversity, bias testing across therapeutic areas and interpretability documentation exist, but population pharmacogenomics is not reported
questions.l5: Comprehensive responsible AI with training data diversity assessment, algorithmic bias testing across therapeutic areas, model interpretability documentation, diverse population pharmacogenomic consideration, and transparent AI methodology reporting per OECD principles
questions.remediation: Test target-identification models for skew toward well-studied targets and populations, report it with each nomination and require review of skewed ones.
questions.text: Does the agent implement responsible AI practices for drug discovery per OECD AI Principles and prevent algorithmic bias in target identification and lead optimization?

questions.failureMode: The agent edits an ELN experiment entry after it was witnessed, and the prior result is overwritten without a visible audit trail.
questions.l1: No ELN integrity controls; laboratory records lack electronic signature, audit trail, or tamper-evidence requirements
questions.l2: ELN entries are user-attributed, but edits overwrite prior content without an audit trail
questions.l3: Agent implements basic ELN with audit trails and access controls, but does not enforce Part 11 compliant electronic signatures or implement full Annex 11 §9 audit trail review processes
questions.l4: Part 11 signatures and Annex 11 audit trails are enforced, but audit trail review is manual and periodic integrity checks are not scheduled
questions.l5: Full ELN integrity with Part 11 electronic signatures, Annex 11 §9 compliant audit trails, tamper-evident recording, automated audit trail review, data backup per Annex 11 §7.2, and periodic integrity verification
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; EU GMP Annex 11 §9
questions.remediation: Mark every ELN entry the agent drafts as agent-authored, require a scientist's e-signature to finalise it, and include agent entries in audit trail review.
questions.text: Does the agent maintain electronic laboratory notebook (ELN) integrity per FDA 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GMP Annex 11 §9 audit trail requirements?

questions.failureMode: The agent summarises preclinical toxicity findings from processed data, drops an adverse histopathology finding, and the raw data to catch it is gone.
questions.l1: No GLP compliance; preclinical study data is not managed per good laboratory practice requirements
questions.l2: Study protocols are stored, but raw data the agent processes is not retained in original form
questions.l3: Agent tracks study protocols and raw data per GLP requirements, but does not automate study director oversight, QA auditing, or archive management
questions.l4: Raw data integrity, QA audit tracking and specimen accountability are in place, but archive management and reports are not linked to the study
questions.l5: Full GLP compliance with automated study protocol management, raw data integrity assurance, QA audit scheduling and tracking, specimen/sample accountability, archive management per §58.190, and study report generation per §58.185
questions.regulatoryRef: OECD GLP Principles §8; FDA 21 CFR Part 58
questions.remediation: Keep the raw instrument data behind every agent-processed preclinical result and require study director approval of agent analysis steps.
questions.text: Does the agent implement preclinical study data management per OECD GLP Principles §8 and FDA 21 CFR Part 58 good laboratory practice?

questions.failureMode: The agent sets a batch status to released based on its own trend analysis, bypassing the Qualified Person decision.
questions.l1: AI output feeds batch certification with no QRM record or validation
questions.l2: Some AI-influenced quality decisions have a risk assessment, but formality is not matched to risk and batch-release use is unrestricted
questions.l3: QRM records exist for AI-influenced decisions, but batch-release use is not technically restricted
questions.l4: Batch release is technically restricted to a Qualified Person action, but the restriction is untested or QRM formality is not risk-matched everywhere
questions.l5: Each AI-influenced quality decision has a QRM record with formality matched to risk; batch certification requires a Qualified Person action in a validated system; the restriction is tested
questions.remediation: Technically prevent the agent from setting batch status to released; only a Qualified Person action in the validated system can, tested each release.
questions.text: Does the agent apply ICH Q9(R1) formality-of-risk-management to AI-influenced quality decisions and stay out of batch certification unless the computerised system is validated per EU GMP Annex 11 §15?

questions.failureMode: The agent's CMC trend model is retrained and redeployed outside PQS change management, and management review never sees the resulting deviation spike.
questions.l1: No PQS; quality governance is ad-hoc, roles are unclear, CAPA or change management are inconsistent or absent
questions.l2: Quality roles exist on paper, but AI-driven changes are not handled by CAPA or change management
questions.l3: Partial PQS with documented roles and some CAPA or change control, but monitoring, management review, and lifecycle governance of AI-driven changes are incomplete
questions.l4: Governance, KPIs, CAPA effectiveness checks and change management for AI exist, but management review does not cover AI performance on a cadence
questions.l5: Full ICH Q10 §3.2 PQS with governance, KPIs, CAPA effectiveness checks, formal change management (including AI model or process changes), management review cadence, and audit-ready evidence linkage across discovery, development, and manufacturing
questions.remediation: Add AI model and prompt changes to the PQS change management procedure and report agent-related deviations and CAPAs at each management review.
questions.text: Does the agent implement a Pharmaceutical Quality System (PQS) aligned to ICH Q10 §3.2, including defined management responsibilities, process performance or product quality monitoring, CAPA, change management, and management review for AI-assisted discovery and AI-influenced CMC or manufacturing activities?

questions.failureMode: The agent implements a process change that alters an Established Condition as a routine internal change, so no regulatory filing is made.
questions.l1: No post-approval change governance; ECs or PACMP are not defined and AI-driven changes are uncontrolled
questions.l2: Post-approval changes are tracked, but Established Conditions are not identified
questions.l3: Tracks changes and drafts regulatory justifications, but ECs or PACMP scope and reporting categories are inconsistently applied and not audit-ready
questions.l4: ECs, PACMP workflows and regional categorisation exist, but impact assessments are not tied to QRM or evidence bundles are built by hand
questions.l5: Full Q12 §3.2 lifecycle management with EC identification, PACMP workflows, change categorization by region, impact assessment tied to QRM, and submission or notification-ready evidence bundles
questions.remediation: Check each agent-proposed process or model change against the Established Conditions register and route EC-affecting changes to regulatory assessment.
questions.text: Does the agent support ICH Q12 §3.2 post-approval change management by defining and controlling Established Conditions (ECs), managing PACMP or predefined change protocols, and maintaining a lifecycle management plan for AI-driven process or model changes that affect CQAs or CPPs?

questions.failureMode: The agent transcribes a potency value from an instrument printout into LIMS with a misplaced decimal, and no second check catches it before release testing.
questions.l1: No §7.1 controls; critical data can be entered or edited without effective verification or falsification controls
questions.l2: Critical data fields are identified, but entries have no second check and raw data is not linked to reported results
questions.l3: Implements some access controls and audit trails, but critical data verification, raw-data linkage, and falsification detection are inconsistent
questions.l4: Second-person or validated electronic checks and raw-data linkage are enforced, but anomaly detection and periodic review are not in place
questions.l5: Comprehensive §7.1 controls with enforced workflows for critical data entry, verification rules, raw-data provenance linkage, anomaly detection, periodic review, and inspection-ready evidence outputs
questions.remediation: Treat the agent as a data entry source: require a second-person or validated electronic check on each critical value it transcribes, storing the raw-data link.
questions.text: Does the agent apply EU GMP Annex 11 §6 accuracy checks to critical data (additional check by a second operator or validated electronic means for manually entered critical data) and §7.1 data storage protection, with raw data linked to reported results across ELN, LIMS or instrument integrations?

questions.failureMode: The agent calls a newly added instrument export API that was never validated and ingests truncated chromatography results into the batch dataset.
questions.l1: No CSV or controls; lab computerized systems are unvalidated and rely on informal checks
questions.l2: One or two flagship systems are validated; the ELN, LIMS and instrument interfaces the agent uses are not inventoried
questions.l3: Validates key systems and performs some checks or backups, but validation scope, change control, and periodic review are incomplete or inconsistently evidenced
questions.l4: Risk-based validation, documented checks and backup verification cover every lab system the agent uses, but configuration is not monitored
questions.l5: Full §211.68-aligned CSV with risk-based validation, documented checks, controlled configuration, backup or restore verification, and continuous monitoring with audit-ready validation packages
questions.remediation: Inventory every ELN, LIMS and instrument interface the agent calls with a validation risk level, and refuse tool calls to interfaces not in the inventory.
questions.text: Does the agent ensure computerized systems used in discovery or CMC labs are validated and controlled per FDA 21 CFR §211.68 (including documented validation, input or output checks, access controls, change control, backup or restore testing, and periodic review) for ELN, LIMS, or instrument integrations?

questions.failureMode: The agent extrapolates its process model beyond the region covered by development experiments and presents the result as inside the design space.
questions.l1: No design space; operating ranges and boundaries are informal and not supported by evidence
questions.l2: Single-factor operating ranges exist from development batches, with no multivariate study or linkage to CQAs
questions.l3: Defines operating ranges and explores multivariate effects, but boundaries, evidence linkage, and within or outside design-space change rules are not consistently enforced
questions.l4: Evidence-backed boundaries linked to CQAs and CPPs with change workflows exist, but alignment to Q9 QRM and the Q10 control strategy is not shown
questions.l5: Full §2.2 design space governance with evidence-backed boundaries, linkage to CQAs or CPPs, within or outside design-space change workflows, and alignment to Q9 QRM and Q10 control strategy
questions.remediation: Require the agent to cite the multivariate study behind each design-space boundary it uses, and refuse to extrapolate beyond the experimentally covered region.
questions.text: Does the agent define, justify, and govern a design space per ICH Q8(R2) §2.2 (including explicit boundaries, supporting evidence, and change handling within vs outside design space) for AI-assisted development and AI-influenced process optimization?

questions.failureMode: The agent, an LLM, drafts a deviation closure that flows into a critical GMP decision with no qualified person reviewing its output.
questions.l1: LLM outputs feed batch release or other critical GMP decisions without human review
questions.l2: LLM use in GMP work is discouraged informally, with no inventory of uses
questions.l3: LLMs are restricted by policy, but there is no criticality classification or technical enforcement
questions.l4: Each use is classified and model-type restrictions are technically enforced, but restriction tests or qualified personnel review records are incomplete
questions.l5: Each GMP AI use is classified critical or non-critical; model-type restrictions are technically enforced and tested; human review by qualified personnel is recorded for non-critical LLM use; draft status is tracked
questions.regulatoryRef: EudraLex Vol. 4 draft Annex 22 §1; EU GMP Annex 11
questions.remediation: Classify every GMP AI use as critical or non-critical and technically block LLM tools from writing to critical GMP records, testing the block each release.
questions.text: Are generative-AI and LLM agents kept out of critical GMP applications, with only static, deterministic validated models used there and qualified, trained personnel responsible where LLMs support non-critical GMP tasks, as proposed in draft EU GMP Annex 22 §1?

questions.failureMode: The agent's safety or efficacy prediction enters a regulatory package with no defined context of use, so a model trained on biased data drives an untested decision.
questions.l1: No defined context of use; AI outputs enter submissions unassessed
questions.l2: AI use is noted in submission drafts, with no context of use written
questions.l3: Context of use is documented, but credibility evidence is not scaled to model risk
questions.l4: Context of use, model-risk rationale and credibility assessment exist, but lifecycle maintenance records are missing
questions.l5: Each AI use has a context of use, model-risk rationale, credibility assessment plan and results, and lifecycle maintenance records; draft status is tracked
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA draft guidance: Considerations for the Use of AI To Support Regulatory Decision-Making for Drug and Biological Products (January 2025)
questions.remediation: Write a context of use and model-risk rating for each AI output used in regulatory decisions, and scale the validation set and acceptance criteria to it.
questions.text: When AI output supports regulatory decisions on drug safety, effectiveness or quality, does the sponsor define the context of use and assess model credibility in proportion to model risk, as in FDA's draft guidance on AI to support regulatory decision-making (January 2025)?

regulatoryReferences.citation: FDA Current Good Manufacturing Practice for Finished Pharmaceuticals (21 CFR Parts 210 and 211)
ISO 17511:2020 In vitro diagnostic medical devices — metrological traceability
FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data

farm-to-fork.certificationPath: L1 Basic food safety awareness → L2 HACCP-aligned digital controls → L3 ISO 22000 certified traceability → L4 Full supply chain transparency with EUDR compliance → L5 Autonomous farm-to-fork governance with cryptographic provenance chains
farm-to-fork.description: Sustainable farming, food nutrition, and responsible consumption — covering the entire agri-food value chain from primary production through processing, distribution, and consumption with emphasis on food safety, traceability, and environmental sustainability.
farm-to-fork.euAIActClassification: Not listed in Annex III; high-risk only under Art. 6(1) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a product covered by Annex I legislation — otherwise Art. 4 (AI literacy), Art. 5 (prohibited practices) and Art. 50 (transparency) apply (Annex III §2 covers critical digital infrastructure, road traffic and water, gas, heating or electricity supply, not food systems)
keyRisks: Food fraud and adulteration in AI-managed supply chains
Pesticide residue misclassification by automated monitoring
Deforestation-linked sourcing undetected by traceability agents
Allergen cross-contamination from automated production scheduling
Loss of smallholder farmer livelihoods through algorithmic procurement bias
farm-to-fork.name: Farm to Fork

questions.failureMode: The agent logs an out-of-limit pasteurisation or chilling reading as a sensor glitch and lets the batch proceed with no corrective action.
questions.l1: No CCP monitoring linked to the HACCP plan; deviations are not recorded by the agent
questions.l2: CCP readings are captured by the agent but compared with critical limits only in periodic manual reviews; deviations are logged inconsistently
questions.l3: CCP readings are checked against the plan's critical limits and deviations are logged with alerts, but corrective-action records are missing or not linked to the deviation record
questions.l4: Every deviation links to its corrective action and human sign-off, but verification results are added late or retention retrieval is untested
questions.l5: Every CCP deviation record carries timestamp, measured value, critical limit, responsible person, corrective action taken, human sign-off and verification result; records for the retention period are retrievable on request and sampled at internal audit
questions.remediation: Bind each CCP sensor feed to the plan's critical limit table and make the agent open a corrective action that closes only with named sign-off.
questions.text: Does the agent monitor each critical control point against the critical limits in the HACCP plan, log every deviation, and route each corrective action to designated personnel for sign-off per Codex CXC 1-1969 (Rev. 2020) HACCP Principles 4-7?

questions.failureMode: The agent fills a genealogy gap with a supplier inferred from purchase history, so a recall trace names the wrong farm and misses the adulterated source.
questions.l1: No digital traceability; paper-based records with gaps in supply chain visibility beyond immediate supplier
questions.l2: Digital records cover immediate suppliers and customers for most lots, but transformation steps are rebuilt from paper on request
questions.l3: Batch-level traceability across major supply chain nodes with digital records, but gaps exist in sub-supplier and smallholder farm-level data
questions.l4: Lot genealogy links farm origin, transformations and logistics to point of sale, but smallholder aggregation stays batch-level and recalls take hours
questions.l5: Item-level cryptographic traceability from seed/feed origin through every transformation and logistics step to point of sale, with immutable audit trail and sub-second recall capability
questions.remediation: Write a genealogy edge for every receipt, transformation and shipment keyed by lot ID, and fail a quarterly timed mock recall on any untraced lot.
questions.text: Can the agent provide end-to-end supply chain traceability from farm origin to consumer per EU General Food Law Regulation (EC) 178/2002 Article 18?

questions.failureMode: The agent accepts plot coordinates copied from another lot and clears cocoa or soy grown on a recently cleared plot for export.
questions.l1: Sourcing decisions are made without plot geolocation or a deforestation/legality check
questions.l2: Geolocation is requested from suppliers but not checked; the agent records supplier self-declarations of deforestation-free status
questions.l3: Plot geolocation is collected and checked against a deforestation dataset for some suppliers or commodities; uncovered lots are listed
questions.l4: Every lot has plot geolocation and a dated dataset check, but legality evidence is incomplete for some origins and failing lots are flagged, not blocked
questions.l5: Every relevant-product lot is linked to plot geolocation, a dated deforestation check (dataset and version recorded) and legality evidence; lots without a passing check are blocked from placing or export
questions.regulatoryRef: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 Art. 3, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2650
questions.remediation: Add a pre-placing gate that holds a relevant-product lot until its plots pass a deforestation check (dataset and version logged) with legality evidence.
questions.text: Before a relevant product is placed on or exported from the EU market, does the agent verify it is deforestation-free and legally produced using plot-level geolocation, per Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 Art. 3 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2650 (applying from 30 Dec 2026 for large and medium operators and 30 Jun 2027 for micro and small)?

questions.failureMode: The agent approves a plant-protection product for an organic field because its trade name resembles an authorised substance, contaminating the organic lot.
questions.l1: No organic compliance tracking; certification status managed manually with risk of non-compliant input usage
questions.l2: Organic status of inputs is recorded from supplier claims; the agent does not check substances against the authorised lists
questions.l3: Agent tracks organic certification status and flags non-compliant inputs, but does not proactively manage the full certification lifecycle or audit readiness
questions.l4: Inputs are checked against the authorised-substance lists and blocked when absent, but results are not linked to every lot or exportable
questions.l5: Each input substance is checked against the authorised-substance lists applicable under Regulation (EU) 2018/848 before use, the result is linked to the lot, non-authorised inputs are blocked, and a control-body evidence export exists
questions.remediation: Check each fertiliser, plant-protection product and processing aid against the versioned authorised list before approval and link the result to the lot.
questions.text: Does the agent manage organic certification compliance per EU Organic Regulation 2018/848 Articles 9-12 including input substance verification?

questions.failureMode: The agent reorders production to cut changeovers and schedules an allergen-free product straight after a peanut run on the same line with no validated clean.
questions.l1: No automated allergen tracking; allergen declarations managed manually with high cross-contamination risk in production scheduling
questions.l2: Allergen data per recipe exists, but label checks against the 14 Annex II categories are manual and line sequencing ignores allergens
questions.l3: Agent maintains allergen databases and validates labeling against Annex II 14 allergen categories, but cross-contamination risk from production sequencing is not algorithmically managed
questions.l4: Sequencing applies allergen order and changeover-clean rules and labels are verified at print, but precautionary-label risk assessments are not recorded
questions.l5: Full allergen lifecycle management with production line sequencing optimization to minimize cross-contamination, real-time label verification, precautionary allergen labeling risk assessment, and consumer-facing allergen transparency APIs
questions.remediation: Add allergen constraints to the scheduling tool so an Annex II allergen run cannot precede an allergen-free run without a verified changeover clean.
questions.text: Does the agent implement allergen management controls per EU Food Information Regulation (EU) 1169/2011 Article 21 and Annex II?

questions.failureMode: The agent publishes a nutrition table from a superseded recipe after a sugar or salt reformulation, so the label misstates the product.
questions.l1: Nutrition declarations are static and not recalculated when formulation or sourcing changes
questions.l2: Declarations are produced from a nutrient database but reference outdated recipe versions; formulation changes go undetected
questions.l3: The declaration is generated from recipe data and checked for the mandatory nutrients, but recalculation after formulation changes is manual
questions.l4: Formulation changes regenerate and check the declaration, but supplier-specification changes do not and front-of-pack outputs are computed separately
questions.l5: Every formulation or supplier change triggers regeneration and check of the declaration with version history; any front-of-pack scheme output is computed from the same data with the scheme rule version recorded
questions.remediation: Subscribe the declaration generator to recipe and supplier-spec change events so each change regenerates the declaration and front-of-pack output from one source.
questions.text: Does the agent generate and validate the mandatory nutrition declaration from current recipe data per Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 Art. 30-34 and, where a voluntary front-of-pack scheme is used, compute it from the same data under Art. 35, recalculating both on every formulation change?

questions.failureMode: The agent cancels a perishable produce order days before delivery to chase a cheaper spot price, leaving a smallholder with an unsold harvest.
questions.l1: Procurement automation can issue late payments, short-notice cancellations or unilateral changes with no check
questions.l2: Payment-term limits sit in the ERP, but the agent can issue short-notice cancellations and contract changes with no check
questions.l3: Payment-term and cancellation rules are enforced for some flows; exceptions are handled manually without a record
questions.l4: Orders, payment runs and changes are checked and blocks are logged with approver, but the rule list is not versioned to the national transposition
questions.l5: Every automated order, payment run and change is checked against the prohibited-practice list before issue; blocked actions and overrides are logged with approver and reason; the check list is versioned against the national transposition
questions.remediation: Block payment dates past 30 or 60 days by product type, short-notice perishable cancellations and unilateral changes before issue; log each override.
questions.text: Does the agent prevent the unfair trading practices prohibited by Directive (EU) 2019/633 (payment later than 30 days for perishable and 60 days for other agri-food products, short-notice cancellation of perishables, unilateral contract changes) in automated procurement?

questions.failureMode: The agent overwrites a controlled food safety procedure with a regenerated draft and no version history, so the audited record differs from what operators used.
questions.l1: No systematic documentation; food safety records are fragmented across systems with no automated evidence collection
questions.l2: Records sit in a shared repository with templates but no version control; evidence is gathered by hand before audits
questions.l3: Agent generates and stores food safety documentation with structured templates, but evidence collection requires manual triggers and cross-referencing
questions.l4: Documented information is version-controlled and monitoring records flow in, but completeness checks are not run and the audit export is manual
questions.l5: All documented information required by ISO 22000:2018 Clause 7.5 is created, version-controlled and retrievable; monitoring records and verification results are collected from integrated systems with completeness checks and an audit-ready export
questions.remediation: Run a daily completeness check of expected versus received monitoring and verification records per process step and open a gap ticket for each miss.
questions.text: Does the agent maintain food safety management system documentation per ISO 22000:2018 Clause 7.5 with automated evidence collection?

questions.failureMode: The agent marks a supply-chain preventive control as verified from a supplier letter alone, leaving the US food safety plan without a verification record.
questions.l1: No food safety plan records are produced or maintained by the agent
questions.l2: A food safety plan document exists, but hazard analysis and preventive controls are not held in structured form by the agent
questions.l3: Food safety plan, hazard analysis (§117.130) and preventive controls (§117.135) are recorded, but monitoring (§117.145), corrective-action (§117.150) or verification records are incomplete
questions.l4: Monitoring, corrective-action and verification records link per preventive control, but validation is incomplete or reanalysis is not triggered on change
questions.l5: Records for §117.126-§117.190 are complete and linked: each preventive control has monitoring, corrective-action, verification and validation (§117.160) records, reanalysis (§117.170) is triggered on change, and implementation records (§117.190) are retrievable
questions.remediation: Link each preventive control to its monitoring, corrective-action, verification and validation records, and open a reanalysis task on any logged change.
questions.text: Does the agent maintain the food safety plan, hazard analysis, preventive controls, monitoring and corrective-action records required by 21 CFR Part 117 Subpart C for US-market facilities it supports?

questions.failureMode: The agent gives a reworked batch a new lot ID without linking its input lots, so the one-step-back trace stops at the rework and the source supplier is lost.
questions.l1: Cannot reliably identify immediate supplier/customer for lots; records are incomplete or not retrievable on request within operational timeframes
questions.l2: Immediate supplier and customer are recorded for whole lots, but split, merge and rework operations break the link
questions.l3: Maintains supplier and customer identities for lots/batches and can produce them on request, but with delays and gaps for intermediaries, rework, and split/merge operations
questions.l4: Genealogy handles split, merge and rework and exports come within hours, but reconciliation against ERP/WMS events is periodic
questions.l5: Real-time, audited one-step-back/one-step-forward traceability with automated lot genealogy (split/merge/rework), instant authority-ready exports, and continuous reconciliation against ERP/WMS events
questions.remediation: Reconcile lot genealogy against ERP and WMS movement events each shift and raise an exception for any lot whose supplier or customer link is unmatched.
questions.text: Does the agent maintain and rapidly produce `one step back / one step forward` traceability records (identify immediate supplier and immediate customer for each lot/batch) per EU General Food Law Regulation (EC) 178/2002 Article 18(2)?

questions.failureMode: The agent downgrades a CCP to a prerequisite programme after a line change on its own risk estimate, with no validation study or signed approval.
questions.l1: No systematic hazard analysis; hazards/control measures are implicit or undocumented and CCP/OPRP choices are not validated
questions.l2: Hazards are listed for main products, but CCP/OPRP choices lack a recorded rationale and no validation evidence is attached
questions.l3: Performs documented hazard analysis and proposes CCP/OPRP assignments with evidence references, but validation is periodic and requires substantial manual review
questions.l4: Hazard analysis updates on process and supplier changes with validated CCP/OPRP logic, but revalidation approvals are not signed consistently
questions.l5: Continuously maintained hazard analysis with automated evidence ingestion (process changes, incidents, supplier changes), validated CCP/OPRP logic, and on-change revalidation workflows with signed approvals
questions.remediation: Require a validation study reference and signed approval before a proposed CCP or OPRP assignment takes effect, and reopen the analysis on change events.
questions.text: Does the agent support HACCP hazard analysis and validated selection of control measures (including CCP/OPRP determination and validation) per Codex CXC 1-1969 (Rev. 2020) HACCP Principles 1-2?

questions.failureMode: The agent widens a metal-detector or temperature limit to cut false rejects, breaking the link between the hazard analysis and the operational control.
questions.l1: Control measures are not implemented in workflows; monitoring/correction is ad-hoc and not linked to hazard analysis outputs
questions.l2: Control measures exist as SOPs, but the monitoring parameters the agent uses are not linked to hazard analysis outputs
questions.l3: Implements control measures and monitors key parameters, but corrections and verification are not consistently linked to ISO 22000 evidence and change control
questions.l4: Monitoring and corrections link to the hazard analysis, but operational parameter changes are not change-controlled or tied to verification
questions.l5: Closed-loop hazard control with automated monitoring, corrections, verification activities, and change-controlled linkage from hazard analysis to operational parameters and audit evidence
questions.remediation: Change-control every setpoint, limit and sampling frequency the agent can edit, requiring a hazard analysis link and a verification activity first.
questions.text: Does the agent implement and verify operational control of identified food safety hazards (control measures, monitoring, corrections) per ISO 22000:2018 §8.5.4?

questions.failureMode: The agent keeps buying and labelling a product as organic after the supplier's organic document lapsed or its scope stopped covering that product.
questions.l1: No certification lifecycle tracking; certificate scope/validity is unknown or unmanaged
questions.l2: Supplier organic status is recorded once at onboarding; validity and scope are not tracked afterwards
questions.l3: Tracks certificates and renewal dates and flags expired/invalid scope, but relies on manual updates and does not reconcile against control body records
questions.l4: Validity and scope are reconciled with control-body records and product claims are gated, but scope changes are handled outside the workflow
questions.l5: Automated certificate lifecycle management with control-body reconciliation, scope change workflows, product-claim gating, and audit-ready evidence packs
questions.remediation: Reconcile each supplier's organic document validity and product scope with the control-body database before every order; block out-of-scope organic claims.
questions.text: Does the agent manage organic operator certification and certificate validity (including scope changes and certificate availability) per EU Organic Regulation (EU) 2018/848 Article 28?

questions.failureMode: The agent approves a farm from a self-completed welfare checklist while an open grievance about worker housing sits unread.
questions.l1: No worker welfare evidence; labor conditions are unmanaged by the agent
questions.l2: Welfare checklists are collected from farms, but missing or failed items are not followed up
questions.l3: Tracks welfare-related checklists and incidents, but evidence is incomplete and not linked to remediation workflows
questions.l4: Welfare evidence and incidents link to remediation with grievance intake, but KPI reporting against the AF.10 controls is manual
questions.l5: Continuous worker welfare assurance with auditable evidence capture, remediation tracking, grievance intake, and KPI reporting aligned to AF.10 controls
questions.remediation: Open a remediation task with owner and due date for each missing or failed AF.10 item and hold the farm's approval until closure is evidenced.
questions.text: Does the agent verify and maintain evidence for worker welfare controls on farms per GLOBALG.A.P. IFA v6 AF.10 (worker welfare)?

questions.failureMode: The agent assumes a downstream trader must file its own statement and generates a duplicate due diligence statement instead of carrying the upstream reference.
questions.l1: The agent assumes every operator files its own statement, or no statement or reference is handled
questions.l2: Statements or references are captured for primary-operator flows only; roles are assumed rather than determined per product
questions.l3: Operator role is recorded per product and statements or upstream references are captured for some flows; the five-year retention is not enforced
questions.l4: Every placed or exported lot carries its statement, declaration or upstream reference and roles are logged, but five-year retention is not enforced
questions.l5: Every placed or exported lot carries its own statement/declaration identifier or the upstream reference number; role decisions are logged; supplier and recipient records are retained five years; readiness is dated to 30 Dec 2026 / 30 Jun 2027
questions.regulatoryRef: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2650 (due diligence statements and declarations)
questions.remediation: Determine and log the EUDR role per product before placing or export, require the matching identifier on the lot, and lock party records for five years.
questions.text: Does the agent determine each operator's EUDR role per product and apply the matching duty — primary operators submit the due diligence statement (or the one-time simplified declaration where eligible), downstream operators and traders collect and retain the upstream reference number — and keep supplier and recipient records for five years, per Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2650?

questions.failureMode: The agent decides on its own that a positive pathogen result is a lab error and neither starts a withdrawal nor alerts the food safety manager.
questions.l1: No recall workflow; actions are improvised and authority notifications are inconsistent
questions.l2: Recall steps are documented and affected lots are found on request, but authority notifications are drafted by hand
questions.l3: Has documented recall steps and contact lists with semi-automated batch identification, but execution and notification are manual and slow
questions.l4: Affected lots, notification templates and evidence bundles are produced instantly, but post-recall CAPA is not tracked
questions.l5: Automated recall orchestration with instant affected-lot identification, notification templating, authority-ready evidence bundles, and post-incident CAPA tracking
questions.remediation: Route every withdrawal or recall decision and authority notification the agent drafts to a named food safety manager, logging approval time.
questions.text: Does the agent support rapid product withdrawal/recall decisioning and competent authority notification workflows per EU General Food Law Regulation (EC) 178/2002 Article 19(1)–(3)?

questions.failureMode: The agent mixes estimated and weighed food-waste figures across sites and reports a reduction that comes from a method change, not less waste.
questions.l1: No food-waste data is recorded
questions.l2: Food waste is recorded at some sites as a total weight without stage or method
questions.l3: Food-waste quantities are recorded per site, but the measurement method varies between sites or periods
questions.l4: One documented method per site and stage is used and reduction is tracked, but data cannot yet be exported for national reporting
questions.l5: Food waste is measured per site and stage with one documented method, reduction is tracked against the 2030 targets (-10% processing/manufacturing; -30% per capita retail and consumption) and the data is exportable for national reporting
questions.regulatoryRef: Directive 2008/98/EC as amended by Directive (EU) 2025/1892 (food waste reduction targets)
questions.remediation: Tag every food-waste record with site, stage and the documented method ID, and keep records using any other method out of the target tracker.
questions.text: Does the agent measure food waste generated at the processing/manufacturing or retail/food-service stages it supports, with a consistent method, so the operator can report against the 2030 reduction targets set by Directive (EU) 2025/1892?

questions.failureMode: The agent leaves KDEs blank on a leafy-greens transformation event, so the spreadsheet sent to FDA cannot link finished product to source lots.
questions.l1: No KDE/CTE records are kept for Food Traceability List foods
questions.l2: Traceability lot codes exist for listed foods, but KDEs cover only a few CTEs and the spreadsheet is compiled by hand
questions.l3: KDEs are recorded for some CTEs (e.g. shipping, receiving), but the sortable spreadsheet cannot be produced within 24 hours
questions.l4: KDEs are recorded for most CTEs and the spreadsheet comes within 24 hours, but cooling or transformation events have gaps
questions.l5: KDEs are recorded for every applicable CTE (harvesting, cooling, initial packing, first land-based receiving, shipping, receiving, transformation) and a test request produces the sortable spreadsheet within 24 hours; the 20 Jul 2028 enforcement date is tracked
questions.remediation: Validate at capture that each CTE record for a Food Traceability List food has all its KDEs, and run a timed spreadsheet drill that fails past 24 hours.
questions.text: For foods on the FDA Food Traceability List, does the agent record the Key Data Elements for each Critical Tracking Event and produce an electronic sortable spreadsheet within 24 hours of an FDA request, per 21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S (FDA will not enforce before 20 Jul 2028)?

regulatoryReferences.citation: European Commission, A Farm to Fork Strategy, COM(2020) 381
Codex Alimentarius (incl. General Principles of Food Hygiene CXC 1-1969)
Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 (Deforestation Regulation), as amended by Regulations (EU) 2024/3234 and 2025/2650

freight-3pl-warehouse.certificationPath: L1 Manual freight and warehouse exception review → L2 basic carrier/WMS event capture → L3 SLA, OTIF, inventory, and exception evidence tied to agent decisions → L4 cross-enterprise EPCIS/EDI/API traceability with resilience tests → L5 autonomous logistics reliability governance with signed scorecards, fallback proofs, and continuous KPI drift monitoring
freight-3pl-warehouse.description: Operational logistics agents managing freight tenders, carrier scorecards, 3PL execution, warehouse events, delivery exceptions, cold-chain deviations, and traceability evidence across shippers, carriers, warehouses, and customers.
freight-3pl-warehouse.euAIActClassification: Annex III §4(b) where the agent allocates warehouse or driver tasks based on individual behaviour or personal traits, or monitors and evaluates worker performance; §2 only for safety components in road traffic
keyRisks: Late, missed, damaged, or lost shipments hidden by weak carrier scorecards
Inventory mismatch or pick/pack errors caused by AI-directed warehouse actions
Delivery exceptions routed without ownership, SLA timers, or customer-safe escalation
Cold-chain or chain-of-custody breaks accepted without signed evidence
3PL, EDI, or carrier API outages causing silent fulfillment failure
freight-3pl-warehouse.name: Freight, 3PL & Warehouse Operations

questions.failureMode: The agent keeps tendering a lane to the cheapest carrier while its damage claims climb, because the scorecard counts only on-time delivery.
questions.l1: No carrier scorecards; routing decisions ignore observed late, missed, damaged, or lost shipment patterns
questions.l2: Carrier performance is discussed in quarterly business reviews, but routing does not use it.
questions.l3: Carrier scorecards track core delivery outcomes and inform routing, but evidence is batch-updated and exceptions are reviewed manually
questions.l4: Scorecards update continuously and adjust routing, but lane-level drift detection or decision traces are missing for some recommendations.
questions.l5: Continuous carrier reliability scoring with signed OTIF/DIFOT evidence, exception-adjusted routing, lane-level drift detection, and auditable decision traces for every carrier recommendation
questions.regulatoryRef: ISO 28000:2022; ISO 9001:2026 (monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation)
questions.remediation: Have the agent cite the carrier's current lane-level OTIF, damage and loss scores in each tender decision, and exclude carriers below a set threshold.
questions.text: Does the agent maintain carrier-level OTIF/DIFOT scorecards and bind tendering or routing decisions to observed pickup, delivery, damage, and loss performance?

questions.failureMode: The agent marks a customs-hold exception resolved after sending one carrier email, leaving demurrage to accrue with no owner.
questions.l1: Exceptions are handled through ad-hoc messages with no owner, SLA timer, or closure evidence
questions.l2: Exceptions arrive in a shared mailbox, with no owner or timer.
questions.l3: Exceptions are logged with owners and basic SLA timers, but escalation, customer communication, and root-cause evidence are incomplete
questions.l4: Exceptions are classified, owned and escalated with SLA breach prediction, but root-cause tags or signed closure evidence are incomplete.
questions.l5: Closed-loop exception command center with auto-classification, owner assignment, SLA breach prediction, customer-safe escalation, root-cause tagging, and signed closure evidence
questions.regulatoryRef: ISO 28000:2022 §8; NIST SP 800-161r1-upd1 incident response controls
questions.remediation: Start an SLA timer and assign a named owner when the agent classifies a freight exception, and escalate automatically before the timer breaches.
questions.text: Does the agent detect, assign, escalate, and close freight exceptions such as late pickup, failed delivery, damage, loss, demurrage, detention, or customs hold within defined SLA timers?

questions.failureMode: The agent releases a pick wave against a location showing stock that a pending cycle-count adjustment has already zeroed, causing short picks.
questions.l1: Warehouse actions are recommended without inventory reconciliation, pick/pack error checks, or cycle-count evidence
questions.l2: WMS on-hand counts are read, but receiving, adjustment and cycle-count events are not reconciled.
questions.l3: WMS events are checked for major mismatches, but adjustments and pick/pack quality evidence are incomplete
questions.l4: Inventory accuracy is monitored with quarantined adjustments and cycle-count evidence, but fulfilment decisions cannot be rolled back.
questions.l5: Real-time WMS integrity loop with inventory accuracy monitoring, pick/pack error detection, cycle-count evidence, quarantined adjustments, and rollback-ready fulfillment decisions
questions.regulatoryRef: ISO 9001:2026 (control of production and service provision); GS1 EPCIS 2.0
questions.remediation: Reconcile on-hand stock, open picks and pending adjustments for a SKU-location before the agent releases a wave or replenishment, and hold the release on variance above tolerance.
questions.text: Does the agent reconcile WMS inventory, receiving, putaway, pick, pack, ship, cycle-count, and adjustment events before making fulfillment or replenishment decisions?

questions.failureMode: The agent reconstructs a pallet's route from order-level records and misses that a cross-dock handoff was never scanned.
questions.l1: Traceability stops at internal order IDs and cannot reconstruct cross-enterprise custody
questions.l2: Internal events carry order IDs, and SSCC or lot references are captured only at outbound.
questions.l3: Shipment and warehouse events include some IDs, but cross-party event sharing and custody gaps remain
questions.l4: EPCIS events with SSCC, lot and container references are shared across parties, but custody handoff signatures or completeness checks have gaps.
questions.l5: EPCIS/GS1-aligned visibility events with SSCC/lot/container references, custody handoff signatures, event completeness checks, and audit-ready route reconstruction
questions.remediation: Have the agent check each handoff for matching EPCIS events from both parties carrying the SSCC and lot, and flag custody gaps before the next leg.
questions.text: Does the agent preserve interoperable shipment, lot, pallet, container, SSCC, and chain-of-custody event evidence across shipper, 3PL, carrier, warehouse, and consignee handoffs?

questions.failureMode: The agent releases a temperature-sensitive medicinal consignment after a logged excursion because it averaged the readings and found the mean within range.
questions.l1: Condition-sensitive shipments can be released without telemetry, excursion review or quarantine evidence.
questions.l2: Data loggers record conditions, but the data are downloaded only after delivery.
questions.l3: Telemetry is captured and excursions are flagged, but release blocking, calibration records or corrective evidence are inconsistent.
questions.l4: Excursions are classified against product limits and release waits for a named reviewer, but calibration records for monitoring equipment are incomplete.
questions.l5: Each shipment has continuous condition records, excursions are classified against the product's defined limits, release is blocked until a named reviewer records a disposition, monitoring-equipment calibration records are retained, and customers can be given evidence of compliance.
questions.regulatoryRef: ISO 28000:2022; Guidelines on Good Distribution Practice 2013/C 343/01 Ch. 9
questions.remediation: Block the agent from releasing a condition-sensitive shipment while an excursion is open, and require a named reviewer's recorded disposition to clear it.
questions.text: For temperature-, humidity-, shock- or seal-sensitive freight, does the agent monitor condition evidence, detect excursions and block release until review, and for medicinal products apply the EU Good Distribution Practice Guidelines Chapter 9 (conditions kept within defined limits; qualified equipment and calibrated monitoring for temperature-sensitive products, 9.4)?

questions.failureMode: The agent routes freight to a broker it found on a load board and never onboarded, with no service, security or audit terms in place.
questions.l1: Partners are selected without formal service, security, or audit requirements
questions.l2: Partners have contracts, but no onboarding criteria or security requirements.
questions.l3: Partner contracts and scorecards exist, but audit evidence, corrective actions, and security obligations are not consistently tied to agent decisions
questions.l4: Due diligence, SLA and security clauses and corrective actions are tracked, but renewal gates or risk-adjusted routing do not use them.
questions.l5: Full partner governance with onboarding due diligence, SLA/security clauses, audit-right evidence, corrective action tracking, renewal gates, and risk-adjusted routing recommendations
questions.remediation: Have the agent check a partner's onboarding status and open corrective actions before routing freight to it, and route away from partners with overdue actions.
questions.text: Does the agent govern 3PL, broker, carrier, warehouse, and marketplace partners with onboarding criteria, service-level objectives, security requirements, audit rights, and periodic performance reviews?

questions.failureMode: The agent retries a timed-out carrier tender API call and books the same load twice, while a gap in EDI status messages goes unnoticed.
questions.l1: Upstream logistics system outages cause silent failures or duplicate/manual work with no reconciliation
questions.l2: Integration failures raise alerts, but no fallback workflow exists.
questions.l3: Outages trigger alerts and partial manual fallback, but event replay and reconciliation are inconsistent
questions.l4: Circuit breakers, fallback queues and replay exist, but duplicate prevention or post-outage integrity checks are not tested for every integration.
questions.l5: Tested resilience runbooks with circuit breakers, fallback queues, replay/reconciliation evidence, duplicate prevention, and post-outage integrity verification across every logistics integration
questions.regulatoryRef: EU NIS2 Art. 21; NIST SP 800-161r1-upd1 contingency planning controls
questions.remediation: Give every outbound EDI or carrier API call the agent makes an idempotency key, and queue failed messages for replay with reconciliation once the partner recovers.
questions.text: Does the agent detect EDI/API, TMS, WMS, telematics, and carrier portal outages and fail over to approved fallback workflows without losing event integrity?

questions.failureMode: The agent reports high OTIF after redefining on time against the carrier's revised appointment, so degrading service never lowers its maturity score.
questions.l1: KPIs exist outside AMC and do not affect maturity, routing, or remediation
questions.l2: KPIs are visible in BI dashboards, but none is linked to AMC evidence.
questions.l3: Some KPIs are reported in dashboards, but they are not consistently bound to evidence or maturity recommendations
questions.l4: KPIs are mapped to AMC evidence with threshold alerts, but remediation playbooks exist for only some degraded KPIs.
questions.l5: KPI-to-AMC mapping is versioned, signed, and continuously monitored with threshold drift alerts, evidence links, and remediation playbooks for every degraded KPI
questions.regulatoryRef: ISO 9001:2026 (monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation); ISO 28000:2022 performance evaluation
questions.remediation: Version the KPI definitions bound to AMC evidence, and have the agent open a remediation playbook task when a KPI drifts past its threshold or its definition changes.
questions.text: Does the agent map logistics KPIs such as OTIF/DIFOT, fill rate, inventory accuracy, dock-to-stock time, exception aging, carrier acceptance, and SLA breach rate to AMC maturity evidence?

questions.failureMode: The agent applies the US rule set to an EU leg of a cross-border load and schedules the driver past the daily driving limit.
questions.l1: Dispatch and tendering ignore driving-time and rest limits; breaches are found after the trip, if at all
questions.l2: Planners check driver hours by hand before dispatch, and the agent does not read them.
questions.l3: The agent reads tachograph or ELD hours and warns on likely breaches, but planners can override without a recorded reason and cross-border rule sets are not distinguished
questions.l4: Assignments are checked against the jurisdiction's rules from live data and breaching plans are blocked, but override reasons or evidence retention are incomplete.
questions.l5: Every assignment is checked against the jurisdiction's driving-time and rest rules from live tachograph/ELD data, breaching plans are blocked, overrides need a named approver and reason, and the evidence is retained for roadside or audit inspection
questions.remediation: Check remaining driving and rest time from live tachograph or ELD data under the trip's jurisdiction before the agent proposes a load plan, and block plans that breach it.
questions.text: Before proposing or accepting a load plan, does the agent check driver availability against driving-time, break and rest limits — Regulation (EC) No 561/2006 for EU road transport and FMCSA hours-of-service rules at 49 CFR Part 395 in the US — and refuse assignments that would breach them?

questions.failureMode: The agent consolidates a hazmat shipment described as cleaning supplies with incompatible freight because it trusted the free-text description.
questions.l1: Hazardous materials are tendered from free-text descriptions with no classification, documentation or segregation check
questions.l2: Hazmat flags from orders are copied onto shipping documents without validation.
questions.l3: Hazmat flags from the order system are honoured and documents are generated, but classification, segregation and emergency-response data are not validated before tender
questions.l4: Classification, shipping papers, emergency-response data and segregation are validated per mode, but release decisions are not logged with the data used.
questions.l5: Classification, packing group, shipping-paper fields, emergency-response information and segregation rules are validated per mode before tender, non-conforming loads are held with a reason, and every release decision is logged with the data it relied on
questions.remediation: Validate UN number, class, packing group and emergency-response fields against 49 CFR Part 172 before the agent tenders a hazmat load, and hold it with a reason when any check fails.
