questions.failureMode: The agent auto-remediates a significant incident and closes the ticket, so the 24-hour early warning clock never starts.
questions.l1: No significant-incident classification or reporting path.
questions.l2: Incidents are logged, but significance is not classified and no reporting owner exists.
questions.l3: Reporting path defined with owners, but at least one of the three deadlines is not tracked or not rehearsed.
questions.l4: All three deadlines are timed and templates are ready, but no timed rehearsal is on record.
questions.l5: Significance classification applied to every incident; timers for the 24-hour, 72-hour and one-month deadlines; templates prepared; at least one timed rehearsal on record; past reports show deadlines met.
questions.remediation: Start 24-hour, 72-hour and one-month timers automatically when an incident is classified significant, and rehearse the full sequence once a year.
questions.text: Where the operator is an essential or important entity under NIS2, can the agent's incident process submit an early warning within 24 hours and an incident notification within 72 hours of becoming aware of a significant incident, and a final report not later than one month after the incident notification (Directive (EU) 2022/2555 Art. 23(4))?

questions.failureMode: The agent's failed batch of payment instructions is logged as a routine error and never classified, so a major ICT-related incident goes unreported.
questions.l1: No ICT incident classification for the orchestration system.
questions.l2: Incidents are logged without applying the DORA classification criteria.
questions.l3: Incidents classified; a major-incident reporting path exists but templates or reporting steps have not been rehearsed.
questions.l4: Reports are produced from the templates, but rehearsals are missing or a past report was filed late.
questions.l5: Classification criteria applied to every incident; initial notification, intermediate and final reports produced from the templates; rehearsal records; past reports filed on time.
questions.regulatoryRef: EU DORA Art. 17; EU DORA Art. 19
questions.remediation: Apply the DORA classification criteria to every agent-related incident at triage and generate initial, intermediate and final reports from the templates.
questions.text: For financial entities in DORA scope, does the agent's ICT-related incident management process (EU DORA Art. 17) classify incidents and report major ICT-related incidents to the competent authority using the Art. 20 templates (Art. 19)?

questions.failureMode: The agent sends customer records to the wrong partner endpoint and nobody records when awareness began, so the 72-hour window cannot be shown.
questions.l1: No path from breach detection to notification.
questions.l2: Breaches are escalated by email; detection and notification times are not recorded.
questions.l3: Path defined, but awareness and notification times are not recorded, so the 72-hour window cannot be shown.
questions.l4: Timestamps are recorded and a breach register is kept, but no rehearsal is on record.
questions.l5: Awareness and notification timestamps recorded per breach; late notifications carry reasons; breach register maintained; rehearsal on record.
questions.remediation: Record the awareness timestamp at breach triage and start a 72-hour countdown that alerts the DPO, logging the notification time or the reason for delay.
questions.text: Does the agent's breach process notify the competent supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware of a personal data breach, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to natural persons' rights and freedoms (GDPR Art. 33(1))?

questions.failureMode: The agent's high-risk component contributes to a serious incident that is handled as an ordinary outage, so no market surveillance report is filed.
questions.l1: No serious-incident classification or reporting path to market surveillance authorities.
questions.l2: Serious incidents are discussed internally, with no criteria and no reporting owner.
questions.l3: Reporting path defined with owners, but awareness and report timestamps are not recorded, so the 15-day limit cannot be shown.
questions.l4: Timestamps are recorded and reports filed, but no timed rehearsal is on record.
questions.l5: Serious-incident criteria applied to every incident; awareness, causal-link and report timestamps recorded; a timed rehearsal on record; past reports show the 15-day limit met.
questions.remediation: Add serious-incident criteria to triage for the high-risk AI system, record awareness and causal-link timestamps, and alert at day 10 of the 15-day limit.
questions.text: For a high-risk AI system in the orchestration chain, does its provider report each serious incident to the market surveillance authority immediately after establishing a causal link, and in any event not later than 15 days after becoming aware of it (EU AI Act Art. 73(1)-(2); Annex III systems from 2 December 2027)?

questions.failureMode: The agent installs a vulnerable third-party tool plugin with no security review, and an exploit in it reaches the orchestration environment.
questions.l1: No vulnerability intake or handling process for the orchestration environment.
questions.l2: Scanner findings are triaged ad hoc; no disclosure channel exists.
questions.l3: Detected vulnerabilities are triaged, but there is no published disclosure channel or no remediation deadline per severity.
questions.l4: A disclosure channel and severity deadlines are tracked, but security requirements are not applied to every acquired component such as agent plugins.
questions.l5: Published vulnerability disclosure channel; every reported or detected vulnerability tracked with severity, remediation deadline and closure evidence; deadline attainment reported; security requirements applied to every acquired or developed component.
questions.remediation: Publish a disclosure channel, set remediation deadlines per severity, and require a security check before the agent loads any new plugin or connector.
questions.text: Where the operator is an essential or important entity under NIS2, does the agent-orchestrated environment apply security in network and information systems acquisition, development and maintenance, including vulnerability handling and disclosure (Directive (EU) 2022/2555 Art. 21(2)(e))?

regulatoryBasis: EU DORA Art. 9 ICT risk management

regulatoryReferences.citation: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Information security management systems (with Amd 1:2024)

regulatoryReferences.text: EU DORA Art. 9 ICT risk management

regulatoryReferences.citation: ISO 22301:2019 Security and resilience — Business continuity management systems (with Amd 1:2024)

sdgAlignment: SDG 8 — Decent Work and Economic Growth

partnerships-prosperity.certificationPath: L1 Basic partnership governance → L2 IP rights management → L3 FRAND/open source compliance → L4 Full SDG 17 partnership framework → L5 Autonomous partnership orchestration with verified equity, IP protection, and measurable prosperity outcomes
partnerships-prosperity.description: Global collaboration and sharing to create intellectual property in an open shared environment — AI agents facilitating multi-stakeholder partnerships, open innovation ecosystems, and IP co-creation with emphasis on governance, fair access, and prevention of exploitation.
partnerships-prosperity.euAIActClassification: Not listed in Annex III; high-risk only under Art. 6(1) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a product covered by Annex I legislation — otherwise Art. 4 (AI literacy), Art. 5 (prohibited practices) and Art. 50 (transparency) apply
keyRisks: IP exploitation by dominant partners through AI-facilitated access
Open source license violation in AI-generated code
Partnership value extraction without reciprocal benefit
Trade secret leakage through AI collaboration tools
Exclusion of developing economy partners from AI-mediated partnerships
partnerships-prosperity.name: Partnerships for Peace & Prosperity

questions.failureMode: The agent attributes a jointly developed design to the partner that hosts the collaboration workspace, handing that partner the IP.
questions.l1: No IP rights management; partnership AI creates joint outputs without clear ownership, licensing terms, or TRIPS-compliant protection
questions.l2: Ownership of joint outputs is discussed per project, without written allocation.
questions.l3: Agent tracks IP ownership in partnership outputs and applies standard licensing templates, but does not implement automated TRIPS compliance or proactive IP conflict detection
questions.l4: Ownership is tracked with agreements and AI authorship disclosure, but contribution tracking or IP conflict detection is partial.
questions.l5: Full IP governance with automated TRIPS-compliant rights management, joint IP ownership agreements, AI authorship disclosure, patent landscape monitoring, copyright registration support, and IP dispute prevention through clear contribution tracking
questions.remediation: Record every partner and AI contribution to a joint output in a contribution ledger at creation, and check new outputs against existing IP claims before release.
questions.text: Does the agent manage IP rights in partnership ecosystems per TRIPS Agreement Articles 27-34 patent rights and Article 10 copyright protection for AI-generated collaborative outputs?

questions.failureMode: The agent pastes a GPL-licensed snippet into a permissively licensed partner library with no licence recorded.
questions.l1: No licence tracking.
questions.l2: Licences of direct dependencies are listed by hand in a README.
questions.l3: Licences detected for direct dependencies; transitive dependencies or AI-generated snippets not covered, or compatibility not enforced.
questions.l4: Every component including generated code is recorded with compatibility gates, but attribution files are not generated.
questions.l5: Licence recorded for every component including transitive and generated code; compatibility rules block release on conflict; attribution files generated.
questions.remediation: Scan generated code for matches to licensed sources, record SPDX expressions for every component, and block release when compatibility rules fail.
questions.text: Does the agent record the licence of every open-source component in software it generates or assembles as SPDX license expressions (SPDX 3.0) and enforce licence-compatibility rules before release?

questions.failureMode: The agent schedules partnership work in languages and time zones that suit the largest partners, and smaller partners' participation falls unmeasured.
questions.l1: No partner contribution or benefit metrics.
questions.l2: Partner participation is discussed at steering meetings without metrics.
questions.l3: Agent monitors partnership contribution metrics and flags imbalanced participation, but does not act on flags through a documented process.
questions.l4: Metrics, thresholds and recorded actions exist per partner, but governance reports do not reach the partners.
questions.l5: Contribution and benefit metrics per partner on a fixed schedule; documented thresholds; each imbalance triggers a recorded action; governance reporting to partners.
questions.remediation: Compute contribution and benefit per partner each quarter and open a recorded action when any partner, including developing-economy partners, falls below threshold.
questions.text: Does the agent implement equitable partnership governance per ISO 26000:2010 §6.8 (community involvement and development), with partner participation measured and imbalances acted on?

questions.failureMode: The agent drafts a standards contribution embodying a partner's patent without flagging the need for a timely essential IPR disclosure.
questions.l1: No tracking of SEP declarations or FRAND undertakings.
questions.l2: Declarations are kept in individual partners' files with no shared tracking.
questions.l3: Declarations tracked; undertakings not linked to the standards and patents they cover.
questions.l4: Every declaration is linked to its standard, patent family and undertaking, but the register is not reviewed on each standard release.
questions.l5: Every declaration linked to its standard, patent family and FRAND undertaking; licensing terms and negotiation records retained; register reviewed on each standard release.
questions.regulatoryRef: ETSI IPR Policy clause 4.1; ETSI IPR Policy clause 6.1
questions.remediation: Link each essential IPR declaration to its standard clause, patent family and FRAND undertaking in a register the agent checks before drafting contributions.
questions.text: Where partners contribute to ETSI standards, does the agent track timely disclosure of essential IPR (ETSI IPR Policy clause 4.1) and the FRAND licensing undertakings given for it (clause 6.1)?

questions.failureMode: The agent replicates partners' non-personal data to a third-country region where a governmental access request can reach it without legal review.
questions.l1: No assessment of third-country governmental access risk.
questions.l2: The risk is acknowledged but not assessed, and contracts are silent on governmental access.
questions.l3: Contract clauses address access requests; no technical measures or request-handling procedure.
questions.l4: Technical, organisational and contractual measures and a procedure exist, but the request log or legal review records are incomplete.
questions.l5: Technical, organisational and contractual measures documented; each access request handled under a written procedure with legal review records; request log maintained.
questions.remediation: Encrypt partners' non-personal data with keys held in the Union and route any third-country access request through a written procedure with legal review.
questions.text: If the agent provides data processing services holding partners' non-personal data in the Union, does the provider take technical, organisational and legal measures, including contracts, to prevent third-country governmental access or transfer that would conflict with Union or national law (EU Data Act Art. 32(1))?

questions.failureMode: The agent includes one partner's confidential process parameters in an answer to another partner using the same collaboration assistant.
questions.l1: No trade-secret inventory or confidentiality controls for information shared with AI systems.
questions.l2: Confidential material is marked, but nothing stops it being pasted into AI tools.
questions.l3: A trade-secret inventory and access controls exist, but they do not cover AI system inputs, logs and outputs, or partner confidentiality agreements are missing.
questions.l4: Inventory, AI-scope access controls and partner agreements exist, but the misappropriation response procedure has not been exercised.
questions.l5: Classified trade-secret inventory; access controls and logging cover AI inputs, logs and outputs; confidentiality agreements with every partner; misappropriation response procedure exercised; evidence assembled for the Art. 2(1)(c) 'reasonable steps' test.
questions.remediation: Classify trade secrets and apply DLP to prompts, logs and outputs of partnership AI tools so classified content is blocked or redacted before reaching the model.
questions.text: Does the agent protect trade secrets in partnership AI systems per EU Trade Secrets Directive 2016/943 Articles 2 and 4 reasonable measures requirements?

questions.failureMode: The agent reports partnership success as output volume while most of the value flows to one partner, and no metric shows the imbalance.
questions.l1: No partnership impact measurement; collaborative outcomes are not systematically measured against SDG targets or GRI economic impact standards
questions.l2: Activity counts are reported, with no economic impact estimate.
questions.l3: Agent tracks partnership outputs and estimates economic impact, but does not implement UN SDG 17 multi-stakeholder monitoring or GRI 203 indirect economic impact reporting
questions.l4: SDG 17 and GRI 203 reporting are in place, but prosperity distribution across partners is not analysed.
questions.l5: Full impact measurement with SDG 17 indicator 17.16.1 tracking, GRI 203 indirect economic impact reporting, prosperity distribution analysis across partners, and transparent partnership impact disclosure for stakeholders
questions.remediation: Report GRI 203 indirect economic impacts per partner alongside activity metrics, and disclose how value created by the partnership is distributed.
questions.text: Does the agent implement partnership impact measurement per UN SDG 17 indicator 17.16.1 multi-stakeholder monitoring frameworks and GRI 203 Indirect Economic Impacts?

questions.failureMode: The agent executes a resource-allocation decision for the consortium that no partner owns, so the harmed partner has nobody to seek redress from.
questions.l1: No assignment of responsibility for partnership AI decisions.
questions.l2: A lead partner is responsible in general, but individual decision types are not assigned.
questions.l3: Agent documents accountability assignments for partnership AI systems, but not for every decision type, or without a redress path.
questions.l4: Every decision type is assigned with a redress mechanism, but accountability is not reviewed or reported on schedule.
questions.l5: Accountability matrix assigns every partnership AI decision type to a named partner; redress mechanism for AI harms; accountability reviewed and reported on a documented schedule.
questions.remediation: Assign each partnership AI decision type to a named partner in an accountability matrix the agent reads, and refuse to execute decision types with no owner.
questions.text: Is responsibility for each partnership AI decision assigned to a named partner, with a redress path for AI harms, consistent with OECD AI Principle 1.5 'Accountability' (OECD/LEGAL/0449, amended 3 May 2024)?

questions.failureMode: The agent exports AI-generated partnership models without protection measures, and a departing partner walks away with the full asset.
questions.l1: No trade secret or TPM compliance; AI collaboration environments lack Art. 2 reasonable measures for confidential information and WIPO WCT Art. 11 technological protection for AI-generated IP
questions.l2: Generic access controls cover partnership data; AI-generated IP has no technological protection.
questions.l3: Agent implements basic access controls for partnership data, but does not systematically apply Art. 2 reasonable measures standard or WIPO WCT Art. 11 technological protection for AI-generated collaborative IP
questions.l4: AI-specific classification, protection measures and an inventory exist, but misappropriation detection or the audit trail is partial.
questions.l5: Full EU Trade Secrets Directive Art. 2 reasonable measures with AI-specific access classification, WIPO WCT Art. 11 technological protection for AI-generated IP, trade secret inventory management, misappropriation detection, and IP protection audit trail for partnership governance
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Trade Secrets Directive 2016/943 Art. 2; WIPO WCT Art. 11
questions.remediation: Apply technological protection measures to AI-generated partnership assets at export, and alert when an asset is accessed outside the partner's entitlement.
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Trade Secrets Directive 2016/943 Article 2 reasonable measures standard for AI collaboration environments and WIPO Copyright Treaty Article 11 technological protection measures for AI-generated partnership IP?

questions.failureMode: The agent proposes the key claim of an invention but keeps no contribution log, so one partner files alone and the others cannot show joint inventorship.
questions.l1: No inventorship, ownership or licence-scope records for partnership inventions.
questions.l2: Inventions are noted in meeting minutes; inventorship and ownership are not recorded.
questions.l3: Ownership and licence scope are documented, but contribution and provenance evidence is missing for some inventions.
questions.l4: Inventorship, ownership and licence scope are recorded, but provenance logs are missing for some inventions.
questions.l5: Every partnership invention has inventorship and ownership records, a licence scope (field of use, sublicensing) covering the Art. 28(1) acts, and retained contribution and provenance logs.
questions.remediation: Capture inventorship, ownership and licence scope at invention disclosure, and attach the agent's contribution and model training provenance logs to each record.
questions.text: Does the agent operationalize TRIPS Agreement Article 28 patent rights (rights to prevent third parties from making, using, offering for sale, selling, or importing) for AI-assisted inventions created in partnerships by (1) documenting inventorship/ownership allocation, (2) defining licensing scopes/field-of-use and sublicensing rights, and (3) preparing enforcement-ready evidence (lab notebooks, model training provenance, contribution logs) for disputes and cross-border enforcement?

questions.failureMode: The agent clones a session musician's recorded performance into a new partner track without any authorisation covering that use.
questions.l1: Fixed performances are reproduced through AI tools with no record of performer authorisation.
questions.l2: Some performer releases are on file, but AI voice tools are used without checking them.
questions.l3: Authorisation obtained in common cases, but scope (media, territory, term) is not recorded or not checked before reproduction.
questions.l4: Every reproduction is linked to a scoped authorisation, but scope is not checked before every use.
questions.l5: Every reproduction of a fixed performance is linked to a recorded authorisation with scope; scope checked before each use; evidence retained.
questions.remediation: Check the performer authorisation register for media, territory and term before the agent reproduces or trains on a fixed performance, blocking on no match.
questions.text: Where partnership projects reproduce performances fixed in phonograms, including through AI voice capture or training, does the agent hold the performers' authorisation for each reproduction (WIPO WPPT Art. 7) and keep evidence linking each use to that authorisation?

questions.failureMode: The agent shares a dataset whose metadata reveals a partner's proprietary formulation before any protective measures were agreed with the recipient.
questions.l1: Trade secrets in shared data are disclosed without identification or agreed protective measures.
questions.l2: Trade secrets are identified ad hoc, only after a recipient asks for data.
questions.l3: Trade secrets are identified for some datasets, or disclosure proceeds before the agreed measures are in place for at least one recipient.
questions.l4: Identification and gating exist per recipient, but trade secrets in metadata are missed or some gate decisions are not logged.
questions.l5: Every shared dataset has its trade-secret elements identified, including in metadata; disclosure is gated on a recorded agreement of protective measures per recipient; every gate decision is logged.
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Data Act Art. 4(6); EU Data Act Art. 5(9)
questions.remediation: Gate every Data Act disclosure on a recorded protective-measure agreement for that recipient and on trade-secret tagging that includes metadata fields.
questions.text: When partnership data access or sharing under the EU Data Act includes trade secrets, does the agent disclose them only after the trade secrets are identified and the protective measures to preserve their confidentiality are agreed with the user (Art. 4(6)) or the third party (Art. 5(9))?

questions.failureMode: The agent recommends a permanent import restriction on a developing-economy partner's produce on thin evidence, with no provisional status or review date.
questions.l1: No SPS 5.7 discipline: measures are recommended/implemented without evidencing insufficiency, provisional status, information-gathering, or review timelines
questions.l2: Precaution is applied informally, with the rationale scattered across emails.
questions.l3: Uses a precautionary approach informally, but does not document provisional status, evidence-gathering plans, and review timelines in a trade-dispute-resilient way
questions.l4: Insufficiency triggers, templates and evidence plans exist, but review deadlines are not tracked.
questions.l5: Full SPS Art. 5.7 governance with structured triggers for insufficiency, provisional-measure templates, evidence acquisition plans, periodic review SLAs, and audit-ready decision records supporting proportionality and WTO defensibility
questions.remediation: Mark any SPS recommendation the agent makes on insufficient evidence as provisional, attach an information-gathering plan, and set a review date that alerts the owner.
questions.text: Where partnership outputs implicate sanitary/phytosanitary (SPS) measures, does the agent apply WTO SPS Agreement Article 5.7 by (1) identifying when scientific evidence is insufficient, (2) implementing provisional measures with documented rationale, (3) actively seeking additional information for a more objective risk assessment, and (4) reviewing/updating measures within a reasonable period with recorded decision trails?

questions.failureMode: The agent treats a performer's recording as a pure authors'-rights asset and skips the neighbouring-rights check the workflow needed.
questions.l1: No mapping governance: WIPO treaty references are generic, WPPT-specific rights are missed, and citations are not reviewed
questions.l2: Treaty references are generic WIPO notes attached to workflows.
questions.l3: Maintains a mapping in documentation, but it is not kept current with workflow changes or used to gate AI content operations
questions.l4: A versioned mapping with legal review exists, but it is not used to gate AI content operations.
questions.l5: Robust mapping governance with versioning, legal review, and workflow gating so that WCT/WPPT obligations are correctly applied and evidence is produced per right/article
questions.remediation: Map each content workflow step (capture, reproduction, distribution, TPM) to the WCT or WPPT article it implicates and gate the agent's workflow on that rights check.
questions.text: Does the program maintain a WIPO treaty-to-right mapping (WCT vs WPPT) for partnership outputs (authors rights vs performers neighboring rights), ensuring each content workflow (capture, reproduction, distribution, TPM/DRM) is mapped to the correct treaty article(s) and reviewed periodically by legal/compliance?

questions.failureMode: The agent assembles a release with an untracked transitive dependency and ships no SBOM that would reveal it.
questions.l1: No SBOM produced.
questions.l2: An SBOM is assembled manually for major releases only.
questions.l3: SBOM produced for some builds, or not machine-readable, or missing top-level dependencies.
questions.l4: A machine-readable SBOM per build covers transitive dependencies, but lacks component hashes or the build does not fail when generation fails.
questions.l5: Machine-readable SBOM per build covering top-level and transitive dependencies with component hashes; delivered with the release; the build fails when SBOM generation fails.
questions.regulatoryRef: EU CRA Annex I Part II(1)
questions.remediation: Generate a machine-readable SBOM in each build the agent triggers, include component hashes, and fail the build when SBOM generation fails.
questions.text: Does the agent produce, for each build of software it generates or assembles, a software bill of materials in a commonly used, machine-readable format covering at least the top-level dependencies, as the Cyber Resilience Act requires from 11 December 2027 (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 Annex I Part II(1))?

questions.failureMode: The agent quietly patches an actively exploited vulnerability in a partner product and never triggers the 24-hour early warning.
questions.l1: No path for reporting actively exploited vulnerabilities.
questions.l2: Actively exploited vulnerabilities reach the security team informally, with no owner.
questions.l3: Path defined with an owner; the 24-hour deadline is not tracked or not rehearsed.
questions.l4: A timed workflow with an early-warning template exists, but no timed rehearsal is on record.
questions.l5: Exploitation detection feeds a timed reporting workflow with an early-warning template; at least one timed rehearsal on record; past notifications show the deadline met.
questions.remediation: Connect exploitation detection to a workflow that starts a 24-hour timer and pre-fills the early-warning template for the single reporting platform.
questions.text: Where the agent's partnership outputs are products with digital elements, can the manufacturer send an early warning of an actively exploited vulnerability within 24 hours of becoming aware of it via the single reporting platform (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 Art. 14(2)(a), applicable from 11 September 2026)?

questions.failureMode: The agent corrupts shared partnership data and only the operating partner is told, leaving downstream partners and communities on bad outputs.
questions.l1: No incident communication between partners.
questions.l2: Incidents are shared in a partner channel with no list of who must be told.
questions.l3: Incidents communicated to the partner that operates the system only; other AI actors or affected communities not informed.
questions.l4: A matrix exists and incident records show who was informed, but the matrix is not reviewed after incidents.
questions.l5: Communication matrix lists every partner AI actor and affected-community channel; each incident record shows who was informed and when; matrix reviewed after each incident.
questions.remediation: Maintain a matrix of every partner AI actor and affected-community channel, and have the incident workflow record each notification sent against it.
questions.text: Are incidents and errors in partnership AI systems communicated to every relevant partner AI actor and to affected communities, per NIST AI RMF MANAGE 4.3?

questions.failureMode: The agent loads a partner fine-tuned model whose training data held other partners' confidential documents, which no development practice screened.
questions.l1: No secure development practice applied to model development.
questions.l2: Partners assert secure development practices without evidence.
questions.l3: SSDF practices applied to code, but the SP 800-218A AI-specific practices are not mapped.
questions.l4: SP 800-218A practices are mapped per model release with evidence, but gaps are not tracked or partner attestations are missing.
questions.l5: Each applicable SP 800-218A practice mapped to evidence per model release; gaps tracked; partner attestations retained.
questions.remediation: Require each partner model release to arrive with SP 800-218A practice-level evidence, and refuse to load a model version whose evidence is missing.
questions.text: Do partners that develop or fine-tune generative AI models used by the agent follow the practices of NIST SP 800-218A (SSDF Community Profile for Generative AI and Dual-Use Foundation Models), with practice-level evidence?

questions.failureMode: The agent accepts a dominant partner's unilaterally imposed term granting it unlimited use of shared data without flagging it for legal review.
questions.l1: Data-sharing terms are not reviewed for fairness
questions.l2: Templates were reviewed informally once, with no record of the outcome.
questions.l3: Legal reviews new templates, but negotiated changes and partner-imposed terms are not screened
questions.l4: Every term set is screened with clause-cited findings, but review outcomes are not always retained.
questions.l5: Every data-sharing term set is screened against the Article 13 list of unfair terms, findings are routed to legal with the clause cited, and the review outcome is retained
questions.remediation: Screen every proposed data-sharing term set against the Article 13 list and route each hit to legal with the clause cited before the agent accepts or proposes it.
questions.text: Does the agent screen data-sharing terms proposed to or by partner enterprises for unfair contractual terms under EU Data Act 2023/2854 Article 13, and flag unilaterally imposed terms on data access and use for legal review?

questions.failureMode: The agent pulls in an abandoned open-source package with known vulnerabilities because it was the first search result.
questions.l1: Third-party components integrated without any security assessment.
questions.l2: Third-party components are chosen by popularity, with occasional security checks.
questions.l3: Direct third-party components are assessed at onboarding; transitive or open-source components, or component updates, are not assessed.
questions.l4: Every component is assessed before integration and on update, but vulnerabilities found are not reported to maintainers.
questions.l5: Every integrated component, including transitive and open-source ones, has a recorded due-diligence assessment (provenance, known vulnerabilities, maintenance status) before integration and on each update; vulnerabilities found in a component are reported to its maintainer (Art. 13(6)).
questions.remediation: Require a due-diligence record (provenance, known vulnerabilities, maintenance status) before the agent adds or updates any third-party component.
questions.text: When the agent assembles products with digital elements that integrate third-party components, including free and open-source components, does the manufacturer exercise due diligence so that those components do not compromise the product's cybersecurity (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 Art. 13(5), applicable from 11 December 2027)?

regulatoryReferences.citation: WIPO Copyright Treaty and WIPO Internet Treaties (1996)

patient-lifecycle.certificationPath: L1 Basic appointment scheduling → L2 Clinical workflow automation with safety checks → L3 Full care coordination with JCI-aligned quality → L4 Predictive clinical decision support with FDA compliance → L5 Autonomous patient lifecycle orchestration with verified clinical outcomes
patient-lifecycle.description: Appointment through investigation, diagnosis, treatment, care, and prognosis — covering the complete patient journey with emphasis on clinical safety, informed consent, care coordination, and outcome measurement.
patient-lifecycle.euAIActClassification: Art. 6(1) and Annex I (Regulation (EU) 2017/745 MDR, 2017/746 IVDR) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a medical device; Annex III §5(d) for emergency healthcare patient triage; §5(a) for public-authority eligibility decisions on healthcare services
keyRisks: Misdiagnosis from AI clinical decision support without adequate validation
Treatment delay from automated triage errors
Informed consent violations through AI-mediated patient communication
Care fragmentation from poor AI-managed handoff between providers
Prognostic model bias leading to disparate care quality across demographics
patient-lifecycle.name: Patient Lifecycle

questions.failureMode: The agent issues a time-critical stroke alert with no basis the clinician can check, and the clinician acts on it as if it were independently reviewable advice.
questions.l1: Opaque recommendations, including time-critical alerts, are offered as non-device CDS
questions.l2: A generic model description is available, but not the inputs and data relied on for each patient
questions.l3: Basis information is available on request but is not patient-specific, and time-criticality is not assessed
questions.l4: Each recommendation shows its patient-specific basis and an intended-use analysis is on file, but automation-bias usability testing is not recorded
questions.l5: Each recommendation shows its patient-specific basis; an intended-use and time-criticality analysis is on file; automation-bias usability testing is recorded; functions that fail the criteria follow the device pathway
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA Clinical Decision Support Software guidance (January 2026)
questions.remediation: Attach to each recommendation the patient inputs used, data sources, validation summary and known missing data, and record a time-criticality assessment for each function before release.
questions.text: Does the agent keep non-device CDS status by letting health care professionals independently review the basis of each recommendation (inputs, data relied on, validation, patient-specific unknowns), and treat time-critical or judgment-directing uses as device functions (FDA CDS guidance, January 2026)?

questions.failureMode: The agent schedules a procedure and sends pre-procedure instructions although the consent on file predates the AI disclosure, so the patient never received it.
questions.l1: No digital consent management; informed consent is paper-based with no AI-specific disclosures about automated decision-making in care
questions.l2: Consent forms are digital, but none mention the agent's role in care decisions
questions.l3: Agent generates digital consent forms with AI disclosure language and tracks consent status, but does not support dynamic consent for evolving AI involvement or multilingual accessibility
questions.l4: AI disclosures are dynamic, multilingual and checked at each care stage, but the consent audit trail is incomplete
questions.l5: Comprehensive informed consent with AI-specific disclosures per JCI PCC.4, dynamic consent for changing AI involvement, multilingual support, health literacy-appropriate language, consent verification at each care stage, and automated consent audit trail per CMS requirements
questions.remediation: Before the agent performs a care step that relies on automated recommendations, check that the patient's consent record includes the current AI disclosure version and block the step if it does not.
questions.text: Does the agent manage informed consent per JCI Standard PCC.4 and CMS 42 CFR §482.24(c) including AI-specific disclosure requirements?

questions.failureMode: The agent assigns ESI 4 to a patient with atypical chest pain from free-text complaint alone and never re-triages after abnormal vital signs are charted.
questions.l1: No automated triage safety; patient prioritization is not validated against ESI criteria or clinical acuity assessment
questions.l2: ESI levels are suggested from chief-complaint text only, without vital signs or clinician confirmation
questions.l3: Agent applies ESI-aligned triage scoring with vital sign integration, but does not implement continuous re-triage or detect clinical deterioration between assessments
questions.l4: ESI agreement is validated and re-triage is logged, but clinicians do not confirm every level or Annex III 5(d) controls are not evidenced
questions.l5: ESI assignments are validated against a clinician-labelled sample with recorded agreement; re-triage triggers and escalation times are logged; clinicians confirm every triage level; where Annex III 5(d) applies the high-risk controls are evidenced
questions.regulatoryRef: ESI v4 Implementation Handbook; EU AI Act Annex III point 5(d)
questions.remediation: Require a clinician to confirm each agent-assigned ESI level before it changes queue position, and re-score automatically when new vital signs arrive, escalating if acuity rises.
questions.text: Does the agent implement triage safety per the Emergency Severity Index (ESI) v4 with escalation protocols, and evidence the high-risk controls where EU AI Act Annex III point 5(d) (emergency patient triage) applies?

questions.failureMode: The agent closes a discharge with follow-up activities still open in the CarePlan and never notifies the receiving community provider.
questions.l1: No digital care coordination; care plans are fragmented across providers with no unified patient journey tracking
questions.l2: CarePlan resources are created, but activities are not updated as care proceeds
questions.l3: Agent maintains FHIR CarePlan resources with activity tracking, but care transitions and discharge planning are not automated or coordinated across care settings
questions.l4: CarePlans drive transition notifications and discharge planning, but plans are not synchronised with other providers
questions.l5: Full care coordination with FHIR CarePlan lifecycle management, automated care transition notifications, discharge planning per CMS §482.43, post-discharge follow-up scheduling, readmission risk prediction, and cross-provider care plan synchronization
questions.regulatoryRef: HL7 FHIR R4 CarePlan Resource; CMS 42 CFR §482.43
questions.remediation: Have the agent send a transition notification with the current CarePlan to the receiving provider at discharge and track receipt, escalating to the care coordinator when receipt is not confirmed.
questions.text: Does the agent maintain care coordination records per HL7 FHIR CarePlan resource and CMS 42 CFR §482.43 discharge planning requirements?

questions.failureMode: The agent computes quality measures with last year's specification logic and value sets and reports them as current-year results.
questions.l1: Measures are computed with unversioned or unknown logic
questions.l2: Current-year specifications are named, but the logic used cannot be tied to a specification version
questions.l3: Current-year specifications are used, but inputs are not retained or the logic version is not shown
questions.l4: Specification version, inputs and results are recorded, but reviewers cannot reproduce a sampled measure
questions.l5: Each computed measure records specification version, inputs and result; reviewers can reproduce a sampled measure; specification updates are applied before the reporting year starts
questions.remediation: Store the eCQM specification version, input patient set and result with every measure the agent computes, and reproduce a sample each reporting period.
questions.text: Where the agent computes clinical quality measures, does it use the CMS-published eCQM specifications for the reporting year, retain calculation inputs, and show the measure logic version to reviewers?

questions.failureMode: The agent recommends advanced imaging less often for patients with limited English proficiency, and nobody detects the pattern.
questions.l1: No equity assessment; diagnostic and treatment patterns are not analyzed for demographic disparities
questions.l2: Demographic counts are reported, but no disparity statistics are run on the agent's recommendations
questions.l3: Agent monitors basic demographic distribution of diagnoses and treatments, but does not perform statistical disparity analysis or implement bias mitigation
questions.l4: Disparity analysis and bias detection run, but alerts do not lead to tracked remediation
questions.l5: Comprehensive equity monitoring with statistical disparity analysis across race, ethnicity, gender, age, and socioeconomic status, automated bias detection in CDS recommendations, disparity alert system, and remediation tracking per ACA §1557
questions.remediation: Compute recommendation rates and outcomes per demographic group for each agent function monthly, and open a remediation ticket when a gap passes a set threshold.
questions.text: Does the agent assess diagnostic and treatment equity across demographics per CMS 42 CFR §482.13 patient rights and ACA §1557 non-discrimination?

questions.failureMode: The agent books a video visit for a patient reporting acute abdominal pain with a clinician who is not licensed where the patient is located.
questions.l1: No telehealth quality standards; virtual care is delivered without standardized quality controls or regulatory compliance verification
questions.l2: Audio and video quality are checked at connection, but provider licensing and patient identity are not verified
questions.l3: Agent enforces basic telehealth quality parameters (video/audio quality, connection stability) and verifies provider licensing, but does not implement full ISO 13131 quality of service framework
questions.l4: Quality monitoring, licensing and identity checks run, but clinical appropriateness screening or telehealth-specific consent is missing
questions.l5: Full telehealth quality management per ISO 13131 Clause 5 with connection quality monitoring, clinical appropriateness screening, provider licensing verification across jurisdictions, patient identity verification, and telehealth-specific informed consent management
questions.remediation: Before the agent books a telehealth visit, check the provider's licence against the patient's location and screen the reason for visit against criteria that require in-person care.
questions.text: Does the agent implement telehealth standards per ISO 13131:2021 Clause 5 quality of service requirements and applicable state/federal telehealth regulations?

questions.failureMode: The agent drafts an amoxicillin order for a patient whose penicillin allergy is recorded only in a free-text note.
questions.l1: No medication safety automation; drug interactions and allergies are not systematically checked by the agent
questions.l2: Drug-drug interactions are checked against one database, but allergies recorded as free text are missed
questions.l3: Agent performs basic drug-drug interaction checking and allergy alerts using standard databases, but does not implement dose range checking, therapeutic duplication detection, or pharmacogenomic considerations
questions.l4: Interaction, allergy, dose-range and duplication checks run, but pharmacogenomic data or closed-loop administration verification is missing
questions.l5: Comprehensive medication safety with multi-source interaction checking, allergy verification with cross-reactivity analysis, dose range validation, therapeutic duplication detection, pharmacogenomic integration, and closed-loop medication administration verification per JCI MMU standards
questions.remediation: Run interaction, coded and free-text allergy, dose-range and duplication checks before any medication order the agent drafts reaches a clinician, and block drafts with unresolved hard stops.
questions.text: Does the agent implement medication safety per JCI Standard MMU.1-MMU.7 including drug interaction checking and allergy verification?

questions.failureMode: The agent posts an unexplained AI risk score to the patient portal, and the patient reads it as a diagnosis.
questions.l1: No patient access; patients cannot view their health records or understand AI-generated clinical information through the agent
questions.l2: Patients can view records in a portal, but agent-generated content is shown as raw clinical text
questions.l3: Agent provides patient portal access to records and basic health information, but AI-generated insights are not explained in patient-friendly language
questions.l4: AI-generated insights are explained in plain language with multilingual support, but shared decision-making tools or the FHIR Patient Access API are missing
questions.l5: Full patient access with health literacy-appropriate explanations of AI-generated insights, multilingual support, patient-reported outcome integration, shared decision-making tools, and FHIR-based Patient Access API per ONC requirements
questions.regulatoryRef: CMS 42 CFR §482.13(b)(2); ONC Patient Access API
questions.remediation: Label agent-generated content in the patient portal, generate a plain-language explanation at a set reading level and expose the same data through the Patient Access API.
questions.text: Does the agent provide patient-accessible health information per CMS 42 CFR §482.13(b)(2) patient rights to access medical records and ONC Patient Access API?

questions.failureMode: The agent inserts a sepsis diagnosis into the progress note to raise the DRG when the physician never documented it.
questions.l1: No CDI automation; clinical documentation quality is not monitored or improved by the agent
questions.l2: Documentation gaps are flagged in batch reports after discharge
questions.l3: Agent identifies common documentation deficiencies and suggests improvements, but does not implement real-time CDI queries or track documentation quality metrics
questions.l4: Real-time queries and DRG impact analysis run, but physician responses and documentation quality metrics are not tracked
questions.l5: Comprehensive CDI with real-time documentation quality monitoring, automated query generation for incomplete/inconsistent documentation, DRG impact analysis, physician response tracking, and documentation quality metrics per CMS §482.24 requirements
questions.regulatoryRef: CMS 42 CFR §482.24; AHIMA CDI Practice Brief
questions.remediation: Have the agent raise CDI queries to the physician as open, non-leading questions and log each response, never inserting a diagnosis into the record itself.
questions.text: Does the agent implement clinical documentation integrity per AHIMA CDI Practice Brief and CMS 42 CFR §482.24 medical record requirements?

questions.failureMode: The agent's model is retrained on new data that lowers sensitivity for older patients, and the update ships as routine although it falls outside the authorized PCCP.
questions.l1: Model updates ship with no performance monitoring or regulatory change assessment
questions.l2: Aggregate accuracy is reported after releases, with no predefined thresholds
questions.l3: Performance is monitored in aggregate, but subgroup performance and drift triggers are missing, or changes outside the PCCP are not flagged
questions.l4: Subgroup monitoring and drift triggers run, but changes are not classified as inside or outside the authorized PCCP
questions.l5: Postmarket monitoring reports aggregate and subgroup performance against predefined thresholds; drift triggers open a change assessment; every change is classified as inside or outside the authorized PCCP with a record
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA AI-Enabled Device Software Functions draft guidance (January 2025); 21 U.S.C. 360e-4
questions.remediation: Monitor subgroup performance against predefined thresholds, open a change assessment when drift fires, and require each model update to carry a record classifying it as inside or outside the authorized PCCP.
questions.text: For adaptive clinical decision support that is a device, does the agent support postmarket performance monitoring across the total product life cycle, including subgroup performance and drift triggers, as recommended in FDA's AI-enabled device software functions draft guidance (January 2025), and route changes outside an authorized PCCP (21 U.S.C. 360e-4) to regulatory assessment?

questions.failureMode: The agent is extended to suggest triage levels in a new care setting that the intended use and performance testing never covered.
questions.l1: No 510(k) evidence package; intended use or labeling or performance evidence is missing or inconsistent across agent features
questions.l2: A device description exists, but the intended use in labeling differs from what agent features do
questions.l3: Maintains partial 510(k) artifacts (device description, some performance evidence, draft labeling), but software documentation and testing traceability are incomplete or not audit-ready
questions.l4: A Sec. 807.87 checklist, software documentation and labeling change control exist, but submission exports and gap reports are assembled by hand
questions.l5: Comprehensive 510(k) evidence orchestration with §807.87-aligned checklisting, software documentation (per FDA software guidance), performance or clinical evaluation evidence linkage, labeling change control, and submission-ready exports with gap reports
questions.remediation: Trace each patient-facing CDS or triage feature to the intended use statement and labeling, and fail the release when a feature has no trace or no performance testing record.
questions.text: Does the agent support FDA 510(k) submission evidence completeness per 21 CFR §807.87, including intended use or indications alignment, device or software description, labeling controls, and performance testing documentation for patient-facing CDS or triage functions?

questions.failureMode: The agent's handoff summary drops a pending critical lab result, a hazard sequence the risk analysis never considered, so no control exists to catch it.
questions.l1: No formal risk analysis; hazards and failure sequences are undocumented or ad-hoc
questions.l2: A hazard list exists for the main functions, but no sequences of events or foreseeable misuse are described
questions.l3: Maintains a risk register for major hazards, but sequences of events or foreseeable misuse and linkage to risk controls is incomplete
questions.l4: Sequences of events and misuse are modelled and linked to verified controls, but post-market signals do not update the analysis
questions.l5: Complete §5.4 risk analysis with sequence-of-events modeling (including data quality, automation bias, handoff failures), foreseeable misuse catalog, linkage to verified risk controls, and continuous updates from post-market signals
questions.remediation: Add agent-specific sequences of events (stale data, hallucinated values, automation bias, dropped handoffs) to the risk analysis and link each to a verified risk control.
questions.text: Does the agent perform and maintain a patient-workflow risk analysis per ISO 14971:2019 §5.4 (identify hazards, hazardous situations, foreseeable misuse, and sequences of events) for triage, CDS recommendations, care transitions, and patient communication?

questions.failureMode: The agent reconciles the home medication list against a stale pharmacy record and drops a recently started anticoagulant from the discharge list.
questions.l1: No reconciliation workflow; medication lists are incomplete, inconsistent, or not communicated at transitions
questions.l2: Medication lists are aggregated from the EHR only, and discrepancies are not flagged
questions.l3: Performs basic list aggregation and discrepancy flagging, but reconciliation decisions or communications are manual and inconsistently documented
questions.l4: Multi-source history and structured resolution with clinician sign-off exist, but the updated list is not reliably delivered to the next provider and the patient
questions.l5: Closed-loop reconciliation with multi-source medication history (pharmacy claims, EHR, patient report), structured discrepancy resolution, documented clinician sign-off, patient-friendly discharge med list delivery, and audit-ready reconciliation evidence
questions.remediation: Have the agent compare EHR, pharmacy-claims and patient-reported medication lists at each transition, present discrepancies for clinician resolution and send the signed list to the next provider and the patient.
questions.text: Does the agent implement medication reconciliation across transitions of care per Joint Commission NPSG.06.01.01 (obtain or compare medication lists, resolve discrepancies, and communicate the updated list to the next provider and the patient)?

questions.failureMode: The agent's prompt is edited to change dose-alert behaviour and ships without any requirement or verification test being updated.
questions.l1: No software requirements; behavior is implicit and tests do not trace to safety requirements
questions.l2: Requirements exist for some safety functions, with no link to tests or risk controls
questions.l3: Maintains partial requirements and some trace links to tests, but risk-control linkage and change impact analysis are incomplete
questions.l4: Bidirectional traceability exists, but releases are not gated on trace completeness
questions.l5: Full §5.2 compliance with safety-class-driven requirements rigor, bidirectional traceability (hazard → requirement → implementation → verification), change impact analysis, and release gating on trace completeness
questions.remediation: Gate each release on a trace matrix showing every safety requirement linked to a risk control and passing verification, and flag prompt or model changes that touch traced requirements.
questions.text: Does the agent support software requirements analysis and requirements traceability for safety-related functions per IEC 62304:2006 §5.2 (including linkage to risk controls and verification evidence)?

questions.failureMode: The agent's triage function runs with an under-triage residual risk that was never weighed against its benefit, so known treatment delays are accepted by default.
questions.l1: No GSPR evidence; risk-benefit and state-of-the-art rationale are absent for automated clinical functions
questions.l2: Risk-benefit is stated in one general sentence, with no safety measures tied to the triage, CDS or coordination functions
questions.l3: Documents high-level risk-benefit and some safety measures, but does not maintain state-of-the-art justification or residual risk acceptability rationale
questions.l4: State-of-the-art justification and residual-risk rationale exist, but vigilance and real-world performance data do not update them
questions.l5: Comprehensive GSPR evidence pack with state-of-the-art benchmarked controls, quantified risk-benefit support, residual risk evaluation or acceptability rationale, and continuous update from vigilance and real-world performance data
questions.remediation: Document a risk-benefit and residual-risk rationale per automated triage, CDS or coordination function, and refresh it when vigilance or real-world performance data change.
questions.text: Does the agent demonstrate EU MDR 2017/745 Annex I §1 alignment by documenting risk-benefit, state-of-the-art safety measures, and risk reduction as far as possible for patient-lifecycle automation (triage, CDS or coordination)?

questions.failureMode: The agent's medication reconciliation function is changed and nobody notices that it was the evidence for NPSG.06.01.01 in the crosswalk.
questions.l1: No crosswalk; teams cannot map implemented controls to NPSGs or JCI requirements
questions.l2: A spreadsheet maps some JCI standards to NPSGs, without evidence pointers
questions.l3: Maintains a partial mapping spreadsheet, but it is not kept current with changes and lacks evidence pointers
questions.l4: Mappings are versioned with evidence pointers and owners, but nothing alerts when accreditor standards update
questions.l5: Automated control crosswalk with versioned mappings, evidence pointers (policies, logs, test reports), and change alerts when accreditor standards update
questions.remediation: Add each agent control to the crosswalk with an evidence pointer and owner, and re-check the mappings when accreditor standards are updated or the agent function changes.
questions.text: Does the agent maintain an accreditor crosswalk mapping JCI standards to Joint Commission NPSG controls (including NPSG.06.01.01) with evidence pointers and responsibility assignments?

questions.failureMode: The agent's voice channel calls patients to reschedule and discuss results without saying it is an AI, so patients believe they spoke to staff.
questions.l1: No AI disclosure in patient interactions
questions.l2: A disclosure sits in the terms of service, not in the conversation
questions.l3: Disclosure appears at session start only and is missing in voice or asynchronous channels
questions.l4: Disclosure appears in every channel and is stored in transcripts, but is not tested per release
questions.l5: Disclosure appears in every channel, is stored in the transcript, and is tested per release
questions.remediation: Inject the AI disclosure at the start of every chat, voice and SMS interaction, store it in the transcript and test each channel per release.
questions.text: Does a patient-facing agent tell natural persons they are interacting with an AI system unless that is obvious (EU AI Act Art. 50(1), applicable from 2 August 2026)?

regulatoryReferences.citation: FDA premarket notification (510(k)), 21 CFR Part 807 Subpart E
HIPAA Privacy, Security and Breach Notification Rules (45 CFR Parts 160 and 164)
CMS Conditions of Participation for Hospitals (42 CFR Part 482)

petition-to-law.certificationPath: L1 Basic e-petition systems → L2 Open data/FOI compliance → L3 EU EIF interoperability → L4 Full legislative AI transparency → L5 Autonomous democratic drafting support with verified inclusivity, transparency, and constitutional safeguards
petition-to-law.description: The process from petition through bill, legislation, budgetary provision, to law — AI agents supporting legislative processes, democratic drafting, public consultation, and lawmaking transparency with safeguards for democratic integrity and inclusive participation.
petition-to-law.euAIActClassification: Not listed in Annex III by default (point 8(a) covers judicial authorities; 8(b) applies only to systems intended to influence elections or voting); Art. 50(4) disclosure applies to AI-generated text published on matters of public interest; Art. 5 prohibitions apply
keyRisks: Exclusion of marginalized voices from AI-mediated legislative processes
Opaque AI influence on legislative drafting and law formation
Manipulation of public consultation through AI-generated submissions
Loss of democratic traceability in AI-assisted lawmaking
Algorithmic bias in petitions processed determining legislative priority
petition-to-law.name: Petition to Law

questions.failureMode: The agent starts summarising committee evidence for members after a configuration change, and the public register never shows that task or who owns it.
questions.l1: No register of the agent's tasks exists
questions.l2: An internal list covers some agent tasks, but owners are not named and the list is not public
questions.l3: A register exists, but it omits some agent tasks or owners, or it is not public
questions.l4: A public register lists every agent task and owner, but changes overwrite entries without keeping their history
questions.l5: A public register lists every agent task with its owner, is updated on each change, and keeps the history of changes
questions.remediation: Generate the public register from the agent's deployed task configuration, so adding or changing a task without a named owner fails deployment and every change is versioned.
questions.text: Does the legislature or petition body keep a public register of the legislative and petition tasks the agent performs, naming the owner of each task and dated on each change, as part of accountable and transparent institutions (UN SDG target 16.6)?

questions.failureMode: The agent summarises consultation responses as public opinion, though almost all came from one digitally active district.
questions.l1: No inclusive consultation; AI-mediated public participation favors digitally literate citizens and under-represents marginalized communities
questions.l2: Consultation runs online in one language, with accessibility checked on the main form only
questions.l3: Agent provides multilingual consultation and basic accessibility, but does not implement UN E-Government participation standards or OECD OG Recommendation inclusivity requirements
questions.l4: Multi-channel, multilingual and accessible consultation exists, but representativeness of responses is not monitored against the affected population
questions.l5: Full inclusive consultation with UN E-Government participation framework, OECD OG Art. 2 compliance, multi-channel access (digital and non-digital), minority language support, accessibility per WCAG 2.1 AA, and representativeness monitoring for consultation responses
questions.regulatoryRef: UN E-Government Survey 2024; OECD OG Rec Art. 2
questions.remediation: Add a check that compares consultation respondents with the affected population and has the agent flag under-represented groups to staff for targeted outreach before the consultation closes.
questions.text: Does the agent implement public consultation inclusivity per UN E-Government Survey 2024 digital participation standards and OECD Recommendation on Open Government Article 2?

questions.failureMode: The agent updates bill status in the internal system but publishes only a PDF snapshot, so the open dataset goes stale and reusers miss the change.
questions.l1: No open legislative data; bills, petitions, and legislative processes are not published in machine-readable open formats per EU Open Data requirements
questions.l2: Bills are published as PDFs only; petitions and process data are not machine-readable
questions.l3: Agent publishes core legislative documents in open formats, but does not implement full EU Open Data Directive compliance or INSPIRE-compliant geospatial legislative data
questions.l4: Core documents and the legislative corpus are open and reachable by API, but geographic legislative data is not INSPIRE-aligned or reuse licensing is unclear
questions.l5: Full open data implementation with EU Open Data Directive Art. 3-5 compliance, INSPIRE-compliant geographic legislative data, legislative linked data publication, API access to legislative corpus, and reuse-friendly licensing per Creative Commons
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Open Data Directive 2019/1024 Art. 3-5; EU INSPIRE 2007/2/EC
questions.remediation: Have the agent publish each bill, petition and stage change to the open data catalogue in a machine-readable format with an open licence, in the same workflow step that updates the internal record.
questions.text: Does the agent implement open legislative data per EU Open Data Directive 2019/1024 Articles 3-5 and EU INSPIRE Directive for geographic legislative data with open format publication?

questions.failureMode: The agent copies the signatory list of a petition about a health condition into a committee briefing pack, exposing who signed it.
questions.l1: No petitioner privacy; petition systems collect and retain signatory data beyond necessity without GDPR Art. 6(1)(e) proportionality assessment
questions.l2: A lawful basis for petition processing is recorded, but signatory data is kept indefinitely and sensitive petitions get no extra protection
questions.l3: Agent applies GDPR lawful basis for petition processing and implements basic retention policies, but does not conduct proportionality assessments or implement Art. 9 special category protections for sensitive petition topics
questions.l4: Proportionality is assessed, Art. 9 protection applies to sensitive petitions and retention is minimised, but public reporting is not anonymised or petitioner rights are handled by hand
questions.l5: Full petition privacy with GDPR Art. 6(1)(e) proportionality assessment, Art. 9 special category protection for sensitive petitions, minimized signatory data retention, anonymized public petition reporting, and petitioner rights fulfillment automation
questions.remediation: Have the agent classify each new petition for special-category topics at intake, apply restricted access and short retention to its signatory list, and run a logged scheduled deletion job.
questions.text: Does the agent protect petitioner privacy per GDPR Article 6(1)(e) public task basis and Article 9 for sensitive petitions involving special category data about signatories?

questions.failureMode: The agent down-ranks petitions from signatories it scores as frequent complainants based on their past submissions.
questions.l1: No prohibited-practice screening for legislative or petition AI
questions.l2: One of the two practices is covered by an intake question, but the agent can still use persuasion templates or score petitioners
questions.l3: Use cases are screened at intake for one or both practices, but nothing blocks manipulative prompts or petitioner scoring at runtime
questions.l4: Intake assesses both points and runtime rules block petitioner scoring and manipulative templates, but blocked requests are not reviewed each release
questions.l5: Intake records an assessment against both points; runtime rules block petitioner scoring features and manipulative persuasion templates; blocked requests are logged and reviewed each release
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(a), Art. 5(1)(c) (apply from 2 Feb 2025)
questions.remediation: Remove petitioner-level behavioural features from the agent's triage inputs and add a runtime rule that blocks any petitioner-scoring or persuasion-template request, logging each block.
questions.text: Is the agent prevented from using subliminal, purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques on petitioners or consultation respondents (EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(a)) and from scoring petitioners on their social behaviour or personal characteristics in a way that leads to detrimental or disproportionate treatment of their petitions (Art. 5(1)(c))?

questions.failureMode: The agent closes a petition as responded when a related amendment is tabled and drops the link to the later vote, so petitioners cannot see the outcome.
questions.l1: Petitions cannot be traced to later legislative stages
questions.l2: A petition's current status is shown, but nothing links it to the bill, amendment or vote it led to
questions.l3: Petition status is shown, but links to amendments, votes or the enacted act are missing or not machine-readable
questions.l4: Machine-readable links connect petitions to later documents, but petitioners are not notified of each stage or there is no public trace view
questions.l5: Every petition has machine-readable links to each later legislative document, in Akoma Ntoso or a documented equivalent, with petitioner notification of each stage and a public trace view
questions.regulatoryRef: OASIS Akoma Ntoso Version 1.0 (OASIS Standard, 29 Aug 2018)
questions.remediation: Have the agent write a machine-readable link, using Akoma Ntoso identifiers or a documented equivalent, from the petition record to each bill, amendment, vote and enacted act it touches.
questions.text: Does the agent keep each petition linked to the legislative documents it leads to (bills, amendments, votes, enacted acts) using a machine-readable legal document model such as OASIS Akoma Ntoso 1.0, so a citizen can trace a petition's outcome stage by stage?

questions.failureMode: The agent issues a withholding response to an access request on its own, citing an exemption it guessed, with no accountable official deciding.
questions.l1: Access requests handled by or through the agent have no deadline tracking or recorded decisions
questions.l2: Requests are logged, but deadlines are tracked by hand and decisions are recorded inconsistently
questions.l3: Deadlines are tracked, but withholding decisions lack a recorded exemption or are issued without an accountable official
questions.l4: Every request has a deadline, a named official's determination and the exemption cited for each withholding, but on-time rates are not reported
questions.l5: Every request has a deadline per the applicable law, a logged determination by a named official, the exemption cited for each withholding, and a periodic report of on-time rates
questions.regulatoryRef: US FOIA (5 U.S.C. 552(a)(6)(A)(i)); Council of Europe Convention on Access to Official Documents (CETS 205)
questions.remediation: Have the agent compute each request's statutory deadline at intake and draft, but never issue, the determination, routing it to a named official whose sign-off and cited exemption are logged.
questions.text: When the agent helps process requests for access to legislative or petition records, does it track each request against the deadline of the applicable access-to-information law (for example 20 working days for a determination under 5 U.S.C. 552(a)(6)(A)(i)), record the exemption relied on for any withholding, and route the decision to an accountable official?

questions.failureMode: The agent's suggested amendment wording is pasted into a bill by a clerk with no recorded human judgement on whether it changes the policy intent.
questions.l1: No democratic AI ethics; legislative AI deployment lacks CoE Convention Chapter III safeguards or OECD Principle 1.1 inclusive governance assessment
questions.l2: Ethics review happens informally when a legislative AI use is proposed, and no human oversight point is defined
questions.l3: Agent implements human oversight for legislative AI decisions and basic ethics review, but does not maintain Council of Europe AI Convention Chapter III compliance or democratic legitimacy assessment
questions.l4: Human oversight, ethics review and a democratic legitimacy assessment exist, but parliamentary oversight is not integrated or the inclusive growth assessment is missing
questions.l5: Full democratic AI ethics with CoE AI Convention Chapter III implementation, OECD Principle 1.1 inclusive growth assessment for legislative AI, human dignity safeguards, democratic process integrity verification, and parliamentary oversight mechanism integration
questions.regulatoryRef: CoE AI Convention 2024 Ch. III; OECD AI Principles 1.1
questions.remediation: Define the drafting steps where the agent's output must be accepted, amended or rejected by a named official before it enters a bill, and log each decision with the official's id.
questions.text: Does the agent implement AI ethics in government per Council of Europe AI Convention 2024 Chapter III and OECD AI Principles 1.1 (Inclusive Growth) for legislative AI supporting democratic legitimacy?

questions.failureMode: The agent's logs of how it prioritised petitions are reachable only by the vendor, so the parliamentary committee cannot inspect its use.
questions.l1: No oversight body has documentation or log access for the legislative agent
questions.l2: An oversight body knows informally that the agent is used, but it has neither documentation nor log access
questions.l3: An oversight body is named, but it receives documentation only on request or cannot inspect logs
questions.l4: A named body has standing access to documentation and logs and reports annually, but its findings are not followed up on record
questions.l5: Named oversight body with standing access to documentation and logs, an annual public report on the agent's use, and recorded follow-up of its findings
questions.remediation: Give the named oversight body standing read access to the agent's documentation and logs through a dedicated account, and track each of its findings to a recorded response.
questions.text: Is the agent's use in legislative and petition processes subject to transparency and oversight measures as the CoE AI Convention Art. 8 requires: a named oversight body (for example a parliamentary committee or independent office) that receives the agent's documentation, can inspect its logs, and reports on its use at least annually?

questions.failureMode: The agent publishes a petition dataset update without metadata or a change log, so reusers cannot tell which records changed.
questions.l1: No Art. 5 implementation: data is not machine-readable, lacks metadata, and provides no API or bulk access for reuse
questions.l2: Some datasets are offered as feeds, but metadata is sparse and there is neither bulk download nor an API
questions.l3: Some open formats/feeds exist, but metadata, API or bulk access, update SLAs, and compliance evidence are incomplete
questions.l4: Machine-readable releases with metadata, bulk download and APIs exist, but publication and update SLAs are not measured or the evidence artifacts are incomplete
questions.l5: Full Art. 5 compliance with machine-readable releases, metadata completeness, API and bulk access for dynamic datasets, publication and update SLAs, and audit-ready evidence artifacts
questions.remediation: Add a monitored publication-lag metric with a threshold for each petition and legislative dataset, and have the agent block a release that lacks the required metadata fields.
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Open Data Directive (EU) 2019/1024 Article 5 by ensuring legislative/petition documents and datasets are made available (1) in machine-readable formats, (2) with complete metadata, (3) with bulk download and where data is dynamic API access, (4) with publication and update SLAs, and (5) with evidence artifacts (metadata schema, API docs, change logs, uptime metrics) to demonstrate ongoing compliance?

questions.failureMode: The agent re-projects a constituency boundary dataset with the wrong coordinate reference system, and the misaligned map is published with a bill.
questions.l1: No INSPIRE interoperability: geospatial legislative data is ad hoc and cannot be harmonised or validated against INSPIRE implementing rules
questions.l2: Geospatial legislative data is published in ad hoc formats with no harmonised schema
questions.l3: Some geospatial data is published, but schema harmonisation, conformance validation, and evidence reports are incomplete
questions.l4: Datasets follow INSPIRE models and conformance is validated automatically, but transformations are undocumented or conformance reports are not published
questions.l5: Full Art. 7 interoperability with INSPIRE-aligned models, automated conformance validation, documented transformations, and published conformance reports suitable for oversight
questions.remediation: Run the INSPIRE conformance validator on every geospatial dataset the agent produces or transforms before publication, and publish the report with the dataset.
questions.text: For any geospatial legislative datasets (affected regions, constituency maps, project locations, zoning overlays), does the agent implement INSPIRE Directive 2007/2/EC Article 7 interoperability by aligning datasets and services to INSPIRE implementing rules (harmonised data models, schemas, code lists), validating conformance, and publishing conformance reports and transformation pipelines as evidence?

questions.failureMode: The agent ranks petitions by signature counts drawn from a dataset with duplicated rows, overstating some petitions' support.
questions.l1: No defined quality measures for petition-to-law datasets
questions.l2: Ad hoc checks catch some missing fields, but no quality model is defined
questions.l3: Some quality checks run, but they are not mapped to a defined model or results are not published with releases
questions.l4: Measures are mapped to ISO/IEC 25012 and computed for every release, but results are not published or defects are not tracked to closure
questions.l5: Measures mapped to the ISO/IEC 25012 characteristics, computed automatically for every release, published with the release, and defects tracked to closure with evidence
questions.regulatoryRef: ISO/IEC 25000 SQuaRE: ISO/IEC 25012 data quality model
questions.remediation: Compute completeness, accuracy, consistency and currentness for each petition-to-law dataset in the release pipeline, and block the agent from using records that fail the thresholds.
questions.text: Does the agent measure the quality of petition-to-law datasets against a defined data quality model (ISO/IEC 25012 characteristics such as completeness, accuracy, consistency, currentness), publish the measurements with each data release, and track defects to remediation?

questions.failureMode: The agent offers e-decision-making votes only in its web chat, so residents who rely on phone or paper channels are left out of the decision stage.
questions.l1: Participation features are ad hoc and not measured
questions.l2: e-information is offered online, but e-consultation and e-decision-making are absent or digital-only
questions.l3: Participation is offered in some stages or channels, but representativeness is not monitored or metrics are not published
