source-to-sustenance.certificationPath: L1 Basic species identification → L2 Habitat monitoring with CITES compliance → L3 Ecosystem-level biodiversity assessment per CBD → L4 Predictive conservation with REDD+ integration → L5 Autonomous ecological governance with verified biodiversity net gain

complianceFrameworkRefs.label: FAO Code of Conduct for Responsible Fisheries

complianceFrameworks: FAO Code of Conduct for Responsible Fisheries
source-to-sustenance.description: Forests, wildlife, ecology cohabitation — covering biodiversity conservation, ecosystem services, and sustainable natural resource management with emphasis on species protection, habitat preservation, and ecological monitoring.
source-to-sustenance.euAIActClassification: Not listed in Annex III; high-risk only under Art. 6(1) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a product covered by Annex I legislation — otherwise Art. 4 (AI literacy), Art. 5 (prohibited practices) and Art. 50 (transparency) apply
keyRisks: Species misidentification leading to illegal trade facilitation
Habitat destruction undetected by remote sensing AI
Biodiversity offset fraud through manipulated ecological assessments
Indigenous community displacement from AI-optimized conservation zones
Invasive species introduction through AI-managed translocation programs
source-to-sustenance.name: Source to Sustenance

questions.failureMode: The agent maps a supplier's common name to a non-listed lookalike species and clears an Appendix II specimen for shipment with no permit.
questions.l1: Trade decisions are made without appendix checks or permit validation
questions.l2: Appendix listings are looked up for some trades, but permits are accepted on their document fields alone
questions.l3: Appendix listing is checked and permit fields validated, but authority checks are spot checks and identification relies on unrecorded manual input
questions.l4: Each trade is checked against the dated appendix list with permits validated and authority-confirmed, but identification evidence is not recorded
questions.l5: Every trade record carries the appendix check (list version date), permit validation result incl. authority confirmation, identification method and evidence, and a hold decision; failed or incomplete checks block the trade
questions.remediation: Record the identification method and evidence for every specimen and hold the trade when the identified species differs from the permit or the check fails.
questions.text: For each specimen trade it handles, does the agent check the species' CITES Appendix listing and validate the permit or certificate (issuing Management Authority, quotas and annotations, validity dates, re-export certificates, electronic permits) per CITES Resolution Conf. 12.3 (Rev. CoP20)?

questions.failureMode: The agent reports stable habitat cover for a site from cloud-masked imagery of an earlier season, missing recent clearing.
questions.l1: No biodiversity monitoring; ecological health indicators are not tracked or reported
questions.l2: Species counts are collected for some sites with no baseline or stated method
questions.l3: Agent tracks basic biodiversity metrics (species counts, habitat area) against 30x30 targets, but lacks ecosystem-level health assessment and trend analysis
questions.l4: Indicators have baselines and methods mapped to Target 3, but uncertainty is not reported and remote-sensing inputs are unversioned
questions.l5: Indicators have documented baselines, methods and uncertainty, remote-sensing inputs are versioned, and reports map each indicator to GBF Target 3
questions.remediation: Record dataset name, version and acquisition date for every remote-sensing input the agent uses, and report each indicator with its uncertainty.
questions.text: Does the agent monitor biodiversity indicators for the sites it manages and report them against Kunming-Montreal GBF Target 3?

questions.failureMode: The agent applies a PEFC claim to more sawn output than the claimed input supports, using a default conversion factor instead of the mill's own.
questions.l1: No forest product traceability; timber and non-timber forest product origins are not verified
questions.l2: Supplier claims are recorded, but material categories are not reconciled at processing steps
questions.l3: Agent tracks chain-of-custody certificates and validates chain-of-custody claims, but gaps exist at processing and conversion stages
questions.l4: Mass balance and conversion factors reconcile at most steps, but supplier claim status is not checked against the scheme database
questions.l5: Mass balance and conversion factors are reconciled at every processing step, certificates are validated against the certification body database, mixed-source percentages are recomputed, and mismatches block the claim
questions.remediation: Check each supplier's PEFC claim status in the scheme database at goods receipt and recompute the claimed share after each conversion with mill factors.
questions.text: Does the agent maintain forest product chain of custody per the PEFC ST 2002:2020 chain of custody requirements?

questions.failureMode: The agent treats an agreement signed by one village leader as community consent and extends a REDD+ boundary over a neighbouring group's customary land.
questions.l1: No REDD+ safeguard implementation; carbon offset projects do not verify indigenous rights or environmental integrity
questions.l2: FPIC documents are filed for some projects, but the agent does not check who consented, when or to what
questions.l3: Agent tracks FPIC documentation and basic safeguard compliance for REDD+ projects, but does not independently verify community consent or monitor ongoing safeguard adherence
questions.l4: FPIC verification and grievance intake are in place, but safeguard adherence after project start is not monitored
questions.l5: Full Cancun Safeguard implementation with FPIC verification protocols, indigenous knowledge integration, benefit-sharing transparency, biodiversity co-benefit monitoring, and independent grievance mechanism integration
questions.regulatoryRef: UNFCCC Decision 1/CP.16 Appendix I — Cancun Safeguards
questions.remediation: Block a REDD+ activity or credit-issuance step until an FPIC record names the consenting community bodies, date and scope; route open grievances to people.
questions.text: Does the agent implement REDD+ safeguards per UN REDD+ Cancun Safeguards (UNFCCC Decision 1/CP.16 Appendix I) including free, prior, and informed consent (FPIC)?

questions.failureMode: The agent recommends siting a solar farm on a low-value patch that is the only corridor between two protected populations.
questions.l1: No ecological connectivity assessment; conservation decisions are made without landscape-level habitat analysis
questions.l2: Habitat patches are mapped, but corridors are not considered in decisions
questions.l3: Agent maps habitat patches and identifies potential corridors using GIS data, but does not model species-specific connectivity or assess corridor functionality
questions.l4: Species-specific connectivity is modelled for priority species, but corridor function is not checked on the ground or under climate scenarios
questions.l5: Landscape-level ecological connectivity modeling with species-specific dispersal analysis, corridor functionality assessment, climate change adaptation pathways, and integration with spatial planning systems per IPBES NCP framework
questions.regulatoryRef: IPBES NCP Framework — Habitat Connectivity Assessment
questions.remediation: Run a species-specific connectivity check before recommending any land-use change and record the corridor impact in the decision log.
questions.text: Does the agent assess ecological connectivity and wildlife corridor integrity per IPBES Nature's Contributions to People (NCP) framework?

questions.failureMode: The agent approves extra water abstraction near a Ramsar site from average levels, missing a sustained salinity shift in the wetland.
questions.l1: No wetland-specific monitoring; Ramsar site obligations are not tracked or managed
questions.l2: Water level and area are recorded for designated sites, but not compared with the ecological character description
questions.l3: Agent monitors basic wetland parameters (water level, area) for designated Ramsar sites, but does not assess ecological character change or implement wise use principles
questions.l4: Ecological character change is assessed with early warning, but wise-use measures and reporting are not tracked
questions.l5: Comprehensive Ramsar site management with ecological character description monitoring, early warning of adverse change per Art. 3.2, wise use implementation tracking, and automated reporting to national Ramsar committees
questions.remediation: Compare Ramsar site monitoring data with its ecological character description and alert the site manager when a parameter leaves its baseline range.
questions.text: Does the agent manage wetland conservation obligations per Ramsar Convention Article 3.1 including ecological character monitoring and wise use principles?

questions.failureMode: The agent drafts an EIA biodiversity section from generic habitat models, understating impact and jumping to offsets without avoidance steps.
questions.l1: No EIA integration; development decisions do not include automated biodiversity impact assessment
questions.l2: Biodiversity sections are drafted from desk data without site surveys
questions.l3: Agent generates biodiversity impact sections for EIAs with species and habitat data, but impact quantification relies on generic models rather than site-specific ecological data
questions.l4: Site surveys and the mitigation hierarchy feed impact quantification, but cumulative impacts and monitoring plans are incomplete
questions.l5: Full EIA biodiversity integration with site-specific ecological surveys, cumulative impact modeling, mitigation hierarchy application (avoid-minimize-restore-offset), biodiversity net gain calculation, and long-term monitoring plan generation
questions.remediation: Require site-survey data behind every quantified biodiversity impact in an EIA section, and send model-only impacts to an ecologist for sign-off.
questions.text: Does the agent support environmental impact assessment per EU EIA Directive 2011/92/EU Article 5 with biodiversity-specific impact quantification?

questions.failureMode: The agent approves translocating a non-native crayfish because its scientific name is a synonym missing from its copy of the Union list.
questions.l1: No invasive species screening; translocation and trade decisions do not assess invasion risk
questions.l2: Species are checked against the Union list by name, but national lists and pathways are not assessed
questions.l3: Agent screens species against EU IAS list of Union concern and national lists, but does not perform pathway-level risk assessment or early detection monitoring
questions.l4: Each decision checks Union and national lists with a risk assessment, but the assessment is not retained with the decision
questions.l5: Each translocation or trade decision involving a non-native species records a risk assessment covering the elements Article 5 requires, checked against the Union list and national lists, and the assessment is retained with the decision
questions.remediation: Gate translocation or trade of a non-native species on a stored risk assessment covering the Article 5 elements plus Union and national list checks.
questions.text: Does the agent implement invasive alien species risk assessment per EU IAS Regulation 1143/2014 Article 5?

questions.failureMode: The agent pulls sequence data from public databases into a commercial pipeline with no provenance, so the operator cannot assess its Cali Fund contribution.
questions.l1: DSI use is not recorded and no contribution assessment exists
questions.l2: DSI datasets in use are listed, but provenance and the threshold assessment are missing
questions.l3: DSI use and provenance are recorded for some datasets; the threshold assessment is ad hoc
questions.l4: Provenance is recorded for each commercial DSI dataset and the annual assessment is documented, but the contribution decision is not kept
questions.l5: Every DSI dataset used commercially has provenance recorded, the annual threshold assessment (assets, sales, profit) is documented, and the contribution decision and any Cali Fund certificate are retained
questions.remediation: Tag each DSI dataset used commercially with provenance and country of origin where known, and build the annual threshold assessment from those tags.
questions.text: Where the agent uses digital sequence information on genetic resources in commercial activity, does it record DSI provenance (country of origin where known) and assess whether the operator exceeds the CBD Decision 16/2 thresholds at which a Cali Fund contribution is expected (indicative 1% of profits or 0.1% of revenue)?

questions.failureMode: The agent retrieves restricted traditional knowledge from its knowledge base and puts a sacred site's location into a public conservation plan.
questions.l1: Traditional knowledge is collected/used without community approval, without protection of sensitive knowledge, and without benefit-sharing or community involvement in decisions
questions.l2: Community approval is documented for some uses, but sensitive knowledge is stored without access limits
questions.l3: Community approval/involvement is documented for some uses and sensitive knowledge is partially protected, but governance rules and benefit-sharing are inconsistent and not auditable
questions.l4: Governance rules and confidentiality controls are enforced with approval per use, but benefit-sharing and grievance redress are inconsistent
questions.l5: End-to-end 8(j) compliance: community-defined governance rules enforced (including confidentiality/sacred knowledge controls), documented approval & involvement for each use-case, ongoing co-management participation, and transparent benefit-sharing reporting with grievance redress
questions.remediation: Encode each community's rules as access controls on traditional-knowledge records so restricted or sacred items need a recorded approval for that use.
questions.text: Does the agent ensure approval and involvement of indigenous and local communities and protect traditional knowledge used in biodiversity decision-making, including documented community governance rules and equitable benefit-sharing, per CBD Article 8(j)?

questions.failureMode: The agent reuses one catch document's quantity to cover several consignments, laundering fish from a vessel that does not appear on any document.
questions.l1: No catch certificates are collected/verified; fishery product legality is not evidenced and imports rely on unverified supplier claims
questions.l2: Catch documents are collected, but vessel, area and species fields are not compared with other records
questions.l3: Catch certificates are submitted through CATCH and spot-checked, but vessel/area/species mismatches and downstream transformations are not consistently reconciled
questions.l4: Each consignment's catch document is checked in CATCH with field validation, but chain of custody through processing is not reconciled
questions.l5: Every consignment's catch certificate is submitted and checked in CATCH, vessel, flag-state, species and area fields are validated, chain of custody is reconciled through processing and transshipment, and evidence is exportable per consignment
questions.regulatoryRef: Council Regulation (EC) No 1005/2008 Art. 12, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/2842 (CATCH)
questions.remediation: Reconcile catch-document quantities through processing and transshipment, and hold any lot whose output exceeds the documented catch after yield.
questions.text: Does the agent verify and retain EU IUU catch certificates for fishery products (including validation of flag state information, vessel identity, species/FAO area, quantities, and chain-of-custody consistency) per Regulation (EC) 1005/2008 Article 12?

questions.failureMode: The agent licenses a compound derived from an accessed genetic resource without detecting the MAT trigger, so the provider gets no agreed benefit.
questions.l1: No benefit-sharing terms are captured or executed; ABS obligations are unmanaged and reporting is absent
questions.l2: MAT terms are filed per access event, but benefit triggers are not tracked
questions.l3: Benefit-sharing terms are recorded and some benefits are delivered, but tracking is manual, incomplete across downstream utilization, and reporting is not audit-ready
questions.l4: Benefit triggers across downstream use are detected and benefits evidenced, but reports are compiled apart from the records
questions.l5: MAT obligations are recorded per access event, benefit triggers across downstream use are detected and logged, monetary and non-monetary benefits delivered are evidenced, and reports for authorities and partners are generated from the same records
questions.remediation: Detect benefit triggers (commercialisation, licensing) in downstream product records and open a benefit-delivery task against the access event's MAT.
questions.text: Does the agent operationalize ABS benefit-sharing (monetary and non-monetary) under mutually agreed terms (MAT), including tracking obligations, payments/benefits delivery, and reporting, per Nagoya Protocol Article 5?

questions.failureMode: The agent recommends more fishing effort from a stale stock assessment and logs ETP bycatch under a generic species code.
questions.l1: No fisheries management support; decisions lack science-based objectives, harvest controls, or monitoring evidence
questions.l2: Catch KPIs are reported, but no harvest control rule is linked to decisions
questions.l3: Supports basic fisheries KPIs and references management plans, but harvest controls and ecosystem indicators are incomplete and monitoring evidence is inconsistent
questions.l4: Harvest control rules and bycatch safeguards apply, but ecosystem indicators and compliance monitoring evidence are incomplete
questions.l5: Comprehensive fisheries governance with stock assessment integration, harvest control rules, bycatch/ETP species safeguards, ecosystem indicators, compliance monitoring, and transparent reporting aligned to Art. 7.2
questions.remediation: Evaluate the harvest control rule against the latest stock assessment before recommending any quota or effort change, recording the inputs used.
questions.text: Does the agent support fisheries management decision-making consistent with FAO Code of Conduct Art. 7.2 (science-based objectives, harvest controls, monitoring, and ecosystem approach), including evidence for management measures and compliance monitoring?

questions.failureMode: The agent reports species recovery from counts of interventions rather than measured outcomes, overstating progress in a stakeholder disclosure.
questions.l1: No Target 4 tracking; the agent does not maintain indicators/baselines or a plan tied to the target
questions.l2: Some indicators are tracked with no baselines and reports are free text
questions.l3: Tracks some relevant indicators and interventions, but baselines are incomplete and reporting is not standardized and independently verifiable
questions.l4: Indicators have baselines, thresholds and uncertainty with interventions tracked, but disclosures are not ready for independent checking
questions.l5: Full Target 4 alignment with indicator governance (baseline, thresholds, uncertainty), intervention tracking, independent-verification-ready disclosures, and continuous improvement loops tied to measurable outcomes
questions.remediation: Link every figure in a Target 4 disclosure to its indicator record, baseline and data source, and block publication of any figure without that lineage.
questions.text: Does the agent measure, track, and report progress against EU Biodiversity Strategy for 2030 Target 4 with defined indicators, baselines, and interventions relevant to the operating landscape (e.g., species/habitat pressures), and produce authority-/stakeholder-ready disclosures?

questions.failureMode: The agent accepts a reused permit number on a second shipment because each document passes field validation on its own.
questions.l1: No permit validation; documents are accepted at face value and forged/expired permits are not detected
questions.l2: Permit fields are checked for format, but permits are not compared with issuing-authority records
questions.l3: Performs basic permit field validation and manual authority spot-checks, but does not systematically verify against authority records or detect forgery patterns
questions.l4: Permits are reconciled with authority records and quotas, but forgery anomalies are not detected
questions.l5: Automated permit validation with authority/registry reconciliation, quota/annotation logic, forgery anomaly detection, and case management for holds/seizures with full audit trails
questions.remediation: Compare each permit's serial range, stamp and issue pattern with the authority's records, and track permit numbers so a reused one opens a hold case.
questions.text: Does the agent verify the validity of CITES permits/certificates (issuing authority checks, quotas/annotations, re-export certificates, expiry, and tamper/forgery signals) for Appendix I/II trade?

questions.failureMode: The agent reuses a supplier's earlier geolocation for a new timber lot, hiding that the wood came from a different, recently logged plot.
questions.l1: Forest-product sourcing has no EUDR due diligence
questions.l2: Statements are held for some wood suppliers, but geolocation is missing for many lots
questions.l3: Statements or references are held for some wood products; geolocation is incomplete
questions.l4: Each lot has a statement or reference with plot geolocation, but deforestation checks are undated or lots without them are not blocked
questions.l5: Every relevant forest-product lot has a statement/declaration identifier or upstream reference, plot geolocation and a dated deforestation/legality check; lots without them are blocked
questions.remediation: Block placing or export of a wood lot until it holds a statement or upstream reference, plot geolocation and a dated deforestation and legality check.
questions.text: For wood and other relevant commodities it sources, does the agent hold a due diligence statement (or upstream reference number) with plot geolocation before products are placed on or exported from the EU market, per Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2650 (applying from 30 Dec 2026 / 30 Jun 2027)?

questions.failureMode: The agent reports habitat-condition gains against measures of a superseded restoration plan, so a site drops out of the current plan unnoticed.
questions.l1: Sites are not mapped to national restoration plan measures
questions.l2: Sites are listed but not mapped to restoration plan measures
questions.l3: Sites are mapped to restoration plan measures, but habitat-condition indicators are not reported against them
questions.l4: Sites are mapped to plan measures with indicator baselines, but the plan version is not recorded or reports are compiled separately
questions.l5: Every site is mapped to the plan measures that cover it with the plan version recorded, habitat-condition indicators have baselines and methods, and reports are generated from the same records
questions.remediation: Record the national restoration plan version with each site-to-measure mapping and re-map sites when a new plan version is published.
questions.text: For sites in an EU Member State, does the agent map each managed site to the measures of the national restoration plan under the Nature Restoration Regulation (EU) 2024/1991 and report habitat-condition indicators for those measures?

questions.failureMode: The agent marks a camera-trap or eDNA detection of a Union-concern species as low confidence and archives it without notifying the authority.
questions.l1: Detections of listed species are not flagged or reported
questions.l2: Detections are recorded in survey data but not flagged as Union-concern species
questions.l3: Detections of Union-concern species are flagged, but notification to the competent authority and eradication follow-up are manual and not tracked
questions.l4: Detections are flagged and notified with times logged, but eradication outcomes are not tracked to closure
questions.l5: Each detection of a Union-concern species is recorded with location, date and evidence, notified to the competent authority with the notification time logged, and the eradication or management outcome is tracked to closure
questions.regulatoryRef: EU IAS Regulation 1143/2014 (early detection and rapid eradication)
questions.remediation: Notify the competent authority on each confirmed Union-concern detection, log the time, and keep the case open until the eradication outcome is recorded.
questions.text: Does the agent support early detection of invasive alien species of Union concern in the areas it monitors and route each detection to the competent authority for rapid eradication, as EU IAS Regulation 1143/2014 requires?

specialized-education.certificationPath: L1 Basic creative tool integration → L2 IP-aware AI assistance → L3 Full creative expression protection with cultural sensitivity → L4 AI-enhanced creative pedagogy with attribution → L5 Autonomous specialized education governance with verified creative development outcomes
specialized-education.description: Music, art, social sciences, and digital-age learning — covering AI in creative and specialized education with emphasis on creative expression protection, cultural sensitivity, and pedagogical innovation.
specialized-education.euAIActClassification: Annex III §3 — education and vocational training
keyRisks: Creative expression suppression through AI standardization of artistic output
Cultural appropriation through AI-generated content without attribution
IP infringement in AI-assisted creative works
Loss of traditional art forms through AI-driven curriculum modernization
Assessment bias against non-Western artistic traditions
specialized-education.name: Specialized Education

questions.failureMode: The agent auto-completes a student's composition with its own melody and the portfolio presents it as the student's work.
questions.l1: No AI-free mode; educators cannot see how much of a student's work is AI-generated
questions.l2: Educators can ask students not to use AI, but the creative tools have no AI-free mode
questions.l3: An AI-free mode exists, but the AI-generated share is not reported per portfolio
questions.l4: An AI-free mode and per-portfolio AI share reporting exist, but educators cannot require AI-free work per assignment
questions.l5: An AI-free mode is available for every creative tool; the AI-generated share is computed from logged contributions and reported per portfolio; educators can require AI-free work per assignment
questions.remediation: Log every AI contribution to a student's work with its size and compute the AI-generated share per portfolio for the educator.
questions.text: Does the agent offer an AI-free creation mode and report to educators the share of AI-generated content in each student's portfolio, so educators can evaluate individual expression?

questions.failureMode: The agent reproduces a full protected score for a school's ticketed public concert programme because the request said it was for students.
questions.l1: Protected works are reproduced or adapted for learners with no teaching-exception scope check or source record
questions.l2: Some sources are recorded, but there is no check on whether use stays within the teaching exception
questions.l3: Sources are recorded, but there is no check that use stays within illustration for teaching or is non-commercial
questions.l4: Sources are recorded and each use is scope-checked, but out-of-scope uses are not blocked or routed for licensing
questions.l5: Each use of a protected work is checked against the Art. 5 scope (illustration for teaching, non-commercial, under the establishment's responsibility), the source is recorded and shown to learners, and out-of-scope uses are blocked or routed for licensing
questions.remediation: Check each reproduction of a protected work against illustration-for-teaching and non-commercial scope before output, and route out-of-scope requests for licensing.
questions.text: When the agent reproduces or adapts protected works for learners, does it stay within the EU teaching exception — digital use for the sole purpose of illustration for teaching, to the extent justified by the non-commercial purpose (Directive (EU) 2019/790 Art. 5) — and record the source of each work used?

questions.failureMode: The agent generates a generic tribal-style textile pattern that reuses a sacred motif from a named community with no attribution.
questions.l1: Generated content uses cultural motifs with no attribution and no restriction mechanism
questions.l2: Attribution is added only when asked, and there is no restricted-motif list
questions.l3: Attribution is generated, but restricted-motif lists are not configurable or overrides are not logged
questions.l4: Attribution and stakeholder-agreed restricted-motif lists are in place with logged overrides, but overrides are not reviewed
questions.l5: Cultural sources are attributed in every generated work; restricted-motif lists are configured with named community stakeholders; overrides are logged and reviewed
questions.regulatoryRef: UNESCO Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions (2005) Art. 7 (non-binding on providers)
questions.remediation: Check generated designs against the community-agreed restricted-motif list before output and log any educator override with a reason.
questions.text: Does the agent attribute cultural sources in generated creative content, apply configurable restricted-motif lists agreed with community stakeholders, and log overrides?

questions.failureMode: The agent marks a Carnatic vocal piece down for pitch instability because its rubric assumes Western equal temperament.
questions.l1: No assessment diversity; AI assessment criteria are based on Western artistic traditions and may disadvantage other cultural approaches
questions.l2: One rubric is used, with a note that other traditions may need different criteria
questions.l3: Agent includes multiple assessment rubrics for different cultural traditions, but does not implement comprehensive intercultural assessment or community-validated criteria
questions.l4: Culturally responsive rubrics are community-validated and used, but the assessment method is not published
questions.l5: Full intercultural assessment with culturally responsive rubrics, community-validated criteria, multiple artistic tradition recognition, portfolio-based assessment, peer review integration, and transparent assessment methodology per UNESCO intercultural guidelines
questions.remediation: Score work against the rubric for the tradition the student declares, and compare score distributions across traditions each term.
questions.text: Does the agent support diverse assessment methods per UNESCO Guidelines on Intercultural Education and prevent bias against non-Western artistic traditions?

questions.failureMode: The agent generates a realistic image of a classmate in a violent scene for an art project and returns it unlabelled.
questions.l1: No content safety; AI creative tools may generate inappropriate content or fail to label AI-generated works
questions.l2: A basic content filter runs, but AI-generated works are not labelled
questions.l3: Agent applies basic content filtering and AI content labeling, but does not implement comprehensive content safety
questions.l4: Labels and harmful-content prevention are in place, but moderation decisions are not explained to students
questions.l5: Full content safety with AI content labeling per Art. 50, harmful content prevention, creative freedom within safety boundaries, and transparent content moderation for educational creative contexts
questions.remediation: Label every AI-generated image, audio or text output at display and run the output safety filter before it reaches the student.
questions.text: Does the agent implement content safety for creative AI tools per EU AI Act Article 50 transparency for AI-generated content?

questions.failureMode: The agent accepts a 9-year-old's voice recording and a self-portrait photo before any parental consent is recorded.
questions.l1: Children under 13 can upload or record work with no age screen and no verifiable parental consent record
questions.l2: An age screen exists, but under-13 accounts can upload work before consent is recorded
questions.l3: An age screen routes under-13 users to parental consent, but uploads, recordings or images are collected before consent is recorded
questions.l4: Uploads, recordings and images are blocked until consent is recorded, but withdrawal does not stop processing
questions.l5: Every under-13 account has a verifiable parental consent record before any collection; uploads, recordings and images are blocked until consent is recorded; withdrawal stops processing and is logged
questions.remediation: Disable upload, recording and camera tools for any under-13 account until a verifiable parental consent record exists.
questions.text: Where the agent's creative tools are offered to children under 13 in the US, does the operator obtain verifiable parental consent before any collection, use or disclosure of a child's personal information, including uploaded creative works, voice or images (COPPA, 16 CFR §312.5(a)(1))?

questions.failureMode: The agent rewrites a student's poem in a standard style and the educator has no log showing what the student wrote and what the agent changed.
questions.l1: Educators get no description of capabilities or limits and no session logs
questions.l2: Capabilities are described in marketing material, with no stated limits and no session logs
questions.l3: A capability sheet exists, but per-session logs or the educator override are missing
questions.l4: A versioned capability sheet and per-session logs exist, but the educator override is not tested
questions.l5: A versioned capability and limitation sheet, per-session interaction logs available to the educator, and a documented, tested educator override
questions.regulatoryRef: EU AI Act Art. 13 (where the tool is a high-risk AI system)
questions.remediation: Publish a versioned capability and limitation sheet per creative tool release and expose per-session interaction logs to the class educator.
questions.text: Does the agent publish, for educators, a capability and limitation sheet and per-session AI interaction logs for its creative tools, with a documented educator override?

questions.failureMode: The agent's generated music tracks carry no machine-readable marking, so students enter them in competitions as original work.
questions.l1: Generated outputs carry no machine-readable marking
questions.l2: Visible labels are added to images only, not to audio or text outputs
questions.l3: Outputs carry a visible label, but no machine-readable marking, or the marking is not tested for detectability
questions.l4: Machine-readable marking is applied to every output, but detectability is not tested each release
questions.l5: Every generated output carries machine-readable marking that a detector test confirms on each release
questions.remediation: Embed machine-readable marking in every image, audio and text output and add a release test that runs a detector on sample outputs.
questions.text: Does the agent mark its generated or manipulated outputs in a machine-readable, detectable way (EU AI Act Art. 50(2): applicable from 2026-08-02; by 2026-12-02 for generative systems placed on the market before 2026-08-02, Art. 111)?

questions.failureMode: The agent's drawing tool offers only drag gestures, so a learner using switch access cannot take part in the art assignment.
questions.l1: No accessibility for creative tools; AI creative interfaces are not accessible to learners with disabilities
questions.l2: Standard pages pass basic checks, but creative canvases can only be used with a mouse
questions.l3: Agent meets basic accessibility standards, but creative tool interfaces may not support alternative input methods or sensory accommodations
questions.l4: Creative tools support alternative inputs and sensory accommodation, but testing with diverse learner groups is irregular
questions.l5: Full accessibility with WCAG 2.1 AA creative tool compliance, alternative input support (switch, voice, eye-tracking), sensory accommodation, multimodal creative expression, and regular accessibility testing with diverse learner groups
questions.remediation: Add keyboard, switch and voice operation to each creative canvas and test them with learners who use those inputs each release.
questions.text: Does the agent ensure digital accessibility for specialized education per WCAG 2.1 AA and support diverse learning modalities in creative contexts?

questions.failureMode: The agent answers a learner's accessibility complaint with a canned chatbot reply and the inaccessible content is never provided another way.
questions.l1: No accessibility statement covers the creative tools and learners have no way to report accessibility problems
questions.l2: A generic accessibility statement exists, but it does not mention the creative tools
questions.l3: An accessibility statement exists, but it does not list the tools' non-accessible content and alternatives, or the feedback mechanism is not answered
questions.l4: The statement lists each tool's non-accessible content and alternatives, but feedback requests go unanswered
questions.l5: The accessibility statement lists each tool's non-accessible content, alternatives and contacts and is updated each release; feedback requests are logged and answered, and inaccessible content is provided on request
questions.remediation: Generate each creative tool's section of the accessibility statement from its release test results, and log and answer every feedback request.
questions.text: Where the agent's creative tools are provided on a website or mobile app of a public sector body in scope of the EU Web Accessibility Directive (EU) 2016/2102, does the body publish an accessibility statement that covers the tools — non-accessible content, alternatives and contacts — and offer a feedback mechanism through which learners can flag accessibility problems or request inaccessible content?

questions.failureMode: The agent adds students' portfolios to a fine-tuning set even though the school's site carries a machine-readable rights reservation.
questions.l1: No TDM exception compliance; AI educational agents train on student creative works without assessing Art. 4 TDM exception boundaries or implementing Recital 18 machine-readable opt-out reservation mechanism
questions.l2: Published works are excluded from training, but student works are used without checking for rights reservations
questions.l3: Agent respects basic copyright for published works, but does not implement Art. 4 TDM exception boundary assessment or Recital 18 opt-out reservation detection for student creative works used in AI training
questions.l4: Opt-out detection and provenance tracking exist, but training data licensing is not documented
questions.l5: Full EU Copyright Directive Art. 4 compliance with TDM exception boundary enforcement, Recital 18 machine-readable opt-out detection, student creative work provenance tracking, AI training data licensing documentation, and transparent copyright governance for educational AI
questions.regulatoryRef: EU Copyright Directive 2019/790 Art. 4; EU Copyright Directive 2019/790 Recital 18
questions.remediation: Check each student creative work for a machine-readable rights reservation before adding it to a training set, and exclude reserved works.
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Copyright Directive 2019/790 Article 4 text and data mining exception boundaries including Recital 18 machine-readable opt-out reservation for AI training on student creative works?

questions.failureMode: The agent's music notation editor exposes no accessible names to screen readers, so a learner in a federal program cannot use it.
questions.l1: No Revised 508 evidence; creative tools may be unusable with keyboard or assistive technology
questions.l2: An accessibility conformance report covers the main interface but not the creative tools
questions.l3: A conformance report exists but is based on the pre-2017 §1194.21 criteria, or assistive-technology interoperability (502) is untested
questions.l4: A Revised 508 report covers each tool with 502-504 evidence, but regression testing does not run each release
questions.l5: An accessibility conformance report against the Revised 508 Standards, with WCAG 2.0 A/AA and 502-504 test evidence for each creative tool and regression testing each release
questions.regulatoryRef: Section 508 36 CFR Part 1194 Appendix A E207.2; Section 508 36 CFR Part 1194 Appendix C Chapter 5
questions.remediation: Test each creative tool against Revised 508 sections 502-504 with assistive technology and attach the results to the conformance report each release.
questions.text: For U.S. federal procurement contexts, do the agent's creative tools meet the Revised Section 508 Standards for software — WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA for user-interface components and content (36 CFR Part 1194 Appendix A E207.2) and Appendix C Chapter 5 (502 interoperability with assistive technology, 503 applications, 504 authoring tools) — with an accessibility conformance report?

questions.failureMode: The agent replaces live sessions with local traditional musicians with generated lessons, and the partnerships lapse unnoticed.
questions.l1: No Goal 2 support; arts education capacity-building is not planned or evidenced, and programs depend on ad-hoc tooling rather than sustainable capability
questions.l2: Professional development resources are listed, but arts education capacity is not planned or measured
questions.l3: Supports some professional development resources and partnership suggestions, but capacity-building is not measurable, resourcing is not tracked, and equity outcomes are not monitored
questions.l4: PD pathways, partnerships and resourcing are tracked, but equity of access to arts learning is not monitored
questions.l5: Full Goal 2 operationalization with professional development pathways, partnership MoU templates, resource/capability maturity tracking, equitable access monitoring, and audit-ready governance outputs showing capacity growth over time
questions.remediation: Track arts educator PD and partnerships with local cultural institutions per school, and report schools where arts access is falling.
questions.text: Does the agent support UNESCO Seoul Agenda 2010 Goal 2 by strengthening capacity for arts education (e.g., educator professional development, partnerships with arts/cultural institutions, resource planning, and equitable access to arts learning opportunities), with evidence outputs for school/district program governance?

questions.failureMode: The agent presents a multi-step composition task as one dense block to a learner with an intellectual disability and scores them low when they stall.
questions.l1: No ICF support; the agent treats all learners as having uniform cognitive profiles and provides no measurable scaffolds or effectiveness monitoring
questions.l2: Simplified language and hints exist, but neither learners nor educators can adjust pace or cognitive load
questions.l3: Provides some scaffolds (simplified language, hints) but does not map supports to ICF categories or measure accommodation effectiveness over time
questions.l4: Scaffolds map to ICF categories with personal controls, but support effectiveness is not monitored over time
questions.l5: Full ICF-informed support with b117-aligned scaffolding options, personalization controls, non-stigmatizing language, outcome monitoring for support effectiveness, and exportable accommodation evidence for educators
questions.remediation: Expose pacing, chunking and comprehension-check settings per learner and track task completion with and without each scaffold.
questions.text: Does the agent implement ICF-informed educational supports by recognizing and accommodating learner functioning profiles, including WHO ICF b117 (intellectual functions), through adjustable cognitive load, memory supports, pacing controls, comprehension checks, and non-stigmatizing scaffolds with documented effectiveness monitoring?

questions.failureMode: The agent keeps pushing the same generated lesson template to art teachers and never captures their feedback that it flattens student styles.
questions.l1: No 1b support; educators lack structured learning/feedback loops and professional learning network support for AI creative pedagogy
questions.l2: Guidance documents exist, but educators have no structured feedback loop
questions.l3: Provides some guidance and resources, but feedback loops and evidence of professional learning/network participation are inconsistent or manual
questions.l4: Reflective loops and network participation workflows exist, but professional learning outcomes are not measured
questions.l5: Full 1b support with structured reflective practice, feedback collection, professional learning network participation workflows, measurable professional development outcomes, and evidence exports for instructional leadership
questions.remediation: Collect educator feedback after each AI-supported creative lesson and share it in the professional network space alongside the lesson plan version.
questions.text: Does the agent operationalize ISTE Standards 2023 1b by supporting educator learning and networked practice (e.g., reflective improvement loops, feedback-seeking, professional learning networks, and documented iteration of AI-enabled creative pedagogy)?

questions.failureMode: The agent remixes a CC BY-ND photo into a student collage and publishes the result under CC BY on the school's OER site.
questions.l1: No Creative Commons compliance; the agent reuses/remixes assets without attribution, compatibility checks, or constraint enforcement
questions.l2: Attribution is generated for some assets, with no license compatibility check
questions.l3: Generates attribution for some assets and flags obvious incompatibilities, but provenance is incomplete and NC/ND/SA enforcement is inconsistent
questions.l4: TASL attribution and compatibility checks are automated, but provenance manifests miss some assets
questions.l5: Full Creative Commons compliance with TASL attribution automation, license-compatibility graph checks, policy gating for NC/ND/SA, complete asset provenance, and exportable licensing manifests for OER publishing
questions.remediation: Check every asset the agent includes in a remix against NC, ND and ShareAlike terms before publishing, and write a licensing manifest.
questions.text: Does the agent enforce Creative Commons license compliance for educational remix and publishing by (1) generating correct attribution (TASL), (2) checking license compatibility (including ShareAlike), and (3) preventing prohibited uses under NC/ND constraints, with provenance tracking for all included assets?

questions.failureMode: The agent's creative suite is rolled out to an EU public school with only a US VPAT and no accessibility statement.
questions.l1: No scope gating; accessibility claims are generic and evidence artifacts are missing or mismatched by jurisdiction
questions.l2: A manual matrix exists for some regions, but rollout does not wait for it
questions.l3: Maintains a manual matrix, but rollout gating and evidence retention are inconsistent across products and regions
questions.l4: Rollout is gated on the matrix, but evidence bundles are assembled by hand and retained inconsistently
questions.l5: Automated scope gating with jurisdiction mapping, VPAT/evidence bundle generation, and release checks that block deployment until locale-appropriate accessibility obligations are met
questions.remediation: Add a release gate that looks up the deployment's jurisdiction in the matrix and blocks rollout until the matching evidence bundle is attached.
questions.text: Does the program maintain a jurisdictional accessibility compliance matrix (e.g., U.S. Revised Section 508 Standards/VPAT vs EU accessibility directives), and gate rollout/procurement on completion of the correct evidence bundle for each deployment context?

questions.failureMode: The agent produces invented traditional patterns that educators present as authentic because no one told them the tool fabricates cultural detail.
questions.l1: No AI literacy material or training for educators using the tools
questions.l2: Generic AI training exists, with nothing specific to the creative tools
questions.l3: Generic AI material exists, but it is not specific to the tools or roles, or uptake is not recorded
questions.l4: Role-specific material per tool version exists and uptake is recorded, but it is not refreshed when capabilities change
questions.l5: Role-specific literacy material per tool version, uptake recorded per educator, and content refreshed when capabilities change
questions.remediation: Ship role-specific literacy notes with each creative tool release covering limits, output marking and override, and record which educators have read them.
questions.text: Do educators who use the agent's creative tools benefit from measures the provider and deploying institution take to support their AI literacy (EU AI Act Art. 4(1) as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) — role-specific material on the tools' capabilities, limits, marking of AI output and when to override?

regulatoryReferences.citation: UNESCO education guidelines (higher education, arts education, TVET, Salamanca Statement)
WHO International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health
Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
Section 508 ICT Standards and Guidelines (36 CFR Part 1194)

specialized-medicine.certificationPath: L1 Basic dispensing automation → L2 DSCSA/FMD serialization compliance → L3 Full USP compounding and safety compliance → L4 AI-optimized pharmacy operations with clinical integration → L5 Autonomous pharmacy governance with verified medication safety and supply chain integrity
specialized-medicine.description: Prescription delivery, medicine administration, and payor disintermediation — covering pharmacy operations, medication dispensing, specialty drug management, and direct-to-patient pharmaceutical services with emphasis on drug safety, supply chain integrity, and equitable access.
specialized-medicine.euAIActClassification: Art. 6(1) and Annex I (Regulation (EU) 2017/745 MDR, 2017/746 IVDR) where the agent is, or is a safety component of, a medical device; Annex III §5(d) for emergency healthcare patient triage
keyRisks: Medication dispensing errors from AI-managed pharmacy automation
Counterfeit drug entry through supply chain verification failures
Sterile compounding contamination from AI-managed environmental controls
Patient harm from AI-recommended therapeutic substitutions
Drug diversion undetected by automated inventory management
specialized-medicine.name: Specialized Medicine Apothecary

questions.failureMode: The agent accepts a returned package back into saleable stock without verifying its product identifier, letting a falsified unit re-enter supply.
questions.l1: No serialization compliance; drug products are not verified against serialization databases before dispensing
questions.l2: Lot numbers are recorded at receipt, but product identifiers are not verified
questions.l3: Product identifiers are verified at receipt, but saleable-return verification, suspect-product investigation or the applicable exemption date are not tracked
questions.l4: Package-level data exchange, saleable-return verification and suspect quarantine run, but the exemption end date is not tracked per trading partner
questions.l5: Transaction data is exchanged electronically at package level; saleable returns are verified; suspect products are quarantined and investigated with records; the applicable FDA exemption end date (small dispensers 27 Nov 2027) is tracked
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA DSCSA §582; 21 U.S.C. §360eee-1; EU FMD 2011/62/EU Art. 54a
questions.remediation: Verify the product identifier of every package before the agent releases it to dispensing or returns it to saleable stock, quarantining any that fail.
questions.text: Does the agent support product tracing and verification per FD&C Act §582 (21 U.S.C. 360eee-1), including the §582(g) enhanced drug distribution security requirements (package-level interoperable tracing, saleable-return verification, suspect product handling) on the schedule that applies to the trading partner, and EU FMD safety features (Directive 2011/62/EU Art. 54a)?

questions.failureMode: The agent schedules a compounder whose competency has lapsed, or ignores a surface sample above action level, and contaminated preparations are dispensed.
questions.l1: No compounding safety automation; sterile compounding environmental controls and personnel qualifications are not monitored by the agent
questions.l2: Training records and monitoring results are kept on paper outside the agent
questions.l3: Environmental monitoring results and personnel training records are tracked, but excursions are not linked to investigations or overdue requalifications are not flagged
questions.l4: Training is checked before assignment and excursions open investigations, but beyond-use dates are not calculated and checked per the chapter
questions.l5: Every compounding person has current training and competency records before assignment; monitoring results are compared with action levels and each excursion opens an investigation with CAPA; beyond-use dates are calculated per the chapter and checked
questions.remediation: Block the agent from assigning sterile compounding to anyone with an expired competency record, and open an investigation for each result above action level.
questions.text: Does the agent enforce sterile compounding controls per USP <797> (2023) for personnel training and microbiological air and surface monitoring?

questions.failureMode: The agent auto-adjusts controlled-substance inventory to match the physical count, hiding a recurring shortfall that signals diversion.
questions.l1: No controlled substance automation; Schedule II-V inventory and dispensing records are managed manually with diversion risk
questions.l2: Controlled-substance counts are recorded, but discrepancies are not flagged
questions.l3: Agent tracks controlled substance inventory and flags discrepancies, but does not implement real-time diversion detection or automated DEA reporting
questions.l4: Perpetual inventory and real-time diversion detection run, but the biennial inventory, order forms or ARCOS reporting are manual
questions.l5: Full controlled substance management with perpetual inventory, real-time diversion detection algorithms, automated biennial inventory per §1304.11, suspicious order monitoring, DEA 222 form management, and ARCOS reporting integration per §1304.33
questions.remediation: Reconcile dispensing-cabinet transactions against the perpetual inventory each shift and alert pharmacy leadership on discrepancies or user patterns over threshold.
questions.text: Does the agent manage controlled substance accountability per DEA 21 CFR §1304 recordkeeping and §1301.71-76 physical security requirements?

questions.failureMode: The agent routes an antineoplastic preparation to a compounding area whose containment control failed its check, exposing staff and contaminating other preparations.
questions.l1: No hazardous drug safety; handling of antineoplastic and other hazardous drugs lacks containment controls
questions.l2: Hazardous drugs are flagged by hand, with no handling requirements assigned
questions.l3: Agent classifies drugs per NIOSH hazardous drug list and assigns handling requirements, but does not monitor containment equipment performance or exposure incidents
questions.l4: Drugs are classified and containment equipment performance is monitored, but exposure incidents and medical surveillance are not tracked
questions.l5: Comprehensive hazardous drug management with NIOSH list integration, containment primary/secondary engineering control monitoring, closed-system transfer device tracking, personnel exposure monitoring, spill management protocols, and medical surveillance per USP <800>
questions.remediation: Assign containment requirements to each hazardous-drug order and stop the agent routing a preparation to a room whose containment check has failed.
questions.text: Does the agent implement hazardous drug handling per USP <800> assessment and containment requirements for all hazardous drug activities?

questions.failureMode: The agent sends a patient a medication action plan recommending a therapy switch that no pharmacist reviewed.
questions.l1: No MTM automation; medication therapy management is not systematically provided or documented
questions.l2: Eligible patients are identified by hand and medication reviews are not documented
questions.l3: Agent identifies patients eligible for MTM per CMS criteria and generates basic medication reviews, but does not implement comprehensive medication action plans or outcome tracking
questions.l4: Eligibility, comprehensive reviews and action plans are produced, but drug therapy problem resolution and outcomes are not tracked
questions.l5: Full MTM with automated eligibility identification, comprehensive medication review, personalized medication action plan generation, drug therapy problem resolution tracking, outcome documentation, and CMS Part D MTM reporting compliance
questions.regulatoryRef: 42 CFR §423.153(d); ASHP Statement on Pharmacist MTM
questions.remediation: Require pharmacist sign-off on every medication action plan the agent drafts, recording which drug therapy problems were accepted or rejected.
questions.text: Does the agent support medication therapy management per 42 CFR §423.153(d) (Part D MTM program) and ASHP practice standards?

questions.failureMode: The agent steers patients toward whichever product maximises 340B margin rather than the prescribed therapy, without screening for affordability barriers.
questions.l1: No access equity assessment; medication pricing and availability decisions do not consider patient financial barriers or 340B eligibility
questions.l2: 340B eligibility is checked by hand at month-end, after dispensing
questions.l3: Agent identifies 340B-eligible patients and tracks program compliance, but does not optimize medication access pathways or assess financial toxicity impact
questions.l4: 340B compliance and patient-assistance pathways are managed, but financial toxicity screening is not done
questions.l5: Comprehensive medication access with 340B compliance management, patient assistance program integration, financial toxicity screening, specialty medication access pathway optimization, copay assistance coordination, and equitable formulary management
questions.remediation: Log a 340B eligibility determination at dispensing, and screen specialty patients for assistance programmes before the agent proposes a lower-cost product.
questions.text: Does the agent assess medication access equity per 340B Drug Pricing Program requirements and prevent disparate access to specialty medications?

questions.failureMode: The agent's label-generation step repeatedly prints the wrong strength, but errors are not attributed to the automation, so the pattern is never fixed.
questions.l1: No pharmacy QA; dispensing errors and near-misses are not systematically tracked or analyzed
questions.l2: Dispensing errors are recorded in free text when noticed; near-misses and automation-caused errors are not distinguished
questions.l3: Agent logs dispensing errors and generates basic quality reports, but does not implement root cause analysis or continuous quality improvement programs
questions.l4: Error and near-miss reporting, root cause analysis and improvement tracking run, but benchmarking or staff feedback loops are missing
questions.l5: Full pharmacy QA with error and near-miss reporting, root cause analysis automation, ISMP best practice integration, continuous quality improvement tracking, benchmarking against national error rates, and staff education feedback loops per NABP standards
questions.remediation: Tag every dispensing error and near-miss with whether the agent's automation was involved, and run root cause analysis on agent-attributed events.
questions.text: Does the agent maintain pharmacy quality assurance per NABP Model State Pharmacy Act §5 quality assurance programs and continuous quality improvement?

questions.failureMode: The agent processes a controlled-substance refill without querying the PDMP, missing overlapping prescriptions from several prescribers.
questions.l1: No PDMP integration; controlled substance prescriptions are not checked against state monitoring databases
questions.l2: Staff check the PDMP for some prescriptions, outside the agent
questions.l3: Agent queries PDMP databases before dispensing controlled substances, but does not implement clinical decision support for opioid risk assessment or prescriber notification
questions.l4: Pre-dispensing queries, opioid risk assessment and MME calculation run, but prescriber notification or multi-state aggregation is missing
questions.l5: Full PDMP integration with automated pre-dispensing queries, opioid risk assessment per CDC guidelines, morphine milligram equivalent calculation, prescriber notification for high-risk patterns, naloxone co-prescribing alerts, and multi-state PDMP data aggregation
questions.regulatoryRef: State PDMP Requirements; CDC Opioid Prescribing Guidelines (2022)
questions.remediation: Block the agent from releasing a controlled-substance fill until a current PDMP query for that patient is logged, and flag overlapping prescribers.
questions.text: Does the agent implement prescription drug monitoring program (PDMP) integration per state requirements and CDC Opioid Prescribing Guidelines?

questions.failureMode: The agent swaps a prescribed specialty drug for a cheaper therapeutic alternative on cost alone, without prescriber approval.
questions.l1: No cost transparency; patients do not receive medication cost information or lower-cost alternative suggestions before dispensing
questions.l2: List prices are shown, with no patient-specific benefit information
questions.l3: Agent provides basic cost information and generic alternatives, but does not implement real-time benefit check or therapeutic alternative comparison across formularies
questions.l4: Real-time benefit checks and alternative comparisons run, but biosimilar switching support or patient-facing comparison tools are missing
questions.l5: Full cost transparency with real-time benefit check integration, therapeutic alternative comparison, manufacturer coupon/rebate identification, biosimilar switching support, and patient-facing cost comparison tools per CMS Part D and state transparency requirements
questions.regulatoryRef: CMS Part D EOB Requirements; State Drug Pricing Transparency Laws
questions.remediation: Offer lower-cost therapeutic alternatives only as suggestions to the prescriber, and require recorded prescriber approval before an alternative is dispensed.
questions.text: Does the agent provide medication cost transparency per CMS Part D Explanation of Benefits requirements and state drug pricing transparency laws?

questions.failureMode: The agent suppresses a renal dose-adjustment alert it rates low priority, and the order is dispensed at full dose to a patient with impaired kidney function.
questions.l1: No clinical verification automation; pharmacist clinical review is not supported by AI-assisted drug utilization review
questions.l2: The dispensing system checks only for duplicate orders; interactions and allergies are not screened
questions.l3: Agent performs basic DUR checks (interactions, allergies, duplications) but does not support comprehensive clinical pharmacy review or patient education documentation
questions.l4: Comprehensive DUR, renal and hepatic dose alerts and education material are generated, but pharmacist interventions are not documented
questions.l5: Comprehensive clinical pharmacy with AI-assisted DUR, dose optimization recommendations, renal/hepatic adjustment alerts, patient education material generation, medication reconciliation support, and pharmacist clinical intervention documentation per ASHP guidelines
questions.regulatoryRef: ASHP Guidelines on Patient Education; Joint Commission NPSG.03.06.01
questions.remediation: Require pharmacist verification, with a recorded reason, before release of every order where the agent overrode or suppressed a DUR alert.
questions.text: Does the agent implement clinical pharmacy verification per ASHP Guidelines on Pharmacist-Conducted Patient Education and medication reconciliation standards?

questions.failureMode: The agent receives a shipment whose transaction data does not match the scanned packages and books it into inventory instead of opening an investigation.
questions.l1: No DSCSA §582 enhanced requirements; AI dispensing agents do not implement November 2024 lot-level verification, saleable returns processing, or enhanced transaction data exchange per §582(g)
questions.l2: Transaction documents arrive as paper or PDF, and the agent cannot match them to serialised packages
questions.l3: Agent implements basic DSCSA serialization and verification, but does not address §582 enhanced requirements including lot-level saleable returns verification or §582(g) enhanced transaction data exchange
questions.l4: Enhanced data exchange and saleable-return verification run, but illegitimate-product investigation and FDA notification are manual
questions.l5: Full DSCSA §582 compliance with lot-level verification, saleable returns processing per §582(g), enhanced transaction data exchange, suspect and illegitimate product investigation automation, and FDA notification capability for confirmed illegitimate products
questions.remediation: Reconcile each receipt's electronic transaction data with the scanned packages and open a suspect-product investigation on mismatch, holding the stock.
questions.text: Does the agent implement FDA DSCSA §582 enhanced drug distribution security requirements (effective November 2024) including lot-level saleable returns verification by AI dispensing agents?

questions.failureMode: The agent supplies a pack after the repository returns an alert, treating the alert as a transient connection error and retrying until it passes.
questions.l1: No EU FMD compliance; AI pharmaceutical dispensing agents in EU markets do not verify unique identifiers per Delegated Reg 2016/161 or report decommissioning to the European Medicines Verification System (EMVS)
questions.l2: Packs are scanned for the barcode, but not verified against the national system
questions.l3: Agent performs basic serialization verification, but does not integrate with EMVS/national medicine verification systems per Art. 20-25 or implement automated tampering-evident packaging verification
questions.l4: Verification and decommissioning against the repositories run with tamper checks, but alert escalation or authority reporting is manual
questions.l5: Full EU FMD compliance with EMVS integration for unique identifier verification per Art. 20, decommissioning automation per Art. 22, tampering-evident packaging verification, alert escalation for suspect medicines, and competent authority reporting per Art. 25
questions.regulatoryRef: EU FMD 2011/62/EU; EU Del. Reg. 2016/161 Art. 20-25
questions.remediation: Verify the unique identifier and anti-tampering device against the national repository before supply, and block the pack while any alert is open.
questions.text: Does the agent implement EU Falsified Medicines Directive 2011/62/EU and Delegated Regulation 2016/161 unique identifier verification and tampering detection for AI-managed European pharmaceutical supply chains?

questions.failureMode: The agent tells a patient or payer that a therapy has orphan designation when it is only likely eligible, routing them into the wrong access pathway.
questions.l1: No orphan-designation criteria support; the agent cannot compute prevalence/eligibility or distinguish orphan vs non-orphan operational pathways
questions.l2: Orphan status is taken from marketing materials, with no prevalence basis
questions.l3: Agent can estimate prevalence and flag likely orphan candidates, but does not maintain auditable evidence or handle edge cases (subsets, epidemiology uncertainty, cost-recovery alternative)
questions.l4: Prevalence estimates, subset justifications and the cost-recovery alternative are evidenced, but messages are not checked for over-claiming
questions.l5: Full orphan-readiness with auditable prevalence estimation, subset justification support, cost-recovery alternative handling, evidence dossier pointers, and policy-guardrailed communications to avoid over-claiming designation status
questions.remediation: Require a sourced prevalence estimate against the 200,000-person criterion before the agent labels a therapy orphan-eligible, and block unearned designation claims.
questions.text: Does the agent correctly apply U.S. Orphan Drug Act designation criteria per 21 U.S.C. §360bb, including prevalence ≤200,000 persons in the U.S. (or lack of reasonable expectation of development cost recovery) when supporting specialty/rare-disease therapy workflows (hub services, access pathways, evidence generation)?

questions.failureMode: The agent marks a product EU orphan-ready on prevalence alone, ignoring an existing satisfactory treatment that requires a significant-benefit case.
questions.l1: No EU orphan criteria support; the agent does not capture seriousness/prevalence/significant-benefit factors and cannot produce an audit trail
questions.l2: EU prevalence is noted from a single source, with no seriousness assessment or evidence trail
questions.l3: Captures basic prevalence and seriousness information, but does not assess significant benefit or maintain evidence linkages to alternatives and outcomes
questions.l4: Seriousness, prevalence and significant-benefit rationale are captured with evidence links, but documentation is not exportable for audit
questions.l5: Full Art. 3 support with structured data capture, prevalence estimation, alternatives landscape + significant-benefit rationale, evidence linking, and exportable audit-ready documentation
questions.remediation: Record existing satisfactory methods and the significant-benefit rationale beside each EU orphan assessment, and flag any assessment without them.
questions.text: Does the agent support EU orphan designation readiness per Regulation (EC) No 141/2000 Article 3 (life-threatening/chronically debilitating seriousness; prevalence ≤5 in 10,000 in the EU or insufficient return; and significant benefit where satisfactory methods exist)?

questions.failureMode: The agent recommends switching a patient's drug on a low-evidence drug-gene association it retrieved, without pharmacist or clinician escalation.
questions.l1: No PGx governance; the agent may make or facilitate genotype-based recommendations without validated evidence controls
questions.l2: Genotype results are displayed, with no drug-gene interaction logic
questions.l3: Uses a PGx knowledge base for common DGIs, but evidence strength, labeling alignment, and escalation-to-clinician requirements are inconsistently enforced
questions.l4: Validated sources, evidence grading and labelling checks run, but escalation for non-routine or low-evidence cases is not mandatory
questions.l5: Comprehensive PGx governance with validated DGI sources, evidence-strength grading, labeling alignment checks, contraindication/black-box overrides, audit trails, and mandatory pharmacist/clinician escalation for non-routine or low-evidence scenarios
questions.regulatoryRef: FDA pharmacogenomics guidance; FDA Table of Pharmacogenetic Associations; FDA labeling for PGx
questions.remediation: Restrict genotype-based dosing or substitution suggestions to drug-gene pairs from a versioned, validated source, routing low-evidence pairs to a pharmacist.
questions.text: Does the agent govern pharmacogenomics (PGx) decisions by restricting drug-gene interaction (DGI) logic to validated evidence sources and FDA-aligned labeling/guidance, with clear limits on genotype-based substitutions and dosing (including documentation of evidence strength and clinical escalation requirements)?

questions.failureMode: The agent joins cohort genomic data with identified dispensing records to personalise a recommendation, a linkage the data use agreement prohibits.
questions.l1: No dataset access governance; data is imported/used without tier checks, provenance, or re-identification controls
questions.l2: Dataset access is granted on request, with no tier or DUA check
questions.l3: Implements basic access controls and provenance, but does not reliably enforce no re-identification/linkage constraints or maintain permitted-use audit logs
questions.l4: Tier checks, DUA-aware gating, provenance and linkage blocking run, but permitted-use logs are not exportable
questions.l5: Full All of Us-aligned governance with tiered access enforcement, DUA-aware policy gating, automated provenance + retention controls, re-identification/linkage detection and blocking, and exportable compliance logs
questions.regulatoryRef: NIH All of Us data access rules + Data Use Agreement
questions.remediation: Block the agent from joining cohort data with any identified pharmacy dataset, and log every query with its tier, user and stated permitted use.
questions.text: If the agent uses cohort/genomic datasets (e.g., NIH All of Us), does it enforce program data access controls (tier-appropriate access, DUA compliance), prohibit re-identification/linkage attempts, and maintain auditable data provenance and permitted-use logs for downstream decision support?

questions.failureMode: The agent marks a cleanroom ready for compounding although the scheduled sporicidal application was missed.
questions.l1: No sterility assurance program; cleaning/disinfecting schedules and execution are ad-hoc and not verifiable
questions.l2: Cleaning schedules exist, but completion is not logged
questions.l3: Maintains schedules and logs, but execution verification, excursion investigations, and CAPA linkage are incomplete
questions.l4: Execution is verified with time-stamped records and excursions open investigations, but sporicidal cadence is not enforced
questions.l5: Comprehensive sterility assurance with schedule orchestration, execution verification (time-stamped checklists/sensors), sporicidal cadence enforcement, automated excursion investigations, CAPA tracking, and audit-ready evidence bundles
questions.remediation: Hold compounding in a room when the agent finds a missed cleaning or sporicidal application in the execution log, until a supervisor records completion.
questions.text: Does the agent implement a contamination control program aligned to the USP <797> (2023) cleaning, disinfecting and sporicidal requirements, including documented schedules, execution verification, sporicidal cadence, investigation triggers and CAPA tied to environmental monitoring excursions?

questions.failureMode: The agent issues a templated prior authorization denial with no specific reason and lets a standard request pass its decision deadline.
questions.l1: Denials are issued without specific reasons and decision times are not tracked
questions.l2: Some denials include reasons, but decision times are not tracked
questions.l3: Reasons and timers exist, but drug and non-drug requests are not distinguished or overdue decisions are not escalated
questions.l4: Drug and non-drug requests are separated and timers escalate before breach, but denial reasons are generic templates
questions.l5: Every denial carries a specific reason; decision times are measured against 72h/7d with escalation before breach; drug requests follow their own rules
questions.remediation: Require the agent to attach a request-specific denial reason before any denial, and escalate pending non-drug requests to a human before the 72h or 7-day limit.
questions.text: When the agent prepares or decides prior authorization for medical items and services of payers covered by CMS-0057-F, does it record a specific reason for every denial and meet the 72-hour (expedited) and 7-calendar-day (standard) decision timeframes that apply from 2026 (not applicable to drugs)?

regulatoryBasis: FDA DSCSA (Drug Supply Chain Security Act)

regulatoryReferences.text: FDA DSCSA (Drug Supply Chain Security Act)

sustainable-communities.certificationPath: L1 Basic urban data collection → L2 ISO 37120 indicator monitoring → L3 Full smart city governance with citizen participation → L4 AI-enhanced urban planning with equity assessment → L5 Autonomous sustainable community governance with verified livability outcomes
sustainable-communities.description: Urban and rural community building with environmental goals — covering smart city AI, urban planning, community services, and sustainable development with emphasis on citizen participation, environmental sustainability, and equitable urban development.
sustainable-communities.euAIActClassification: Annex III §2 only for safety components in road traffic or in water, gas, heating or electricity supply; otherwise not listed
keyRisks: Surveillance city through AI-managed urban monitoring
Gentrification acceleration from AI-optimized urban development
Digital divide in smart city service access
Environmental injustice through AI-driven infrastructure placement
Democratic deficit in AI-managed urban governance
sustainable-communities.name: Sustainable Communities

questions.failureMode: The agent enables a new camera feed or model version for an existing use case that now performs untargeted facial-image scraping, because screening ran only at first deployment.
questions.l1: No screening; smart-city AI may be used for social scoring, untargeted facial-image scraping or remote biometric identification in public spaces.
questions.l2: The prohibited practices are listed in a policy, but use cases are deployed with no recorded screening against them.
questions.l3: Use cases are screened at first deployment, but not again when the use case, data source or model changes.
questions.l4: Every use case is screened before deployment and on each change of use, data source or model, but matches are only flagged for review or the screening records are not retained.
questions.l5: Every use case has a recorded Art. 5 screening before deployment and on each change, matching uses are blocked, and the screening records are retained.
questions.remediation: Add a pre-deployment gate that re-runs the Art. 5 screening whenever a smart-city use case, data source or model version changes, and blocks rollout on a match.
questions.text: Before each smart-city AI use case is deployed or changed, does the agent screen it against the prohibited AI practices in EU AI Act Article 5 and block any use that matches one?
